general/preface/variable-speed-reading.title: Read at appropriate speeds
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.action: Read different things at different, appropriate speeds rather than reading everything as fast as possible.
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.check: Did I pick a speed suited to this material, not just the fastest I can manage?
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.quote: the ability to read different things at different—appropriate—speeds, not everything at the greatest possible speed
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.mistake: Treating maximum speed as the goal of reading.

general/preface/variable-speed-reading.title: Neither too fast nor slow
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.action: Avoid reading either too fast or too slowly for the material, since both defeat understanding.
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.check: Was my pace so fast or so slow that I lost the sense?
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.quote: “When we read too fast or too slowly, we understand nothing.”

general/preface/variable-speed-reading.title: Always read better
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.action: Aim to read better every time, going slower or faster as the material requires.
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.check: Did changing my speed here improve my reading, not just my rate?
general/preface/variable-speed-reading.quote: the aim being to read better, always better, but sometimes slower, sometimes faster

general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.title: Go beyond elementary skill
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.action: Do not stop at elementary reading skill; train yourself in the higher, distinct levels of reading.
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.check: Am I working at a level of reading above simply following the words?
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.quote: the failure to carry instruction in reading beyond the elementary level
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.mistake: Assuming sixth-grade reading skill is enough for serious books.

general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.title: State the central thought
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.action: Practise stating the central thought of a passage and the levels of emphasis and subordination in its argument.
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.check: Can I say what the passage's central thought is and which points are subordinate?
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.quote: amazingly inept at indicating the central thought of a passage, or the levels of emphasis and subordination in an argument or exposition

general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.title: Prepare for close argument
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.action: Expect expositions and tightly stated arguments to need more than the skill that suffices for simple fiction.
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.check: Could I follow a closely written argument as easily as a simple story?
general/preface/beyond-the-elementary-le.quote: But put him up against a closely written exposition, a carefully and economically stated argument, or a passage requiring critical consideration, and he is at a loss.

general/preface/the-four-levels.title: Four levels of reading
general/preface/the-four-levels.action: Learn the four levels of reading, elementary, inspectional, analytical and syntopical, which organize the whole book.
general/preface/the-four-levels.check: Can I name the four levels in order?
general/preface/the-four-levels.quote: the distinction of four levels of reading—elementary, inspectional, analytical, and syntopical—is the basic and controlling change

general/preface/the-four-levels.title: Read related books together
general/preface/the-four-levels.action: Read several related books in relation to one another so you grasp what they say, complementary and conflicting, on a common subject.
general/preface/the-four-levels.check: Can I state where these books agree and where they conflict on the shared subject?
general/preface/the-four-levels.quote: how to read a number of related books in relation to one another

general/preface/the-four-levels.title: Pyramid of books
general/preface/the-four-levels.action: Picture the books worth reading as a pyramid: many at the broad bottom, very few at the top.
general/preface/the-four-levels.check: Do I know which books belong near the top of my pyramid?
general/preface/the-four-levels.quote: the conception of a pyramid of books to read, broad at the bottom and tapering at the top

general/preface/the-four-levels.title: Adapt rules to kinds
general/preface/the-four-levels.action: Apply the basic rules flexibly to each different type of reading matter.
general/preface/the-four-levels.check: Have I adjusted the rules to the kind of material in front of me?
general/preface/the-four-levels.quote: the flexible application of the basic rules to different types of reading, in fact to every variety of reading matter

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Avoid packaged opinions
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Make up your own mind instead of absorbing a ready-made opinion and playing it back when convenient.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I think this view through, or merely replay one I was handed?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: he inserts a packaged opinion into his mind, somewhat like inserting a cassette into a cassette player
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.mistake: Performing acceptably without having had to think.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Facts are not understanding
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Do not confuse piling up facts with understanding; too many facts can obstruct it.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Do I understand the matter, or only hold many facts about it?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: too many facts are often as much of an obstacle to understanding as too few

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Read as actively as possible
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Make your reading as active as you can, since the more active the reading, the better.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: How much effort and activity did I actually put into this reading?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: the more active the reading the better

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Demand more of yourself
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Demand more of yourself and of the text, widening the range of activity and effort you bring.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I ask much of the text and of myself, or just let it pass?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: He is better if he demands more of himself and of the text before him.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Reading is never passive
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Do not treat reading as passive reception; it is an activity that needs an awake mind.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Was my mind working, or were my eyes simply moving over the page?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: Completely passive reading is impossible; we cannot read with our eyes immobilized and our minds asleep.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.mistake: Supposing receiving communication is like receiving a blow or a legacy.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Be the catcher
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Think of yourself as the catcher: as active in receiving as the writer is in sending.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Was I actively catching what was thrown, or just letting the ball hit me?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: the reader or listener is much more like the catcher in a game of baseball.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Catch every sort of communication
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Train yourself to catch every kind of communication as well as possible, as a catcher handles every pitch.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Could I handle this kind of writing as well as the kinds I am used to?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: the art of reading is the skill of catching every sort of communication as well as possible.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Cooperate with the writer
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Work with the writer so that what he wanted you to receive actually reaches you.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I receive what the writer wanted to convey?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: Successful communication occurs in any case where what the writer wanted to have received finds its way into the reader’s possession.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Effort determines what you catch
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Put more activity and skill into reading, because how much you catch depends on both.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I catch little or most of what the writer intended?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: The amount the reader “catches” will usually depend on the amount of activity he puts into the process

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: More active, more skilful
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Improve by reading more actively and by performing each of the acts of reading more skilfully.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Was I both more active and more skilful in each step this time?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: first, by reading it more actively, and second, by performing each of the acts involved more skillfully.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Reading is many acts
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Treat reading as a complex activity made of many separate acts, all of which a good reading performs.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Which acts of reading did I perform, and which did I skip?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: It consists of a large number of separate acts, all of which must be performed in a good reading.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Apply rules to anything printed
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Use the rules of reading on all printed matter, from books to newspapers, pamphlets and advertisements.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I read this article or ad as actively as I would a book?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: can be applied also to printed material in general, to any type of reading matter

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Measure of success
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Judge your reading by how much of what the writer intended to communicate you actually received.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: How much of what the author meant to communicate did I receive?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: Your success in reading it is determined by the extent to which you receive everything the writer intended to communicate.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Notice what you don't understand
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Notice when a book has more to say than you understand, since it can then raise your understanding.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Do I know which parts I do not yet understand?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: you understand enough to know that you do not understand it all.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Don't hand off or give up
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Do not hand the hard parts to someone else to explain or dismiss them as not worth the bother.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I tackle the difficult parts myself, or skip or outsource them?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: In either case, you are not doing the job of reading that the book requires.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.mistake: Deciding that what is over your head is not worth bothering about.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Work on the book yourself
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Without outside help, work on the text with your own mind until you understand more than before.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I raise my own understanding using only the text and my mind?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: Without external help of any sort, you go to work on the book.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: The art of reading defined
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Understand the art of reading as the mind lifting itself from understanding less to understanding more by its own operations.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Do I understand more now than when I began, by my own effort?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: The mind passes from understanding less to understanding more.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Information versus understanding
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Distinguish reading that adds information within your present understanding from reading that raises your understanding.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Was this book at once intelligible to me, or did it stretch my understanding?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: Such things may increase our store of information, but they cannot improve our understanding, for our understanding was equal to them before we started.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Stay alert to puzzlement
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Stay alert and honest enough to feel the puzzlement that tells you a book is over your depth.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I notice and admit where I was puzzled?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: we would have felt the shock of puzzlement and perplexity that comes from getting in over our depth—that is, if we were both alert and honest.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Conditions for understanding
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Read for understanding only where the writer understands more than you and you can partly close that gap.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Is this writer my superior in understanding, and am I closing the gap?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: First, there is initial inequality in understanding.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Learn from your betters
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Choose writers who understand more than you, and learn how to learn from them.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Is this book better or higher than me, so I can learn from it?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: In short, we can learn only from our “betters.”

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Information takes care of itself
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Concentrate on reading for understanding; reading for information will then usually look after itself.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Am I aiming at understanding rather than just collecting information?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: if you learn to do that, reading for information will usually take care of itself.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Reading for entertainment
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Recognize entertainment as a third goal that needs no rules and least effort; reserve effortful reading for understanding.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Am I reading this for entertainment, information, or understanding?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: It is the least demanding kind of reading, and it requires the least amount of effort.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Informed versus enlightened
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Go beyond knowing that something is the case to knowing why, its connections, and how it is alike or different.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Do I know why this is so and how it connects with other facts?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: To be informed is to know simply that something is the case.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Know meaning and reasons
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Know not only what the author says but what he means and why he says it.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Can I state what the author means and why he says it?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: Enlightenment is achieved only when, in addition to knowing what an author says, you know what he means and why he says it.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Explain, don't just remember
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Test yourself by explaining the author's point, not merely remembering it.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Could I explain this, or can I only repeat it?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: the differences between being able to remember something and being able to explain it.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Don't stop at information
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Remember what the author said, but do not stop at being informed.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Having got the facts, did I go on to understand them?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: The point, however, is not to stop at being informed.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Widely read is not well-read
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Do not assume that reading widely is the same as reading well.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Have I read these books well, or just many of them?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: the error of assuming that to be widely read and to be well-read are the same thing
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.mistake: Becoming a bookful blockhead, ignorantly read.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Instruction versus discovery
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Distinguish learning by instruction, from speech or writing, from learning by discovery through research or reflection.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Am I learning from a teacher's discourse or directly from the world?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: Instruction occurs when one person teaches another through speech or writing.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Treat instruction as aided discovery
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Treat being taught as aided discovery: the learning still has to happen actively in you.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I do the learning, or expect the book to do it for me?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: a better way to make the distinction clear is to call instruction “aided discovery.”

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: You must do the learning
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Accept that, however much a teacher or book helps, you yourself must do the learning.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Has knowledge actually grown in my own mind?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: it is the student himself who must do the learning.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: The art of being taught
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Treat reading and listening as one art, the art of being taught.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Am I applying the skills of being taught whether I read or listen?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: reading and listening are the same art—the art of being taught.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Think while reading
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Think actively as you read, just as you would in doing research.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Was I thinking about the text, or reading thoughtlessly?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: We must think in the course of reading and listening, just as we must think in the course of research.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Use every faculty
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Bring observation, memory, imagination and analytical reflection to your reading.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I observe, remember, imagine and analyse as I read?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: keenness of observation, readily available memory, range of imagination, and, of course, an intellect trained in analysis and reflection.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Imagine when reading poetry
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Use your imagination when reading a poem, just as the poet did in writing it.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I actively imagine what the poem presents?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: many people assume that though a poet must use his imagination in writing a poem, they do not have to use their imagination in reading it.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Reading means an absent teacher
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Recognize that reading is learning from an absent teacher, unlike listening to a living one.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Is there anyone here to answer my questions, or must I answer them?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: listening is learning from a teacher who is present—a living teacher—while reading is learning from one who is absent.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Answer your own questions
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: When you question a book, work out the answer yourself through your own thinking and analysis.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Did I answer my question about the book by my own work?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: If, however, you ask a book a question, you must answer it yourself.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Understand explanations
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: Even when a teacher explains, work to understand the explanation yourself.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Do I actually understand the explanation I was given?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: if you are seeking an explanation, you have to understand it or nothing has been explained to you.

general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.title: Make books teach you
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.action: To keep learning outside school, learn how to make books teach you well without a teacher.
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.check: Can I learn from this book alone, with no teacher's help?
general/the-activity-and-art-of-reading/.quote: we must know how to make books teach us well.

general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.title: Let your goal set the way
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.action: Decide whether you read for entertainment, information or understanding, since the goal determines how you read.
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.check: What is my goal with this book, and am I reading accordingly?
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.quote: The goal a reader seeks—be it entertainment, information or understanding—determines the way he reads.

general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.title: More effort, better reading
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.action: Put in more effort, especially with books initially beyond your powers.
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.check: Did I give this demanding book the effort it needs?
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.quote: the more effort the better, at least in the case of books that are initially beyond our powers as readers

general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.title: Know how to read alone
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.action: Learn how to read without help, since reading is usually learning from an absent teacher.
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.check: Could I make progress with this book with no one to help me?
general/the-levels-of-reading/goals-and-.quote: Reading, like unaided discovery, is learning from an absent teacher.

general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.title: Levels are cumulative
general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.action: Understand that each higher level of reading includes the lower ones rather than replacing them.
general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.check: Am I still using the lower-level skills inside the higher one?
general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.quote: it is characteristic of levels that higher ones include lower ones.

general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.title: Understand the levels first
general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.action: Grasp the differences between the levels before trying to improve your reading skills.
general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.check: Can I say how the four levels differ?
general/the-levels-of-reading/levels-not.quote: The differences between the levels must be understood before any effective improvement in reading skills can occur.

general/the-levels-of-reading/elementary.title: What does the sentence say?
general/the-levels-of-reading/elementary.action: At the elementary level, ask what each sentence says.
general/the-levels-of-reading/elementary.quote: At this level of reading, the question asked of the reader is “What does the sentence say?”

general/the-levels-of-reading/elementary.title: Identify words first
general/the-levels-of-reading/elementary.action: When reading a language you know poorly, first identify the actual words before struggling with their meaning.
general/the-levels-of-reading/elementary.check: Have I recognized each word before trying to interpret it?
general/the-levels-of-reading/elementary.quote: Then our first effort must be to identify the actual words.

general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.title: Most from limited time
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.action: Read inspectionally to get the most out of a book in a set, usually short, time.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.check: Did I get the most I could from the book in the time I had?
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.quote: its aim is to get the most out of a book within a given time

general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.title: Skim systematically, not randomly
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.action: Skim systematically, not by casual or random browsing.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.check: Did I follow a system, or just flip at random?
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.quote: Inspectional reading is the art of skimming systematically.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.mistake: Casual or random browsing through a book.

general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.title: Learn from the surface
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.action: Examine the surface of the book and learn everything the surface alone can teach.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.check: What has the surface of the book told me?
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.quote: your aim is to examine the surface of the book, to learn everything that the surface alone can teach you.

general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.title: What is the book about?
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.action: At the inspectional level, ask what the book is about.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.quote: the question typically asked at this level is “What is the book about?”

general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.title: Structure and parts
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.action: Ask what the structure of the book is and what its parts are.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.check: “What is the structure of the book?” or “What are its parts?”
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.quote: others of a similar nature are “What is the structure of the book?” or “What are its parts?”

general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.title: What kind of book?
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.action: After an inspectional reading, be able to say what kind of book it is.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.check: “What kind of book is it—a novel, a history, a scientific treatise?”
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.quote: “What kind of book is it—a novel, a history, a scientific treatise?”

general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.title: Don't just plow through
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.action: Do not start on page one and plow straight through without even reading the table of contents.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.check: Did I inspect the book before trying to understand it?
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.quote: They start a book on page one and plow steadily through it, without even reading the table of contents.
general/the-levels-of-reading/inspection.mistake: Trying to get superficial knowledge and understanding at the same time.

general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.title: Best reading, unlimited time
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.action: Read analytically when you want the best, most complete reading possible given unlimited time.
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.check: Have I given this book thorough, complete reading?
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.quote: analytical reading is the best and most complete reading that is possible given unlimited time.

general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.title: Ask organized questions
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.action: Ask many organized questions of what you are reading analytically.
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.check: Did I ask the book questions in an orderly way?
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.quote: The analytical reader must ask many, and organized, questions of what he is reading.

general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.title: Work until it is yours
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.action: Grasp the book and work at it until it becomes your own.
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.check: Is this book now mine, or still the author's alone?
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.quote: the reader grasps a book—the metaphor is apt—and works at it until the book becomes his own.

general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.title: Chew and digest
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.action: Taste some books, swallow others, and chew and digest the few that deserve analytical reading.
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.check: Does this book deserve tasting, swallowing, or chewing and digesting?
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.quote: “some books are to be tasted, others to be swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.”

general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.title: Analytical for understanding
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.action: Save analytical reading for understanding; it is rarely needed for information or entertainment.
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.check: Do I need understanding from this book, or only information?
general/the-levels-of-reading/analytical.quote: analytical reading is hardly ever necessary if your goal in reading is simply information or entertainment.

general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.title: Many books, one subject
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.action: Read syntopically by reading many books and placing them in relation to one another and to a common subject.
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.check: Have I related these books to each other and to the subject?
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.quote: the reader reads many books, not just one, and places them in relation to one another and to a subject about which they all revolve.

general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.title: More than comparison
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.action: Do not settle for merely comparing texts when reading syntopically.
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.check: Did I go beyond comparing the books?
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.quote: But mere comparison of texts is not enough.

general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.title: Construct your own analysis
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.action: Use the books to build an analysis of the subject that may not be in any of them.
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.check: Have I produced an analysis that none of the books gives by itself?
general/the-levels-of-reading/syntopical.quote: the syntopical reader is able to construct an analysis of the subject that may not be in any of the books.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Four stages of learning
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Know the four stages toward mature elementary reading: readiness, simple materials, vocabulary growth, refinement.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Can I name the four stages of learning to read?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: there are at least four more or less clearly distinguishable stages in the child’s progress toward what is called mature reading ability.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Reading readiness
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Recognize that readiness involves physical, intellectual, language and personal preparation before reading instruction.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Are the physical, intellectual, language and personal kinds of readiness in place?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: Reading readiness includes several different kinds of preparation for learning to read.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Don't jump the gun
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Do not push reading instruction on a child before he is ready.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Is the learner actually ready, or am I rushing?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: The important thing to remember is that jumping the gun is usually self-defeating.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.mistake: Teaching a child not yet ready, causing lasting dislike of reading.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Stage two: simple materials
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: In the second stage, learn to read very simple materials using sight words, context clues and beginning sounds.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Can the learner read simple books independently?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: In the second stage, children learn to read very simple materials.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Unlock words by context
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Build vocabulary and unlock the meaning of unfamiliar words through context clues.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Did I work out this unfamiliar word from its context?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: increasing skill in “unlocking” the meaning of unfamiliar words through context clues.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Carry concepts across
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Carry concepts from one piece of writing to another and compare different writers' views on one subject.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Have I compared this writer's view with others on the same subject?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: to carry over concepts from one piece of writing to another, and to compare the views of different writers on the same subject.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Keep building for life
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Keep building on mature elementary reading for the rest of your life.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Am I still developing as a reader?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: Ideally, they should continue to build on it for the rest of their lives.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Work on all levels
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Do not focus on elementary reading alone; improvement must happen on all levels of reading.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Am I working at the higher levels too, not only the basics?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: effective remedies for the overall reading deficiencies of Americans cannot be found unless efforts are made on all levels of reading.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Stages belong to level one
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Recognize that all four stages of learning to read are stages of the first, elementary level.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Do I keep stages of elementary reading distinct from the levels of reading?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: the four stages outlined here are all stages of the first level of reading

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Names of the stages
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Know the stages as readiness, word mastery, vocabulary growth and use of context, and mature elementary reading.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Can I match each stage to its name?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: The third stage of elementary reading—vocabulary growth and the utilization of context

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Elementary mature is not mature
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Do not mistake mastery of elementary reading for being a mature reader in the full sense.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Can I read beyond the elementary level, or only read on my own?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: However, he is not yet a “mature” reader in the sense in which we want to employ the term in this book.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Master elementary reading first
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Master all four stages of elementary reading before moving on to the higher levels.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Can I read on my own with ease before attempting higher levels?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: Only when he has mastered all of the four stages of elementary reading is the child prepared to move on to the higher levels of reading.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Read independently
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Once elementary reading is mastered, read independently and learn on your own.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Am I learning on my own, without a teacher smoothing difficulties?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: Only then can he read independently and learn on his own.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Remedial is not higher
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Do not mistake remedial reading instruction for training in the higher levels of reading.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Is this course teaching higher levels or just catching up basics?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: Remedial reading instruction is not instruction in the higher levels of reading.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Speed courses are remedial
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Do not expect speed or effective-reading courses to take you beyond the first level.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Does this course aim beyond elementary reading?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: On the whole (though there are exceptions), these courses are remedial.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Aim for analytical competence
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Aim to become a competent analytical reader, as a good high school should produce.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Am I a competent analytical reader yet?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: A good liberal arts high school, if it does nothing else, ought to produce graduates who are competent analytical readers.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Aim for syntopical competence
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Aim further to become a competent syntopical reader, able to do independent research on almost any subject.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Could I undertake independent research on a subject from books?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: A good college, if it does nothing else, ought to produce competent syntopical readers.

elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.title: Beyond functional literacy
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.action: Aim to be a truly competent reader, not merely functionally literate.
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.check: Am I a competent reader, or just functionally literate?
elementary/the-first-level-of-reading-el.quote: We must be more than a nation of functional literates.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read the text steadily
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Before reading inspectionally, be able to read the text steadily without many lookups or stumbling over grammar and syntax.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can I read on without stopping often for words or grammar?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: You must be able to read an author’s text more or less steadily, without having to stop to look up the meaning of many words

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Make sense of most
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Make sense of most sentences and paragraphs, though not necessarily the best sense of all.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can I make some sense of the majority of sentences and paragraphs?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: You must be able to make sense of a majority of the sentences and paragraphs, although not necessarily the best sense of all of them.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Two steps of inspection
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: As a beginner, treat systematic skimming and superficial reading as two separate steps.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I doing skimming and superficial reading as distinct steps?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: the beginning reader is well-advised to consider them as two different steps or activities.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Later, do both together
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: As you gain experience, learn to perform both inspectional steps at the same time.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can I now skim and read superficially in one pass?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: The experienced reader learns to perform both steps simultaneously

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Skim when unsure
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Skim the book when you don't know whether it deserves careful reading and your time is limited.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I know yet whether this book deserves an analytical reading?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: In this case, what you must do is skim the book, or, as some prefer to say, pre-read it.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Decide on careful reading
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Skim mainly to find out whether the book requires a more careful reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Does this book need a more careful reading?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Your main aim is to discover whether the book requires a more careful reading.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Separate chaff from kernels
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Use skimming as a threshing process to separate what is worth your time from what is not.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: What, if anything, in this book is worth more of my time?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: a threshing process that helps you to separate the chaff from the real kernels of nourishment.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Main contention and kind
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Come away from skimming knowing at least the author's main contention and what kind of book it is.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can I state the author's main contention and the kind of book?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: you will know at least what the author’s main contention is, as well as what kind of book he has written

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read title page and preface
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Look at the title page and preface, read each quickly, and note subtitles or signs of the book's scope, aim, or angle.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I now have a good idea of the subject?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Note especially the subtitles or other indications of the scope or aim of the book or of the author’s special angle on his subject.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Pigeonhole the book
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Pause to place the book in the right category in your mind alongside other books.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: What pigeonhole that already contains other books does this one belong in?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: What pigeonhole that already contains other books does this one belong in?

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Study the table of contents
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Study the table of contents to get a general sense of the book's structure, using it like a road map before a trip.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I have a general sense of how the book is structured?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: use it as you would a road map before taking a trip.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Never glancing at the table of contents except to look something up.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read contents carefully
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read the table of contents carefully before going on to the rest of the book, even if chapter titles seem mysterious.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I read the whole table of contents before starting?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: a table of contents can be valuable, and you should read it carefully before going on to the rest of the book.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Check the index
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Check the index, quickly estimating the range of topics and the kinds of books and authors referred to.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: What range of topics and authors does the index show?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Make a quick estimate of the range of topics covered and of the kinds of books and authors referred to.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Look up crucial terms
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: For index terms that seem crucial, look up at least some of the passages cited; they may hold the book's crux.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did a cited passage show the point on which the book hinges?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: When you see terms listed that seem crucial, look up at least some of the passages cited.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Judge terms from steps 1-2
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Decide which index terms are crucial from your general sense of the book gained in steps 1 and 2.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I picking terms based on what the title, preface and contents told me?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Here you must make your judgment of their importance on the basis of your general sense of the book, as obtained from steps 1 and 2.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Count index references
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Use the number of references under an index term to spot which terms are important.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can you identify, for example, by the number of references under them, any others that also seem important?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Can you identify, for example, by the number of references under them, any others that also seem important?

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read the publisher's blurb
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: If the book has a dust jacket, read the publisher's blurb, which often summarizes the main points accurately.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: What main points does the blurb claim for the book?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: It is not uncommon for authors to try to summarize as accurately as they can the main points in their book.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Dismissing every blurb as sheer puffery.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read an empty blurb
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: If the blurb is pure puff, take that as a sign the book may say nothing of importance.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Does the blurb say anything, or is it mere puffery?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Perhaps the book does not say anything of importance—and that is why the blurb does not say anything, either.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Decide after four steps
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: After the first four steps, decide whether to read the book carefully, drop it, or go on to skim it properly.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I already know whether I want to read this book carefully?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Upon completing these first four steps you may already have enough information about the book

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Look at pivotal chapters
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Look at the chapters that seem pivotal to the argument, reading carefully any summary statements at their opening or close.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Have I read the summaries of the chapters that carry the argument?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: If these chapters have summary statements in their opening or closing pages, as they often do, read these statements carefully.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Dip in here and there
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Turn the pages, dipping in to read a paragraph or two, sometimes several pages in sequence, never more.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I sample throughout without settling into reading whole chapters?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Thumb through the book in this way, always looking for signs of the main contention, listening for the basic pulsebeat of the matter.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read the last pages
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Always read the last two or three pages, or the last pages of the main part if the end is an epilogue.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I read where the author sums up what is new and important?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Above all, do not fail to read the last two or three pages, or, if these are an epilogue, the last few pages of the main part of the book.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Skim in minutes
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Keep systematic skimming to a few minutes, at most an hour.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I spend no more than an hour skimming?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: after having spent no more than a few minutes, at most an hour, with it.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: File the book mentally
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: After skimming, decide whether the book deserves more time and place it in your mental card catalogue.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I know whether to dig further, and where the book fits?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: You should also be able to place the book even more accurately than before in your mental card catalogue

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Stay alert while skimming
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Keep all your faculties awake while skimming; it is a very active kind of reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I daydream through pages without knowing what I covered?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: It is impossible to give any book an inspectional reading without being alert, without having all of one’s faculties awake and working.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Daydreaming through several pages with no idea of the ground covered.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Follow a general thread
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Use a system so that you follow a general thread through the book.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can I trace the general thread of the book?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: if you have a system for following a general thread.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read like a detective
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Think of yourself as a detective hunting for clues to the book's general theme or idea.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: What clues to the main theme have I found?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Think of yourself as a detective looking for clues to a book’s general theme or idea, alert for anything that will make it clearer.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read straight through first
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: On a first reading of a difficult book, read it through without stopping to look up or ponder what you don't understand.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I reach the end without stopping at difficulties?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: In tackling a difficult book for the first time, read it through without ever stopping to look up or ponder the things you do not understand right away.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Don't expect too much
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Don't expect too much from the first going-over of a difficult book.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I demanding full understanding on a first pass?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Rather it was in expecting too much from the first going over of a difficult book.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Concluding it was a mistake to try a difficult book at all.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Attend to what you understand
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Pay attention to what you can understand and don't be stopped by what you can't grasp right away.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I concentrate on the parts I could understand?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Pay attention to what you can understand and do not be stopped by what you cannot immediately grasp.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read past difficulties
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Keep reading past difficult points; you will soon reach things you understand, and should concentrate on those.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: When I hit a hard patch, did I keep going?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Go right on reading past the point where you have difficulties in understanding, and you will soon come to things you do understand.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read undeterred
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read the book through, undismayed by paragraphs, footnotes, comments and references that escape you.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I let footnotes or references stop me?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Read the book through, undeterred and undismayed by the paragraphs, footnotes, comments, and references that escape you.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Don't get stalled
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Do not let any one stumbling block stall you; sticking to it seldom solves it.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I get stuck trying to puzzle out one passage?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: If you let yourself get stalled, if you allow yourself to be tripped up by any one of these stumbling blocks, you are lost.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Stopping at the first difficult passage.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read once to reread
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Finish one complete reading so a second reading can resolve what you passed over.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Have I read the whole book once, so a second reading can work?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: You will have a much better chance of understanding it on a second reading, but that requires you to have read the book through at least once.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Half is better than none
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Accept understanding only half of a really tough book on the first reading rather than none of it.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I understand some of the book rather than nothing?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: understanding half of a really tough book is much better than not understanding it at all

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: No premature lookups
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Don't run to dictionaries, encyclopedias, footnotes or commentaries during a first reading; done prematurely they impede reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I interrupt my first reading with reference works?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: But when these things are done prematurely, they only impede our reading, instead of helping it.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Looking up every strange word and studying every footnote first time through.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read a play at one sitting
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read a play at one sitting and discuss what you got from that first quick reading before studying it closely.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I read the whole play through before studying it scene by scene?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: they should have been encouraged to read the play at one sitting and discuss what they got out of that first quick reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Forgetting the beginning by the end and losing sight of the whole.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Don't miss the big points
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: In expository works, don't insist on understanding every page before moving on, or you will miss the big points.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I catch the author's big points, not just fine ones?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: In your effort to master the fine points, you will miss the big points
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Missing the forest for the trees.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Do both steps quickly
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Carry out both steps of inspectional reading rapidly, whatever the length or difficulty of the book.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I inspect this book quickly despite its length?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: The competent inspectional reader will accomplish them both quickly, no matter how long or difficult the book he is trying to read.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read some things faster
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read faster the things not worth much time, so you don't waste time on them.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I spending more time on this than it is worth?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: most people ought to be able to read faster than they do.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Some things too fast
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Slow down for things you are reading too fast.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I racing through something that deserves slower reading?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: But many people also read some things too fast, and they ought to read those things more slowly.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Vary your rate
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Vary your reading rate according to the nature and complexity of the material.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did my speed match the nature and complexity of this material?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: It should enable you to vary your rate of reading in accordance with the nature and complexity of the material.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Skip, fast, or slow
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Sort books into those hardly worth skimming, those to read quickly, and the few to read slowly for complete comprehension.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Which of the three groups does this book belong to?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Many books are hardly worth even skimming; some should be read quickly; and a few should be read at a rate, usually quite slow, that allows for complete comprehension.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Know what to look for
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Learn the rules of reading so you know what you are looking for and when you've found it; speed alone won't help.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I know what I am looking for in this book?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: he does not know what he is looking for and does not know when he has found it.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Thinking speed solves the problems of a difficult book.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Know which speed when
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Be able to read at different speeds and know when each speed is appropriate.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I know why this passage calls for this speed?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: the ideal is not merely to be able to read faster, but to be able to read at different speeds— and to know when the different speeds are appropriate.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Inspection reads less
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: In inspectional reading read less of the book, in a different way and with different goals, not just faster.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I reading selectively, with inspectional goals?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: you read less of a book when you give it an inspectional reading, and because you read it in a different way, with different goals in mind.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read filler quickly
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Even in analytical reading, read the interstitial material of a book quickly.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I move quickly through connecting material?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Every book, no matter how difficult, contains interstitial material that can be and should be read quickly

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Read hard parts slowly
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read the difficult matter in a good book very slowly.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I slow down on the difficult passages?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: every good book also contains matter that is difficult and should be read very slowly.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Stop sub-vocalizing
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Notice and outgrow the habit of sub-vocalizing as you read.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I silently sounding each word?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: most people continue to sub-vocalize for years after they are first taught to read.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Eye fixations
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Know that untrained eyes stop five or six times per line, taking in only a word or short phrase each time.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: How many times do my eyes stop on each line?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: the eyes of young or untrained readers “fixate” as many as five or six times in the course of each line that is read.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Eye regressions
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Know that poor readers' eyes go back to earlier phrases or sentences as often as every two or three lines.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do my eyes keep jumping back to reread?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: the eyes of incompetent readers regress as often as once every two or three lines

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Let the mind take more
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Feed your mind larger units; it can grasp a whole sentence or paragraph at a glance.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I taking in phrases and sentences rather than single words?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: The mind, that astounding instrument, can grasp a sentence or even a paragraph at a “glance”

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Correct fixations and regressions
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Correct your fixations and regressions so you read as fast as your mind allows, not as slow as your eyes make you.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I reading as fast as my mind will let me?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Thus the primary task—recognized as such by all speed reading courses—is to correct the fixations and regressions that slow so many readers down.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Make a hand pointer
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Put your thumb and first two fingers together to make a pointer to guide your eyes.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I using my hand to pace my eyes?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Place your thumb and first two fingers together.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Sweep a bit too fast
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Sweep the pointer across each line a little faster than is comfortable for your eyes, and force yourself to keep up.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Was my hand moving slightly faster than felt comfortable?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Sweep this “pointer” across a line of type, a little faster than it is comfortable for your eyes to move.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Keep up with your hand
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Force your eyes to keep up with your moving hand until you can read the words as you follow it.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can I read the words while following my hand?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Force yourself to keep up with your hand.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Keep raising the speed
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Keep practising and steadily increase the speed of your hand until your reading speed doubles or trebles.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Has my reading speed doubled or trebled?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Keep practicing this, and keep increasing the speed at which your hand moves

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Pace to concentrate
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Use your hand or another timer to keep your mind from wandering and improve concentration.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did pacing with my hand keep me from daydreaming?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: As long as you are following your hand it is harder to fall asleep, to daydream, to let your mind wander.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Concentration is activity
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read actively, with concentration, since concentration is another name for activity in reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Was I concentrating, or drifting?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Concentration is another name for what we have called activity in reading.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Concentration is not comprehension
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Don't assume that concentration alone gives comprehension properly understood.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Beyond concentrating, did I actually comprehend?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: But concentration alone does not really have much of an effect on comprehension, when that is properly understood.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: More than answering facts
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Aim at comprehension beyond answering simple factual questions about what the text says.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Can I answer more than factual questions about this text?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Comprehension involves much more than merely being able to answer simple questions of fact about a text.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.mistake: Equating comprehension with answering “What does it say?”

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Vary speed in one text
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read the Declaration of Independence: skim its list of facts and closing flourish, but read its first two paragraphs slowly.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I read the opening paragraphs far more slowly than the list of grievances?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: But the first two paragraphs of the Declaration of Independence require more than a first rapid reading.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Rhetoric deserves speed
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read mere rhetorical flourishes quickly.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Is this passage substance or a rhetorical flourish?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: This is a rhetorical flourish, and it deserves what mere rhetoric always deserves.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Dwell on key words
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Dwell on and puzzle over key words, such as inalienable, rights, liberty and consent, when reading for full comprehension.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I stop to consider the meaning of the crucial words?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: are worth dwelling over, puzzling about, considering at length.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Comprehend analytically
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: To comprehend a book, read it analytically, since analytical reading exists for the sake of understanding.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Have I read this book analytically, or only fast?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: You cannot comprehend a book without reading it analytically

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Speed versus comprehension
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Treat the real problem of speed reading as the problem of comprehension beyond the elementary level.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did reading faster cost me comprehension?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: The problem of speed reading, then, is the problem of comprehension.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: No single right speed
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Have no single reading speed; develop the ability to read at various speeds and to know when each fits.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Is there one speed I use for everything?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: There is no single right speed at which you should read

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Speed is dubious
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Value great speed only for material not really worth reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Is this worth reading carefully, or only quickly?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Great speed in reading is a dubious achievement; it is of value only if what you have to read is not really worth reading.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: The speed formula
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Read every book no more slowly than it deserves and no more quickly than you can with satisfaction and comprehension.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I reading this as slowly as it deserves, and no faster than I comprehend?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Every book should be read no more slowly than it deserves, and no more quickly than you can read it with satisfaction and comprehension.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Always skim first
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Skim before reading, especially when you don't know whether a book is worth reading carefully.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I skim this book before deciding how to read it?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Skimming or pre-reading a book is always a good idea

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Skim books you'll study
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Skim even a book you intend to read carefully, to get an idea of its form and structure.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Do I know the book's form and structure before reading closely?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: It is generally desirable to skim even a book that you intend to read carefully, to get some idea of its form and structure.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Don't understand everything first
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Do not try to understand every word or page of a difficult book the first time through.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did I let myself pass over what I didn't understand on the first reading?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: This is the most important rule of all; it is the essence of inspectional reading.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Dare to be superficial
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Do not be afraid to be, or seem, superficial on a first reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Did fear of seeming superficial slow me down?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Do not be afraid to be, or to seem to be, superficial.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Race through the hardest
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Race through even the hardest book first, to prepare yourself to read it well the second time.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Am I ready to read this well a second time?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Race through even the hardest book.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Skimming prepares stage one
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Use systematic skimming as preparation for grasping the book's structure in the first stage of analytical reading.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Does my skim help me state the book's structure?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Systematic skimming, in other words, anticipates the comprehension of a book’s structure.

inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.title: Superficial reading prepares stage two
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.action: Use superficial reading as the first step toward interpreting the book's contents in the second analytical stage.
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.check: Has my first read-through prepared me to interpret the contents?
inspectional/the-second-level-of-reading.quote: Superficial reading is the first necessary step in the interpretation of a book’s contents.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.title: Keep awake to profit
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.action: When you read to grow in mind, keep awake by reading as actively as possible.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.check: Am I wide awake and working, or drifting?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.quote: If your aim in reading is to profit from it—to grow somehow in mind or spirit—you have to keep awake.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.title: No good book as sedative
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.action: Don't use a good book as a sleeping aid or let your mind wander during time set aside for reading.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.check: Did my mind wander during my reading time?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.quote: To use a good book as a sedative is conspicuous waste.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.title: Make your mind work
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.action: Keep your mind on the book by making it do the work without which no profit is earned.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.check: Did my mind do real work on the book?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/sta.quote: how to keep their mind on what they are doing by making it do the work without which no profit can be earned.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Ask questions while reading
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Ask questions while you read, questions you yourself must try to answer in the course of reading.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: What questions did I ask, and did I try to answer them?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: Ask questions while you read—questions that you yourself must try to answer in the course of reading.
