general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Right questions, right order
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Form the habit of asking the right questions in the right order.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Did I ask the four questions in order?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: The art of reading on any level above the elementary consists in the habit of asking the right questions in the right order.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: What is it about?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Discover the book's leading theme and how the author develops it through subordinate themes or topics.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: What is the book about as a whole?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: You must try to discover the leading theme of the book, and how the author develops this theme in an orderly way

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: What is said, and how?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Discover the main ideas, assertions and arguments that make up the author's particular message.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: What is being said in detail, and how?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: You must try to discover the main ideas, assertions, and arguments that constitute the author’s particular message.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Is it true?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Decide whether the book is true in whole or part, but only after answering the first two questions.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Is the book true, in whole or part?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: You have to know what is being said before you can decide whether it is true or not.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.mistake: Judging truth before knowing what is being said.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Make up your own mind
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Once you understand a book, make up your own mind about it; knowing the author's mind is not enough.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Have I reached my own judgment, not just learned the author's?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: When you understand a book, however, you are obligated, if you are reading seriously, to make up your own mind.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: What of it?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Ask the significance of what the book tells you: why the author thinks it important, and whether it matters to you.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Why does the author think it is important to know these things? Is it important to you to know them?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: If the book has given you information, you must ask about its significance.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: What else follows?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: If the book has enlightened you, seek further enlightenment by asking what else follows or is implied.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: What else follows, what is further implied or suggested?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: it is necessary to seek further enlightenment by asking what else follows, what is further implied or suggested.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Ask of anything
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Ask the four questions of anything worth reading, from books to articles and advertisements.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Did I put the four questions to this article or ad?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: They apply to anything worth reading—a book or an article or even an advertisement.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: No questions, no answers
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Be a demanding reader; the undemanding reader asks no questions and gets no answers.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Did I ask the book anything at all?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: The latter asks no questions—and gets no answers.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Inspection answers first two
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Expect inspectional reading to answer the first two questions better than the last two.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Are my answers to questions 3 and 4 still tentative?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: Inspectional reading tends to provide more accurate answers to the first two questions than to the last two

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Finish with all four
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Don't consider an analytical reading done until you can answer the questions of truth and significance.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Do I have some idea of the book's truth and its significance to me?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: An analytical reading of a book has not been accomplished satisfactorily until you have answers to those last questions

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: What of it in syntopical
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: In syntopical reading give special weight to the question What of it?, after answering the first three.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Have I answered the first three before asking what of it?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: The last question—What of it?—is probably the most important one in syntopical reading.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Remember to ask them
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Remember to ask the four questions as you read; the habit marks a demanding reader.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Did I actually ask the four questions while reading?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: You must remember to ask them as you read.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Answer precisely
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Learn to answer the four questions precisely and accurately.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Are my answers precise and accurate, or vague?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: you must know how to answer them precisely and accurately.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Will plus skill
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Bring both the will and the skill to read actively, so you can reach up to books over your head.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Do I have the skill, not just the will, for this book?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: To keep on reading actively, you must have not only the will to do so, but also the skill

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Stretch with skill
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Develop the skill to stretch effectively; frustrated, unskilled stretching is what makes good books tiring.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Am I tired from the effort, or from not knowing how to make it?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: It is not the stretching that tires you, but the frustration of stretching unsuccessfully because you lack the skill to stretch effectively.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Adapt questions for fiction
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Adapt the four questions when reading fiction and poetry, since as stated they suit expository works.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Have I adjusted the questions to this novel or poem?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: the questions, when adapted, apply to fiction and poetry as well.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Read with a pencil
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Answer your questions with a pencil in hand, as a sign of your alertness.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Do I have a pencil in hand while reading?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: it is much easier to do it with a pencil in your hand.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Write between the lines
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Write between the lines as well as reading between them.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Did I write my reactions in the book?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: But we want to persuade you to “write between the lines,” too.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Own it by writing
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Make the book a part of yourself by writing in it; purchase is only the prelude to ownership.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Have I made the book mine, or only bought it?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: Full ownership of a book only comes when you have made it a part of yourself

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Marking keeps you awake
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Mark the book to keep yourself wide awake, not merely conscious.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Am I wide awake as I mark the text?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: First, it keeps you awake—not merely conscious, but wide awake.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Put thoughts in words
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Express your thinking in written words as you read, since thinking tends to express itself in words.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Can I write down what I think about this passage?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: The person who says he knows what he thinks but cannot express it usually does not know what he thinks.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Write to remember
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Write your reactions down to help you remember the author's thoughts.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Will my notes help me recall the author's thought later?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: Third, writing your reactions down helps you to remember the thoughts of the author.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Converse with the author
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Treat reading as a conversation, questioning the author and yourself, and arguing once you understand.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Have I questioned and, where warranted, argued with the author?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: Reading a book should be a conversation between you and the author.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Argue after understanding
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Be willing to argue with the author, but only once you understand what he is saying.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Do I understand his point well enough to argue with it?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: He even has to be willing to argue with the teacher, once he understands what the teacher is saying.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Underline major points
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Underline major points and important or forceful statements.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Are my underlines on major points, not everything?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: of major points; of important or forceful statements.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Vertical lines in margin
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Draw vertical lines in the margin to stress an underlined statement or mark a passage too long to underline.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Did I mark long key passages with margin lines?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: to emphasize a statement already underlined or to point to a passage too long to be underlined.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Star the top dozen
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Use a star or asterisk sparingly in the margin to flag the ten or dozen most important passages in the book.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Have I limited stars to about a dozen key passages?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: to be used sparingly, to emphasize the ten or dozen most important statements or passages in the book.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.mistake: Starring so many passages the marks lose meaning.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Flag starred pages
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Fold the corner or insert a slip at pages with stars so you can quickly refresh your memory later.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Can I find my most important passages quickly?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: You may want to fold a corner of each page on which you make such marks or place a slip of paper between the pages.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Number argument steps
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Write numbers in the margin to show the sequence of points in the author's argument.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Can I follow the argument's steps from my numbering?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: to indicate a sequence of points made by the author in developing an argument.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Cross-reference pages
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Write other page numbers in the margin, often with Cf, where the author makes the same, related or contradictory points.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Have I linked related points scattered across the book?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: to indicate where else in the book the author makes the same points

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: The Cf symbol
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Use Cf before a page number to mean compare or refer to.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Did I use Cf to tie related passages together?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: Many readers use the symbol “Cf” to indicate the other page numbers; it means “compare” or “refer to.”

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Circle key words
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Circle key words or phrases, much as you would underline.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Have I circled the key words?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: This serves much the same function as underlining.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Write in the margins
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Write in margins or at top or bottom of the page to record questions, simplify complex discussions, and track major points.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Did I note my questions and reduce complex passages to simple statements?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: to record questions (and perhaps answers) which a passage raises in your mind; to reduce a complicated discussion to a simple statement

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Personal index at back
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Use the back endpapers to make a personal index of the author's points in the order they appear.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Does my back-endpaper index list the points in order?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: The endpapers at the back of the book can be used to make a personal index of the author’s points in the order of their appearance.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Outline at front
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: After finishing, outline the book on the front endpapers as an integrated structure with a basic outline and order of parts.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Does my outline show the book's whole structure, not just a list of points?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: turn to the front and try to outline the book, not page by page or point by point

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.title: Outline measures understanding
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.action: Use your front-endpaper outline as the measure of your understanding and intellectual ownership.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.check: Could I outline the book's structure from memory?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/how.quote: That outline will be the measure of your understanding of the work

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Notes depend on level
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Choose the kind of notes according to the level at which you are reading.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Which level am I reading at, and so which notes fit?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: Which kind you make depends upon the level at which you are reading.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Inspectional note questions
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: When reading inspectionally, note what kind of book it is, what it is about, and its structural order.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: What kind of book is it? What is it about as a whole? What is its structural order?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: first, what kind of book is it? second, what is it about as a whole?

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Record answers fresh
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Record your inspectional answers while fresh, especially if analytical reading must wait days or months.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Did I jot down my answers before I forget them?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: it would be desirable, even if it is not always possible, to record your answers when they are fresh in your mind.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Use contents or title page
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Write structural notes on the contents page or the title page.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Are my structural notes on the contents or title page?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: The best place to make such notes is on the contents page, or perhaps on the title page

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Structural notes
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Make structural notes about the book's structure, not its detailed substance.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Do these notes concern structure rather than substance?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: these notes primarily concern the structure of the book, and not its substance

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Defer judgment of truth
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Put off judging the accuracy or truth of statements until you have read the book more carefully.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Am I judging truth before a careful reading?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: certainly you should put off making any judgment of the accuracy or truth of the statements until you have read the book more carefully.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Conceptual notes
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: During analytical reading, make conceptual notes about the author's concepts and your own as they develop.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Do my notes record the author's concepts and how my own changed?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: They concern the author’s concepts, and also your own, as they have been deepened or broadened by your reading of the book.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Cross-book references
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: In syntopical reading, let conceptual notes refer to pages in other books as well as this one.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Do my notes link to pages in the other books?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: the notes on a page may refer you not only to other pages in that book, but also to pages in other books.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Dialectical notes
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: As an expert syntopical reader, make dialectical notes on the shape of the discussion among all the authors.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Do my notes map the discussion across the authors?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: That is to make notes about the shape of the discussion

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.title: Separate sheets
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.action: Make dialectical notes on separate sheets, since they concern several books.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.check: Have I put cross-book notes on separate sheets?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/the.quote: they often have to be made on a separate sheet (or sheets) of paper.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.title: Skill is habit
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.action: Treat an art as a habit of operating according to its rules.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.check: Am I operating by the rules habitually yet?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.quote: Any art or skill is possessed by those who have formed the habit of operating according to its rules.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.title: Learn by doing
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.action: Form the reading habit by actually reading according to the rules, again and again.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.check: Am I practising the rules, or only reading about them?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.quote: Now there is no other way of forming a habit of operation than by operating.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.title: Practice makes perfect
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.action: Practise until what you did imperfectly becomes almost automatic, second nature.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.check: Has this step become easier and more automatic?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.quote: That is what it means to say practice makes perfect.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.title: Rules versus habit
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.action: Don't confuse knowing the rules with having the habit; skill is possessing the habit.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.check: Can I do it, or only state the rules?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.quote: Knowing the rules of an art is not the same as having the habit.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.title: Know the rules
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.action: Learn the rules explicitly, since you cannot follow rules you do not know.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.check: Do I know the rules I am trying to follow?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.quote: You cannot follow rules you do not know.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.title: Originality still uses rules
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.action: Do not think skilled originality dispenses with rules; even original artists follow rules of their craft.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.check: Am I excusing myself from rules in the name of originality?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/for.quote: not everyone understands that being an artist consists in operating according to rules.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Learn acts separately first
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: Learn each separate act of reading first as a separate act, before trying to fuse them.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Have I practised this act on its own?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: But in order to forget them as separate acts, you have to learn them first as separate acts.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Full attention per act
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: Give each separate act your full attention while you are doing it.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Was I focusing fully on the one act I was practising?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: Each separate act requires your full attention while you are doing it.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Then combine into a whole
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: After practising the parts separately, gradually put them together into a smoothly running whole.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Are the separate acts starting to run together smoothly?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: After you have practiced the parts separately, you can not only do each with greater facility and less attention

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Forget acts to perform them
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: Aim eventually to forget the separate acts so you can perform them all well together.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Am I still thinking about each step, or reading fluently?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: you must learn to forget the separate acts in order to perform all of them, and indeed any of them, well.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Be patient
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: Recall your patience in learning other skills and be tolerant of the long list of reading rules.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Am I being as patient as when I learned other skills?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: If you can recall your patience in any other learning experience you have had, you will be more tolerant

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Don't fear many rules
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: Do not be daunted by the number of rules at the start of learning.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Am I discouraged by how many rules there are?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: he need not fear the array of rules that present themselves at the beginning of something new to be learned.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Many rules, one habit
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: See the many rules as parts of one complex habit, not many distinct habits.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Do I see the rules as one integrated habit?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: The multiplicity of the rules indicates the complexity of the one habit to be formed, not a plurality of distinct habits.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Then attend to the goal
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: Once the acts are automatic, turn your attention from technique to the goal it lets you reach.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Am I now thinking about the book rather than my technique?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: the learner can at last pay attention to the goal that the technique he has acquired enables him to reach.

general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.title: Think about your thinking
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.action: As a beginning analytical reader, be conscious of your own mental acts while reading.
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.check: Am I aware of which mental act I am performing?
general/how-to-be-a-demanding-reader/fro.quote: in a sense, he is thinking about his own thoughts.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/reading-w.title: Adapt rules to shorter pieces
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/reading-w.action: Apply the rules given for whole books to articles, stories and other shorter materials, adapting them where they do not fit exactly.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/reading-w.check: Have I adapted the rule to this shorter piece rather than skipping it?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/reading-w.quote: it will always be easy for you to adapt them so that they are applicable.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.title: Know what kind of book
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.action: Know what kind of book you are reading, and know it as early as possible, preferably before you begin to read.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.check: Before starting, can I say what kind of book this is?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.quote: MUST KNOW WHAT KIND OF BOOK YOU ARE READING, AND YOU SHOULD KNOW THIS AS EARLY IN THE PROCESS AS POSSIBLE, PREFERABLY BEFORE YOU BEGIN TO READ.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.title: Fiction vs. expository
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.action: Decide first whether the book is fiction (novel, play, epic, lyric) or an expository work that conveys knowledge.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.check: Is this book primarily telling a story, or conveying knowledge claimed to be true in some sense?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.quote: An expository book is one that conveys knowledge primarily, “knowledge” being construed broadly.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.title: Fiction can look like science
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.action: Do not assume the fiction/nonfiction line is always obvious; some novels carry much social science and some sociology much fiction.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.check: Have I checked whether this novel or study might be mistaken for the other kind?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.quote: There is so much social science in some contemporary novels, and so much fiction in much of sociology, that it is hard to keep them apart.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.mistake: Judging a book's kind from its readability or its best-seller list category alone.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.title: Identify the kind of instruction
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.action: For an expository book, go beyond 'it instructs' and identify in what particular way it instructs: history, philosophy, physics, morals and so on.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.check: Do I know what kind of problems this book deals with and what methods it will use?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.quote: It is not merely a question of knowing which books are primarily instructive, but also which are instructive in a particular way.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.title: Inspect to classify
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.action: Classify the book by inspecting it: read the title, subtitle and table of contents, glance at the preface and index, and read the publisher’s blurb.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.check: Have I read the front matter and blurb before deciding what kind of book this is?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/the-impor.quote: These are the signal flags the author waves to let you know which way the wind is blowing.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Ask what sort of book
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Begin any discussion or reading of a book by stating, in the most general terms, what sort of book it is.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: In the most general terms, what sort of book is this?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: This is a good way, almost an indispensable way, to begin a discussion of a book.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Read the title exactly
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Read the title carefully, word for word, and think about what it means instead of assuming you know it.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: Can I state the exact title and explain what each word in it tells me?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: many think they know the title of the book, although few have actually ever read the title carefully and thought about what it means.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.mistake: Misreading a title from assumptions, e.g. 'The Origin of the Species' for Darwin's book.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Draw inferences from title
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Work out what the title implies about the book’s scope and starting point before you start reading.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: What does the title lead me to expect about where the book begins and ends?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: Reading the title, in other words, could have given them essential information about the book before they started to read it
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.mistake: Silently translating the title into something else, e.g. 'decline and fall' into 'rise and fall'.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Use preface and chapter headings
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Use the preface, subtitle and chapter headings, which authors write to show what kind of book they are giving you and to amplify the title.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: Have I read what the author says in the preface about how the book should be read?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: the chapter headings listed in the front serve the purpose of amplifying the significance of the main title.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Never skip the kind question
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Ask yourself what kind of book this is; if you cannot answer it, expect to be unable to answer many other questions about the book.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: Have I explicitly asked myself what kind of book this is?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: If he cannot answer that question, and if he never asks it of himself, he is going to be unable to answer a lot of other questions about the book.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Carry classification categories
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Keep the broad lines of classification in your mind, because titles and front matter cannot help you classify without them.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: Do I have categories ready (fiction, history, science, philosophy, practical) to place this book in?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: will not help you to classify a book unless you have the broad lines of classification already in your mind.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Name the kind itself
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Do not stop at noticing that books are alike; name what kind of book they are.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: Can I name the category, not just say it resembles some other book?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: to group books as being of the same kind is not enough; to follow this first rule of reading you must know what that kind is.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Peruse headings for problems
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: When titles do not reveal the kind, look carefully through the chapter headings to find the problems the book shares with others.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: Do the chapter headings show which problems this book treats?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: a careful perusal of their chapter headings would reveal the problems that are common to these three books.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.title: Rough classification of books
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.action: Divide books into fiction and expository works, and divide expository works further into history, philosophy, science and mathematics.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.check: Which of these slots does the book fit: fiction, history, philosophy, science, mathematics?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/what-you-.quote: Among expository works, we can further distinguish history from philosophy, and both from science and mathematics.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Knowledge or action
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Ask whether the writer’s end is knowledge (something to be seen or understood) or action (something that works).
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Is the author aiming at my understanding, or at what I should do?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: we come to the distinction between knowledge and action as the two ends a writer may have in mind.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Knowing that vs. how
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Classify the book as theoretical if it teaches that something is the case, and practical if it teaches how to do something.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Does the book teach me that something is so, or how to do something?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: Theoretical books teach you that something is the case. Practical books teach you how to do something you want to do or think you should do.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: What counts as practical
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Treat as practical any book telling you what you should do or how to do it: arts, manuals, and moral works on ethics, economics or politics.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Does this book tell me what I should do or how to do it?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: Any book that tells you either what you should do or how to do it is practical.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Disagreeing is not impractical
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Do not call a book theoretical or unpractical just because you think its advice is wrong or would not work.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Am I classifying by the book’s aim, or by whether I agree with it?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: Again, we may disagree, but our disagreement does not make the book unpractical.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.mistake: Calling an ethics or economics book 'impractical' because you reject its conclusions.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Reporting behavior is theoretical
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Classify studies that merely report or measure behavior without judging it as theoretical works, even in fields like sociology or economics.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Does the book judge what should be done, or only report what is done?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: Some modern sociological studies merely report the actual behavior of men, without judging it.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Expect persuasion in practical books
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Expect a practical book to try to persuade you as well as advise you, and recognize its oratorical element.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Where is the author trying to persuade me to follow the advice?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: Anyone who writes practically about anything not only tries to advise you but also tries to persuade you to follow his advice.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Oratory vs. treatise
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Distinguish mere oratory or propaganda from a practical treatise or analysis, even though every practical book is somewhat hortatory.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Is this a harangue, or an analysis of a practical problem?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: There is a difference between a political harangue and a treatise on politics, between economic propaganda and an analysis of economic problems.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Spot practical titles
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Look in the title for phrases like 'the art of' or 'how to', or names of practical fields such as ethics, politics, engineering or business.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Does the title contain a practical phrase or name a practical field?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: If the title contains such phrases as “the art of” or “how to,” you can spot it at once.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Validity vs. purpose questions
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Read the author's stated intention: questions about validity or certainty mark a theoretical book; questions about the end or purpose mark a practical one.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Is the author asking whether something is valid, or what end it serves?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: Questions about the validity of something are theoretical, whereas to raise questions about the end of anything, the purpose it serves, is practical.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Read summaries, beginnings, ends
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: When front matter does not settle the kind, read summary passages and the beginning and end of the book and of its major parts.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Have I sampled summary passages and the openings and closings of major parts?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: You should also read the beginning and end of the book and of its major parts.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Watch for should and ought
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Watch for frequent 'should' and 'ought', 'good' and 'bad', 'ends' and 'means': they reveal a practical book.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Are the characteristic statements about what should be done or what is better?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: A practical book will soon betray its character by the frequent occurrence of such words as “should” and “ought,” “good” and “bad,” “ends” and “means.”

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Theoretical books say 'is'
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Recognize a theoretical book by its steady use of 'is': it tries to show what is true and what the facts are.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Is the book showing that something is true rather than how to make things better?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: In contrast, a theoretical book keeps saying “is,” not “should” or “ought.”

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Be suspicious of signs
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Treat these signs with suspicion; some economics books are purely theoretical and some books claim to teach 'how to think'.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Have I confirmed the classification with more than one sign?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: You have to be suspicious in classifying books.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.mistake: Classifying by field name alone, as if economics were always practical.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.title: Detect the author's approach
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.action: Expect some books to be partly theoretical and partly practical, and still work out how the author approaches his problem.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.check: Which parts are theoretical and which practical, and how does the author approach the problem?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/practical.quote: It remains, nevertheless, to your advantage as a reader to detect the way an author approaches his problem.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: History, science, philosophy
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Subdivide theoretical books into history, science and philosophy, using rough approximations at first.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Is this theoretical book history, science or philosophy?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: The traditional subdivision of theoretical books classifies them as history, science, and philosophy.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: History is narration
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Recognize history by its narration of particular past events or things that changed over time, usually signalled by the title or front matter.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Does the book narrate particular past happenings, whether long ago or yesterday?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: The essence of history is narration.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: History is chronotopic
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Remember that history always deals with things or events at a particular date and particular place.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Are the events tied to specific times and places?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: History always deals with things that existed or events that occurred on a particular date and in a particular place.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Science seeks laws
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Recognize science by its search for laws or generalizations that hold at any time or place, not for how particular things happened.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Is the author after what happens for the most part or in every case?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: The scientist seeks laws or generalizations.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Science titles reveal less
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Do not rely on the title of a scientific work; the subject name may belong to science or philosophy, or both.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Does this subject matter belong to the scientist, the philosopher, or both?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: The title of a scientific work is usually less revealing than the title of a history book.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Philosophy seeks general truths
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Recognize philosophy as seeking general truths like science, but asking different questions with a different method.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Does the book seek general truths without relying on special investigations?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: Philosophy is like science and unlike history in that it seeks general truths rather than an account of particular events

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Special vs. common experience
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Call a theoretical book scientific if it relies on experience beyond normal daily life, and philosophical if it relies only on common experience.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Does the book appeal to laboratory, field or clinical experience, or to experience everyone has?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: If a theoretical book emphasizes things that lie outside the scope of your normal, routine, daily experience, it is a scientific work. If not, it is philosophical.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Note the experience referred to
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: While reading, note what sort of experience the author requires as a condition of understanding him, and classify accordingly.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: What experience must I have, or imagine, to follow this point?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: If you note the sort of experience that is being referred to as a condition of understanding what is being said

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Armchair is not inferior
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Do not treat the science/philosophy contrast as invidious; both observe and think, but prove their points from different kinds of experience.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Am I judging the method fairly rather than ranking one kind above the other?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: Both have to observe and think, but they think about different sorts of observations.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Expect different argument styles
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Classify the book so you can expect the right style of argument, terms and propositions for history, science or philosophy.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: What style of argument should I expect from this kind of book?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: Their styles in arguing are different.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Read history as story
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Expect a history to be narrative and to obey the rules for telling a good story.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Is the history working as a good narrative?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: The historian must write poetically, which means he must obey the rules for telling a good story.

analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.title: Read each kind appropriately
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.action: Adjust how you read to the kind of book, just as a student responds differently to classes in history, science or philosophy.
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.check: Am I reading this book in the way its kind of teaching requires?
analytical/pigeonholing-a-book/kinds-of-.quote: if we are to follow them, we must learn to read each kind in an appropriate manner.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.title: Find the skeleton
analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.action: Read every book with X-ray eyes to find the structure hidden beneath its surface.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.check: Can I see the book's underlying structure, not just its surface?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.quote: Every book has a skeleton hidden between its covers. Your job as an analytical reader is to find it.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.title: Assume unity and organization
analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.action: Approach any book worth reading, poetry or science, assuming it has a unity and an organization of parts to be discovered.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.check: What unity and arrangement of parts does this kind of book have?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/reading-the-s.quote: But every book without exception that is worth reading at all has a unity and an organization of parts.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: State the unity
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: State the unity of the whole book in a single sentence, or at most a few sentences (a short paragraph).
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Can I tell myself or anybody else what the unity is, in a few words?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: This means that you must say what the whole book is about as briefly as possible.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Unity vs. kind
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Distinguish saying what the book is about (its theme or main point) from saying what kind of book it is.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Have I said what the author is up to, not just what kind of book it is?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: To say what the whole book is about is not the same as saying what kind of book it is.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Theme: what author is up to
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Ask what the author is up to, what he is trying to do, to discover the book’s theme or main point.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: What is the author trying to do in this book?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: To find out what a book is about in this sense is to discover its theme or main point.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Too many words means multiplicity
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Express the unity definitely and in a few words; if it takes many words, you have seen a multiplicity, not the unity.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Is my statement short enough to be one unity rather than a list?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: If it requires too many words, you have not seen the unity but a multiplicity.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Do not just feel it
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Do not be satisfied with a feeling of the unity that you cannot put into words.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Can I actually say it, or do I only 'know it but can’t say it'?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: Do not be satisfied with “feeling the unity” that you cannot express.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.mistake: Saying 'I know what it is, but I just can’t say it.'

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Reduce story to plot
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: For a story, state the essence of the plot in a few sentences, as Aristotle did for the Odyssey, and treat the rest as episode.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Have I separated the main thread of plot from the episodes?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: “This,” says Aristotle, “is the essence of the plot; the rest is episode.”

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Practice on novels
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Practise stating the unity of novels you have read, such as Tom Jones or Crime and Punishment, then place the parts.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Can I state each novel’s plot briefly enough to place the parts in it?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: You might find it a good exercise to try this with some novels you have read.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Use the author's help
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Look to the title, especially elaborate ones, and the preface or opening paragraph for the author’s own statement of the unity.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Has the author stated the book’s plan in the title, preface or first paragraph?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: You do not always have to find out the unity of a book all by yourself. The author often helps you.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Expect early self-summary
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: In expository books, expect the author to state his plan early, even in the first paragraph, since he has no reason for suspense.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Does the first paragraph or preface summarize the whole?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: Like a newspaper article, an expository book may summarize itself in its first paragraph.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Do not rely on preface
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Accept the author’s stated plan as a guide but do not rely on it completely; plans go awry.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Have I tested the author’s stated plan against the book itself?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: Do not be too proud to accept the author’s help if he proffers it, but do not rely too completely on what he says in the preface, either.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Read the whole book
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Remember that finding the unity is finally your obligation, and discharge it honestly only by reading the whole book.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Is my statement of unity based on the whole book?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: You can discharge that obligation honestly only by reading the whole book.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Elaborate the author's summary
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: After reading through, elaborate the author’s opening summary with the main figures and events, but leave out the remaining details.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Have I added the essential figures and events and omitted the rest?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: All the rest of the fascinating details, with which Herodotus richly prepares you for his climax, can be left out of your summary of the plot.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: History's unity is plot
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: State the unity of a history as a single thread of plot, as you would for fiction.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Have I stated the history’s single thread of plot?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: Note, here, that the unity of a history is a single thread of plot, very much as in fiction.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Add subordinate qualifications
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: If the author’s statement of plan misses some parts, add subordinate qualifications so your statement does justice to all of them.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Does my statement cover every major part of the book?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: except to add two subordinate qualifications to do justice to the first and third parts of the essay

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Heed introductory words
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Pay attention to the author’s introductory words, which most readers ignore as they ignore titles.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Have I actually read the introduction?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: many readers pay as little attention to the author’s introductory words as they ordinarily do to his title.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Brief, accurate, comprehensive
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Judge your statement of unity by how brief, accurate and comprehensive it is; there is no single right wording.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Is my statement brief, accurate and comprehensive?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: One statement is better than another, of course, in proportion as it is brief, accurate, and comprehensive.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.title: Not anything goes
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.action: Feel free to word the unity your own way, but check it against the book, which stays the same for every reader.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.check: Would my statement survive comparison with the text by another careful reader?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/of-plots-and-.quote: Though readers are different, the book is the same, and there can be an objective check upon the accuracy and fidelity of the statements anyone makes about it.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Set forth the major parts
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Set forth the major parts of the book, and show how they are organized into a whole by being ordered to one another and to the unity.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Can I name the major parts and show how each serves the whole?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: THE MAJOR PARTS OF THE BOOK, AND SHOW HOW THESE ARE ORGANIZED INTO A WHOLE

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Complex unity: organized many
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Know not only how the book is one but how it is many: an organized many, not a collection of separate things.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Have I shown how the parts are connected, not merely listed them?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: You must also know how it is many, not a many that consists of a lot of separate things, but an organized many.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: House, not heap of bricks
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Picture the book as a house of connected rooms, each partly independent but related functionally to the whole.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: How does each part connect with the others, like rooms by corridors?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: A good book, like a good house, is an orderly arrangement of parts.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Find the plan anyway
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Even in lesser books, try to find the plan; if the book hangs together at all, there must be one.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Have I looked for the plan even though the book is poorly made?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: if they are a complex unity to any degree and not mere collections, there must be a plan and you must find it.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Outline parts as wholes
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Do more than enumerate parts: outline each as a subordinate whole with its own unity and complexity.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Have I given each major part its own unity and subdivisions?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: It means outlining them, that is, treating the parts as if they were subordinate wholes, each with a unity and complexity of its own.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Use the outline formula
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: After stating the unity, say how many major parts there are and what each is about, then each part’s sections, then each section’s points.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Could I give the parts, their sections and the points made in each section?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: The author accomplished this plan in five major parts, of which the first part is about so and so

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Rough approximation is fine
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Be satisfied with a rough approximation of the ideal outline; good readers do this habitually without writing it all out.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Could I give an account of the structure if asked, even if not written down?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: You should be satisfied if you make a very rough approximation to what is required.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Match effort to book
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Vary how closely you outline according to the character of the book and your purpose in reading it.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Does this book and my purpose justify a close outline or only a rough one?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: The degree of approximation varies with the character of the book and your purpose in reading it.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Outline the book, not subject
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Outline only what is in the book itself, not the subject matter, and do not put in what the author did not.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Is everything in my outline actually in the book?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: Your outline is of the book itself, not the subject matter that the book is about.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: See model outlines
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: To see the rule followed near perfection, look at a great commentary such as Aquinas on Aristotle, which outlines each part and its fit.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Does my outline say how each part fits the parts before and after?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: You might look into a commentary of this sort if you want to see the rule followed as close to perfection as man can do.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Outline the Constitution
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Make your own division of the U.S. Constitution into main parts, then go further and state the parts of the parts.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Did outlining reveal things in the document I had never seen before?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: We suggest that you try your hand at making your own division of the Constitution into its main parts.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Look past chapter divisions
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Do not assume the chapter divisions give the real structure; your major parts may cut across them.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Do my major parts follow the book’s logic rather than just its chapter breaks?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: you need not follow the apparent structure of a book as indicated by its chapter divisions.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Make your own outline
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Make your own outline in order to read the book well, as the author made his in order to write it.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Is this outline mine, worked out by me, not copied from the contents page?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: the point is to make your own outline.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Use headings as guides
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Use the author’s chapter headings and sections as guides to your own activity, not as something to rely on passively.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Have I used the headings actively without following them slavishly?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: But you must use them as guides for your own activity, and not rely on them passively.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Look beneath the surface
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Look beneath the surface of the book to discover its real structure, which may contain more plan than first appears.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Have I found structure that is not obvious at first glance?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: The surface can be deceiving. You must look beneath it to discover the real structure.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Outline backs the unity
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Back up your statement of unity by outlining the parts; a unity guessed from a cursory glance is only a lucky hit.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Can I show how and why I stated the unity as I did?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: But for you, from your point of view, it would have been merely a good guess, a lucky hit.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.title: Show parts develop theme
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.action: Show how the outlined parts exemplify and develop the main theme you stated.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.check: Does each part visibly develop the main theme?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/mastering-the.quote: The requirement that you outline the parts of a book, and show how they exemplify and develop the main theme, is thus supportive of your statement of the book’s unity.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.title: Reading and writing reciprocal
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.action: Treat the rules of unity and structure as rules of writing too: the reader searches for what the writer organized.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.check: What did the author organize that I must now uncover?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.quote: Writing and reading are reciprocal, as are teaching and being taught.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.title: Uncover what author covered
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.action: Uncover the skeleton the author has covered with flesh; look for the joints and articulation of the parts.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.check: Can I detect the joints between the parts beneath the prose?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.quote: The reader tries to uncover the skeleton that the book conceals. The author starts with the skeleton and tries to cover it up.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.title: Find unity, clarity, coherence
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.action: Find the unity, and appreciate clarity and coherence by finding the distinction and order of the parts.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.check: Have I found the unity and the distinct, ordered parts?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.quote: If the writing has unity, we must find it.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.title: Detect badly made books
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.action: If, with enough skill, you cannot find a book’s unity or its parts and their relations, judge it probably a bad book whatever its reputation.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.check: Have I tried hard enough to be confident the fault is in the book?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.quote: then very likely the book is a bad one, whatever its reputation.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.title: Do not judge too quickly
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.action: Do not be too quick to blame the book, but do not always blame yourself either; most books are badly made.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.check: Have I fairly considered both my failings and the book’s?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.quote: You should not be too quick to make this judgment; perhaps the fault is in you instead of the book.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.title: Apply rules to parts
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.action: Use the unity and outline rules on any substantial, relatively independent part of an expository book as well as on the whole.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.check: Have I found the unity and parts of the section I am reading?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.quote: These two rules can also, we might add, be used in reading any substantial part of an expository book, as well as the whole.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.title: Novels need the whole
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.action: Do not claim to get the idea of a novel from part of it; its idea is in the whole.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.check: Have I read the whole novel before stating its idea?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.quote: if the novel is any good at all, the idea is in the whole and cannot be found short of reading the whole.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-reciproca.mistake: Saying you have 'read enough to get the idea' of a novel.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Find the author's problems
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Find out what the author’s problems were: the question or questions the book sets out to answer.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: What question is this book trying to answer?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: The author of a book starts with a question or a set of questions.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Formulate the questions precisely
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Whether or not the author states his questions, formulate them yourself as precisely as you can.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Have I written the questions as precisely as possible?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: it is your task as a reader to formulate the questions as precisely as you can.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Main and subordinate questions
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: State the main question the book tries to answer, and the subordinate questions if the main one is complex.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Can I state the main question and its subordinate parts?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: You should be able to state the main question that the book tries to answer, and you should be able to state the subordinate questions

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Order the questions
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Put the questions in intelligible order, deciding which are primary and which must be answered first.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Which are primary and which secondary? Which questions must be answered first, if others are to be answered later?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: Which questions must be answered first, if others are to be answered later?

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Problems help unity and outline
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Use the search for the author’s problems alongside stating the unity and outlining; it helps especially with difficult books.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Do my unity and outline make sense as answers to the author’s questions?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: following the fourth rule is a useful procedure in conjunction with obeying the other two.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Avoid intentional fallacy
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Do not try to read the author’s private mind or psychology out of the book, especially in literary works.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Am I stating the problem the book addresses, not psychoanalyzing the author?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: That is the fallacy of thinking you can discover what was in an author’s mind from the book he has written.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.mistake: Psychoanalyzing Shakespeare from the evidence of Hamlet.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Say what poet tried
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Even with a poetical work, try to say what the author was trying to do.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: What was this poem, play or novel trying to do?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: even with a poetical work, it is often extremely helpful to try to say what the author was trying to do.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Without problems, structure fails
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Find the problems, or your grasp of the main theme will be deficient and your outline chaotic, lacking the end it serves.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Do I see why the book has the unity it has?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: They will fail to see the unity of a book because they do not see why it has the unity it has

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Theoretical question list
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Detect theoretical problems by asking: does it exist, what kind is it, what causes it, its purpose, consequences, properties, relations, behavior?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Is the author asking whether something exists, what it is, why, or how it behaves?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: Does something exist? What kind of thing is it?

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Practical question list
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Detect practical problems by asking: what ends to seek, what means to choose, what to do in what order, what is right or better under conditions?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Is the author asking about ends, means, steps, or what is better?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: What ends should be sought? What means should be chosen to a given end?

analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.title: Adapt questions for literature
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.action: Adapt the theoretical and practical question lists when applying them to imaginative literature.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.check: Have I adapted the questions to fit this imaginative work?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/discovering-t.quote: The questions have to be adapted when applied to works of imaginative literature, and there too they will be useful.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: Stage one gives structure
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Treat rules 1 to 4 as one group with a single aim: knowledge of the book’s structure.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: After rules 1-4, do I know the book’s structure?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: Together, they provide the reader who applies them with a knowledge of a book’s structure.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: Inspect before analyzing
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Inspect the book well before reading it analytically, since that helps you apply the first four rules.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: Did I give the book an inspectional reading first?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: if you inspect a book well before reading it, that will help you to apply them.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: Stages are not sequential
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Do not think you must read the book once for rules 1-4 and again for the others; practised readers do all stages at once.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: Am I applying the stages together as I read?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: The practiced reader accomplishes all of these stages at once.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: What is it about?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Use rules 1-4 to answer the first basic question: what is the book about as a whole, and how is its theme developed?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: What is the book about as a whole?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: What is the book about as a whole?

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: Refine your answer later
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Expect your answer about the whole to grow more accurate as you apply the later rules.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: Have I revised my statement of the unity after interpreting the contents?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: your answer will improve in accuracy as you proceed to apply the other rules

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: Classify the book
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Classify the book according to kind and subject matter.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: Can I state the book’s kind and subject matter?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: Classify the book according to kind and subject matter.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: State the whole briefly
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: State what the whole book is about with the utmost brevity.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: Can I say what the whole book is about in a sentence or short paragraph?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: State what the whole book is about with the utmost brevity.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: Enumerate and outline parts
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Enumerate the major parts in their order and relation, and outline these parts as you outlined the whole.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: Have I listed the major parts in order and outlined each?
