analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: Enumerate its major parts in their order and relation, and outline these parts as you have outlined the whole.

analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.title: Define the problems
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.action: Define the problem or problems the author is trying to solve.
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.check: Can I state the problems the author is trying to solve?
analytical/x-raying-a-book/the-first-sta.quote: Define the problem or problems the author is trying to solve.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Terms come after outline
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Make coming to terms your first step beyond the outline; without it no knowledge passes from author to reader.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I come to terms before trying to interpret the propositions?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: But in the analytical reading of a book, coming to terms is the first step beyond the outline.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Term: unit of knowledge
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Treat the term as the basic element of communicable knowledge.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Do I know which terms carry the author’s knowledge?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: For a term is the basic element of communicable knowledge.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Term is not word
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do not mistake finding important words for coming to terms; a word can have many meanings.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Do I know the meaning, not only the word?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: A term is not a word— at least, not just a word without further qualifications.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Ambiguity blocks communication
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Resolve ambiguity: if the author uses a word in one meaning and you read it in another, no communication has occurred.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Am I reading this word in the same meaning the author uses it?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Where there is unresolved ambiguity in communication, there is no communication, or at best communication must be incomplete.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Same words, same meanings
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Use the same words with the same meanings as the author, so that a meaning, not just words, is shared.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Do the author and I share the meaning, not merely the word?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: it is necessary for the two parties to use the same words with the same meanings— in short, to come to terms.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Term: word used unambiguously
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Define a term as a word used unambiguously, in one sense at a time.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: In this passage, is the word used in one definite sense?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: What we should have said is that a term is a word used unambiguously.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Terms not in dictionaries
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do not expect to find terms in a dictionary; it supplies only materials, and terms arise in the act of communication.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I worked out the author's meaning from his usage rather than a dictionary?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: You cannot find terms in dictionaries, though the materials for making them are there.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Follow the author's usage
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Help the author avoid ambiguity by trying to follow his use of words.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Am I tracking how this author uses the word?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: They occur when a writer tries to avoid ambiguity and a reader helps him by trying to follow his use of words.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Poetry may be ambiguous
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Apply the demand for unambiguous terms to expository works; poetry and fiction may be intentionally and richly ambiguous.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Is this an expository work where ambiguity is a fault, or poetry where it may be intended?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: it has been said with justice that any good poet is sometimes intentionally ambiguous in his writing.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Find words, come to terms
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Find the important words and through them come to terms with the author.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I spotted the important words and figured out how the author uses them?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Stated roughly, it is this: You must spot the important words in a book and figure out how the author is using them.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Locate the important words
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: First, locate the important words, the ones that make a difference.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I marked the words that make a difference?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The first part is to locate the important words, the words that make a difference.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Determine meanings precisely
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Second, determine with precision the meaning of these words as the author uses them.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Can I state precisely what each important word means as used here?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The second part is to determine the meaning of these words, as used, with precision.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Grammatical and logical steps
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Take two steps in each interpretive rule: one dealing with language (grammar) and one going beyond it to thought (logic).
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I moved from the words to the thought behind them?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: these rules have a grammatical and a logical aspect.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Meet the author halfway
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do your share of the work against the barrier of language; do not expect the author to reach you alone.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Am I tunnelling through from my side, or waiting passively?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: We must meet him halfway.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Words and terms many-to-many
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Remember that one word can carry many terms and one term can be expressed by many words.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which sense of the word is used here, and which other words express the same term?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The main point is that one word can be the vehicle for many terms, and one term can be expressed by many words.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Think the word as author
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Think each important word in the same particular sense the author intends at that place.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Do I take this occurrence in sense a, b or c, as the author does?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Only when you think the word as we think it, do we have one thought between us.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Look for special uses
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Pass over words used in ordinary ways; focus on those the author uses in a special way.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Is the author using this word specially, or as anyone would?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Only those words that he uses in a special way are important for him, and for us as readers.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Ordinary words follow context
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Read most words as in ordinary conversation, trusting context to signal shifts of meaning.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Does the context make the ordinary meaning clear here?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: An author uses most words as men ordinarily do in conversation, with a range of meanings, and trusting to the context to indicate the shifts.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Beware old usage
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: In books from the past, archaic usage, or translations, take extra care to tell ordinary words of that time from special ones.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Was this word ordinary in the author's time and place?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: in reading books written in the past, it may be more difficult to detect the words the author is using as most people did
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.mistake: Assuming a word in an old or translated book carries today's ordinary meaning.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Work at the passage
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Make an effort to understand the passage in which a word occurs in order to locate the key words.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I tried to understand the whole passage around the word?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: You cannot locate the key words without making an effort to understand the passage in which they occur.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Mark words that trouble
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Mark the words that trouble you; they are likely to be the ones the author uses specially.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I marked every word that gave me trouble?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: If you mark the words that trouble you, you may hit the very ones the author is using specially.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Troubling words matter most
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Treat the words that give you trouble as the most important ones for you, while allowing they may not be the author's key words.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which words trouble me, and are they the author's key words too?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: From your point of view as a reader, therefore, the most important words are those that give you trouble.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Work where terms fail
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Spend your effort where you have not yet come to terms; key words you already understand need no more work.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Where have I failed to come to terms?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Only where you fail to come to terms have you work still to do.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Not ordinary for you
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Identify important words negatively by noticing that they are not ordinary words for you.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which words are not ordinary to me?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: You discover some of the important words by the fact that they are not ordinary for you.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Watch the author's stress
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Look for words the author explicitly stresses with quotation marks or italics, or by discussing their senses and how he will use them.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which words has the author marked, discussed or defined?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The first and most obvious sign is the explicit stress an author places upon certain words and not others.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Note defined things
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Treat words that name things the author defines as important.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which words name things the author has defined?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Or he may emphasize the word by defining the thing that the word is used to name.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Words in primary propositions
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Note words that occur in the author’s primary propositions, such as axioms; the terms composing them are basic.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which words occur in the axioms or opening principles?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: You know they are important from the fact that they occur in the axioms.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Find technical vocabulary
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Expect every field to have a technical vocabulary, and discover it yourself when the author does not set it out.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: What is this field’s technical vocabulary in this book?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: In books differently written or in other fields, the technical vocabulary must be discovered by the reader.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Use prior knowledge
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Use any prior knowledge of the subject to discern which words are technical.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: What do I already know about this field’s vocabulary?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: If the author has not pointed out the words himself, the reader may locate them through having some prior knowledge of the subject matter.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Use stage-one results
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Use what you know of the book’s kind, unity, major parts, title, chapter headings and preface to separate technical from ordinary words.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Do the title, headings and outline point to the technical words?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The rules of analyzing a book’s structure may help here.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: List the key words
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Make a list of the author’s important words, letting one technical word lead you to others.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I listed the key words, as with Smith’s labor, capital, wages, rent?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Since one technical word leads to another, you cannot help but discover other technical words in a similar fashion.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Philosophers' private vocabularies
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Expect philosophers to coin words or turn common words into technical ones, and read their warnings about it.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Is a familiar word being used here in a special philosophical sense?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Philosophers are notorious for having private vocabularies.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Familiar words made technical
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do not treat a common word as ordinary just because you think you know it; the author may have made it technical.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Am I assuming I know this word’s meaning when the author uses it specially?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: This last procedure is likely to be most misleading to the reader who supposes that he knows what the word means, and therefore treats it as an ordinary word.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.mistake: Treating a technical use of a common word as ordinary.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Note quarrels over words
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Treat any word the author argues about with other writers, explaining their usage and his own, as one that matters greatly to him.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Does the author dispute how others use this word?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: one clue to an important word is that the author quarrels with other writers about it.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Special vocabulary
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Identify the small set of words expressing the author’s main ideas and leading concepts; they carry his analysis and argument.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which few words carry the author’s main ideas?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The relatively small set of words that express an author’s main ideas, his leading concepts, constitutes his special vocabulary.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Any unclear word matters
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Treat as important for you any word whose meaning is not clear, in addition to the author’s key words.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Are there unclear words I have not yet worked on?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: in addition any other word whose meaning is not clear is important for you.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Ponder or mark words
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Make a deliberate effort to ponder, or at least mark, the words you do not understand.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I marked the words I do not fully understand?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The reader who fails to ponder, or at least to mark, the words he does not understand is headed for disaster.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Not all words ordinary
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do not read a book that can increase your understanding as if all its words were as plain as a newspaper’s.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Am I treating difficult words as if they were everyday ones?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: If you proceed as if they were all ordinary words, all on the same level of general intelligibility as the words of a newspaper article, you will make no headway

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Inattention to words
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Avoid the outstanding fault of non-active reading: inattention to words and failure to come to terms.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Am I paying attention to the words, or reading passively?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The outstanding fault of the non-active or undemanding reader is his inattention to words, and his consequent failure to come to terms with the author.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Single or shifting sense
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: For each marked word, recognize whether the author uses it in a single sense throughout or in several senses that shift.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Does this word stand for one term or several?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Either the author is using these words in a single sense throughout or he is using them in two or more senses, shifting his meaning from place to place.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: One or many meanings?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: First, try to determine whether the word has one meaning or many.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Does this word have one meaning or many in this book?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: First, try to determine whether the word has one or many meanings.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Relate the meanings
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: If the word has many meanings, try to see how they are related.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: How are the different meanings of this word related?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: If it has many, try to see how they are related.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Track the shifts
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Note where the word is used in each sense and look in the context for the reason for the shift.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Can I follow each shift in meaning as flexibly as the author does?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: note the places where the word is used in one sense or another, and see if the context gives you any clue to the reason for the shift in meaning.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Use the words you know
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Find the meaning of a word you do not understand by using the meanings of all the surrounding words you do understand.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I used the familiar words around it to fix its meaning?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: you have to discover the meaning of a word you do not understand by using the meanings of all the other words in the context that you do understand.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Build from known meanings
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Work from meanings you already possess, as when you use the familiar words of a definition to grasp the defined term.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which words in the definition or passage do I already understand?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: You operate with meanings you already possess.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: It is not all Greek
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do not give up on a book as 'all Greek'; the familiar words surrounding the strange ones give you the materials you need.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Have I tried to use the surrounding familiar words before giving up?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The surrounding words are the context for the words to be interpreted.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Work like a jigsaw
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Fit unclear words into place by trial and error, like a jigsaw, letting each word placed make the next easier.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Does each meaning I assign fit with the picture formed so far?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The process is something like the trial-and-error method of putting a jigsaw puzzle together.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Readjust after errors
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Expect to make errors and be ready to readjust a series of meanings when a later word does not fit.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Does any later word force me to readjust earlier meanings?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: The errors will get corrected because, so long as they are not found out, the picture cannot be completed.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Check your understanding
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: With experience, check yourself so you know whether you have come to terms and do not blithely think you understand.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Am I honestly sure I understand, or only assuming it?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: You will not blithely think you understand when you do not.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Ambiguous books show badness
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: When an author uses words ambiguously, recognize that you can only find out that he was not precise.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Is my difficulty due to the author's ambiguity rather than my reading?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: If the author uses words ambiguously you cannot find out what he is trying to say. You can only find out that he has not been precise.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Several senses vs. ambiguity
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do not count using a word in several senses as ambiguity if the author distinguishes and relates the senses; that is offering terms.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Has the author distinguished the senses so I can follow them?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: To use a word ambiguously is to use it in several senses without distinguishing or relating their meanings.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Two-column vocabulary list
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: List the important words in one column and their important meanings in another to see vocabulary versus terminology.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Does my list show which words map to which meanings?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: If you make a list in one column of the important words, and in another of their important meanings, you will see the relation between the vocabulary and the terminology.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Combined senses are terms
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Recognize that a word may stand for one, some, or all of its related meanings at once; it is a term if each usage is definite.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Is this usage definite, even if it combines several senses?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: So long as each usage is definite, the word so used is a term.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Spot synonyms for terms
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Recognize that authors often use different words with the same meaning, so two words may express one term.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Are these different words expressing the same term?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: here, one and the same term is represented by two or more words used synonymously.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Changed word, same term
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Do not assume a change of words means a change of terms, nor that the same word always means the same term.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Did the term change, or only the word?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: If you supposed that every time an author changed his words, he was shifting his terms, you would make as great an error

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Phrases can be terms
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Treat a unified phrase, one that can be subject or predicate of a sentence, as possibly expressing a term like a single word.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Is this phrase standing for one of the author’s terms?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: It follows, therefore, that a term can be expressed by a phrase as well as by a word.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Use phrases to clarify
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Use the author’s elaborate phrases as clarifications of his key words, since phrases are less likely to be ambiguous.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Which phrases does the author substitute to make a key word’s meaning sure?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: In general, a phrase is less likely to be ambiguous than a word.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Pursue grammar and logic
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: As practice raises questions, study literal and metaphorical use, abstract and concrete words, definition and emotive language in books on these subjects.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: What questions about words has my reading raised that further study could answer?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: You will want to know something about the literal and metaphorical use of words.

analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.title: Make it a habit
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.action: Make a habit of finding the important words, identifying their shifting meanings, and coming to terms.
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.check: Did I find the key words and their meanings in this reading?
analytical/coming-to-terms-with-an-autho.quote: Seldom does such a small change in a habit have such a large effect.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Proposition: author's judgment
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Treat a proposition as the author’s declaration of knowledge: what he affirms as true or denies as false.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: What is the author affirming or denying here?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: It is an expression of the author’s judgment about something.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Check promises against propositions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Look for the author’s propositions to find out whether he keeps the promises made in his preface.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do the propositions deliver what the preface promised?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: To find out whether he keeps those promises, we must look for his propositions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Terms before propositions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Come to terms with the author first, before trying to find what judgment he is declaring.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I come to terms before interpreting this proposition?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: But the reader must usually come to terms with an author first, before he can find out what the author is proposing

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Seek the reasons
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Do not be satisfied with the author’s opinions; find out why he thinks you should accept them.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: What reasons does the author give for this proposition?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: His propositions are nothing but expressions of personal opinion unless they are supported by reasons.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Watch argument signal words
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Look for words like 'because', 'if... then', 'since... therefore', 'it follows that', which signal an argument.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Where do 'because', 'therefore' or 'it follows' link statements here?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The word “because” here signifies a reason being given.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: What an argument is
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Treat an argument as a set of statements, some giving grounds for a conclusion, requiring at least a collection of sentences.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Which statements are the grounds and which the conclusion?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: An argument is always a set or series of statements of which some provide the grounds or reasons for what is to be concluded.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Valid is not true
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Remember that a valid conclusion follows from premises but may still be false if a premise is false.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does the conclusion follow, and are the premises themselves true?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: That does not necessarily mean that the conclusion is true, since one or all of the premises that support it may be false.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Attend to all units
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Attend to sentences and paragraphs as well as words, building from terms to propositions to arguments.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Am I reading the sentences and paragraphs as units, not just words?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The active reader is attentive not only to the words but also to the sentences and paragraphs.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Outline meets interpretation
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Work down by outlining to the points made in each part and up from terms to propositions and arguments until they meet.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do the points in my outline match the propositions and arguments I found?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Thus, the two processes, outlining and interpretation, meet at the level of propositions and arguments.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Grammatical vs. logical units
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Distinguish sentences and paragraphs (units of language) from propositions and arguments (units of thought).
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Am I dealing with the sentence or with the proposition it expresses?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Sentences and paragraphs are grammatical units. They are units of language. Propositions and arguments are logical units, or units of thought and knowledge.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: No one-to-one relation
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Never assume a one-to-one relation between language elements and elements of thought.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I assumed each sentence is exactly one proposition?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The greatest error you can make in applying these rules is to suppose that a one-to-one relationship exists between the elements of language and those of thought or knowledge.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Skip questions and wishes
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Recognize that questions and sentences expressing wishes or intentions do not express propositions, though they may reveal purpose.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is this sentence declarative, or a question or wish?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Not every sentence in a book expresses a proposition.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Propositions answer questions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Treat propositions as answers to questions, expressed in declarative sentences.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: What question does this proposition answer?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Propositions are the answers to questions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Same sentence, different propositions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Watch for the same sentence expressing different propositions when its words shift terms.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do the words in this repeated sentence carry the same terms each time?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: it is possible for the same sentence to express different propositions if there is a shift in the terms the words express.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Compound sentences, several propositions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Expect a compound sentence, joined by 'and', 'if... then', 'not only... but also', to express two or more propositions, perhaps an argument.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: How many propositions does this compound sentence contain?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: But even when its words are used unambiguously, a compound sentence expresses two or more propositions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Separate before judging
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Distinguish the propositions in a complex sentence so you can agree with some and disagree with others.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I separated each claim so I can judge them one by one?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Unless you recognize the distinct propositions in a complicated sentence, you cannot make a discriminating judgment on what the writer is saying.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Simple sentences hide claims
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Examine even simple sentences, as lawyers do, for several separate claims that may be true or false independently.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does this simple sentence assert more than one thing?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: In short, even a grammatically simple sentence sometimes expresses two or more propositions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Different sentences, same proposition
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Recognize when two different sentences express one and the same proposition.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Are these two sentences saying the same thing?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: one and the same proposition can also be expressed by two or more different sentences.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Know some grammar
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Attend to the order and relation of words in sentences, since some grammar is needed to get beneath language to thought.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do I understand how the words in this sentence relate grammatically?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Some knowledge of grammar is indispensable to a reader.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Different for poetical works
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Apply the rules about propositions and arguments primarily to expository works; they change for novels, plays and poems.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is this an expository work, or must I adapt the rule?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The rules about propositions and arguments are quite different when you are reading a poetical work—a novel, play, or poem.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Mark key sentences, find propositions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Mark the most important sentences in a book and discover the propositions they contain.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I marked the leading sentences and stated their propositions?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Grasp the author’s leading propositions by dealing with his most important sentences.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Understand every sentence
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Understand every sentence, but expect most to cause no difficulty and read them relatively quickly.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Did I understand the ordinary sentences while saving effort for the hard ones?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Obviously, you have to understand every sentence.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Find sentences needing effort
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Treat as important for you the sentences that need an effort of interpretation, those you understand just well enough to know there is more.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Which sentences do I understand only partly?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: From your point of view as a reader, the sentences important for you are those that require an effort of interpretation because, at first sight, they are not perfectly intelligible.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Read them slowly
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Read the difficult, important sentences much more slowly and carefully than the rest.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I slowed down on the sentences that matter?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: They are the sentences that you read much more slowly and carefully than the rest.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Find judgments argument rests on
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Find the sentences expressing the judgments on which the author’s whole argument rests: his major affirmations, denials and reasons.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Which sentences carry the author's main affirmations and denials?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: From the author’s point of view, the important sentences are the ones that express the judgments on which his whole argument rests.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Raise them in relief
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Separate the main sentences from surrounding discussion, history of views and comment, seeing them as if raised from the page.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I distinguished the core claims from supporting discussion?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: To come to grips, therefore, you have to see the main sentences as if they were raised from the page in high relief.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Heed author's signals
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Stop and examine sentences the author flags as important or makes stand out typographically.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Did I stop at sentences the author marked as important?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: They either tell you that this is an important point when they make it, or they use one or another typographical device to make their leading sentences stand out.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.mistake: Reading on past clearly marked important sentences.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Use format cues
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Use formats that put leading sentences in relief, like Euclid’s labelled propositions or Aquinas’s 'I answer that'.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does the book’s format mark its conclusions and reasons?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The place where Aquinas begins to argue his own point is marked by the words, “I answer that.”

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Not everything equally important
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Do not treat everything you read as equally important and read it all at one speed.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Am I varying my attention according to importance?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: it remains all a blur for those readers who treat everything they read as equally important

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Be perplexed, know it
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Be sensitive to passages you cannot readily understand; being perplexed and knowing it locates the sentences that carry the meaning.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Where am I perplexed, and have I noticed it?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Perhaps you are beginning to see how essential a part of reading it is to be perplexed and know it.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Ask about meaning
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Ask yourself questions about the meaning of passages, or the book cannot give you any new insight.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: What question do I have about this passage’s meaning?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: If you never ask yourself any questions about the meaning of a passage, you cannot expect the book to give you any insight you do not already possess.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Key words point to sentences
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Let the important words you have marked lead you to the sentences that deserve attention.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Which sentences contain my marked key words?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: If you have already marked the important words, they should lead you to the sentences that deserve further attention.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Rules order is flexible
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Feel free to work from a puzzling sentence back to its key words; terms and propositions illuminate each other.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Has a puzzling sentence shown me words I should mark?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The fact that we have stated these rules in a fixed order does not mean that you have to follow them in that order.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Look for premises, conclusions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Recognize principal propositions as premises or conclusions of the main argument.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is this sentence a premise or conclusion of the main argument?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: They must be either premises or conclusions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Find sentence sequences
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Detect sentences that form a sequence with a beginning and an end; they are probably the important ones.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do these sentences form a sequence moving toward a conclusion?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: if you can detect those sentences that seem to form a sequence, a sequence in which there is a beginning and an end

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Follow argument's movement
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Follow an argument as a movement of thought, whether it starts with the conclusion and gives reasons or starts with evidence.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Where does this argument begin, and where does it get to?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: An argument begins somewhere, goes somewhere, gets somewhere.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Keep your mind awake
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Keep your mind awake while reading so that your natural sensitivity to arguments can work.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Am I alert enough to notice an argument when I see one?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: But the eye will not see if it is not kept open, and the mind will not follow an argument if it is not awake.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Pause on puzzles, not interests
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Slow down over the sentences that puzzle you, not merely those that interest you.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Am I pausing at what puzzles me or only at what interests me?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: They pause over the sentences that interest them rather than the ones that puzzle them.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.mistake: Going slow over interesting sentences instead of puzzling ones.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Seek ideas, not curiosities
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: In old books, do not confuse surprising facts or interest in the author and his world with understanding his ideas.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Am I attending to the author's ideas or to curiosities?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: But when you are reading for understanding it is not that kind of novelty that you are seeking.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Know what it means
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: For each leading sentence, discover the proposition or propositions it contains, that is, what the sentence means.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I say what this sentence means?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: This is just another way of saying that you must know what the sentence means.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Interpret the principal words
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Interpret all the words in the sentence, especially its principal words, as you did to find terms.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do I know the terms the principal words express?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: You discover propositions similarly by interpreting all the words that make up the sentence, and especially its principal words.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Dissect the sentence
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Use grammar to dissect the sentence: roles of modifiers, verbs and nouns, and how clauses restrict or amplify meanings.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: How do the clauses and modifiers restrict or extend the meaning?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Ideally, you should be able to dissect a sentence according to the rules of syntax, although you do not necessarily have to do it in a formal way.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Use surrounding sentences
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Bring all the surrounding sentences to bear on the sentence in question, moving from what you understand to what you do not.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I used the neighbouring sentences to interpret this one?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: You bring all the surrounding sentences to bear on the sentence in question, just as you used the surrounding words to interpret a particular word.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Separate all propositions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Separate out of each complicated important sentence all its different, though related, propositions.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I listed every distinct proposition in this sentence?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: You have not completed your interpretation of an important sentence until you have separated out of it all the different, though perhaps related, propositions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Number and relate assertions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Take complicated sentences and state in your own words each thing asserted; number them and relate them.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I numbered each assertion and shown how they relate?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Take some of the complicated sentences in this book and try to state in your own words each of the things that is being asserted.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: State it in own words
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Test your grasp by restating the proposition in totally different words, not the author’s words reshuffled.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I say the same thing in totally different words?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Ideally, you should be able to say the same thing in totally different words.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.mistake: Repeating the author's words with minor changes in order.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Words passed, not thought
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: If you cannot get away from the author’s words, suspect that only words, not knowledge, have passed to you.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do I know his mind, or only his words?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: You know his words, not his mind.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Translate within English
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Translate the author's English sentence into another English sentence faithful to the thought alone, as the best self-test.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I digested the proposition or only swallowed the words?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: if you want to be sure you have digested the proposition, not merely swallowed the words.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Recognize equivalent statements
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Recognize when the author states the same proposition in different words, and be able to offer an equivalent statement yourself.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I tell when two sentences state the same proposition?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The reader who has not seen through the words to the proposition they convey is likely to treat the equivalent sentences as if they were statements of different propositions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Compare authors through language
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: When comparing authors, see through their language: they may say the same thing differently or different things alike.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is this a real disagreement or only a verbal one?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Different authors frequently say the same thing in different words, or different things using almost the same words.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.mistake: Misreading authors as disagreeing, or missing real differences, because of wording.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Can you give an example?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Test your understanding by pointing to an experience the proposition describes or a particular instance of it.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can you exemplify the general truth that has been enunciated by referring to a particular instance of it?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Can you exemplify the general truth that has been enunciated by referring to a particular instance of it?

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Imagine a possible case
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: If you have no actual example, imagine a possible case; if you can do neither, suspect you do not understand.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I imagine even one possible case the proposition fits?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: To imagine a possible case is often as good as citing an actual one.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Some need special experience
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Accept that some scientific propositions can only be exemplified with special laboratory experience.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does this proposition need special experience to exemplify?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: It may be necessary to have the special experience that only a laboratory can afford to be sure you have grasped certain scientific propositions.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Relate to the world
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Connect every proposition to actual or possible facts it refers to, or you are playing with words.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: What facts in the world does this proposition refer to?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Propositions do not exist in a vacuum. They refer to the world in which we live.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Translate, then exemplify
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Apply both tests in order: restate the proposition in other words, then give an example of it.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I both restate and exemplify the proposition?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Failing to get a translation, we would then ask for an exemplification of the proposition.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Avoid verbalism
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Avoid verbalism: using words without regard to the thoughts they convey or the experiences they refer to.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Could I do more than recite the words?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The vice of “verbalism” can be defined as the bad habit of using words without regard for the thoughts they should convey
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.mistake: Reciting an author's words from verbal memory as if that were understanding.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Locate or construct arguments
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Locate or construct the basic arguments in the book by finding them in the connection of sentences.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I state the book's basic arguments as sequences of propositions?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: OR CONSTRUCT THE BASIC ARGUMENTS IN THE BOOK BY FINDING THEM IN THE CONNECTION OF SENTENCES

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Paragraphs are not arguments
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Do not assume paragraphs correspond to arguments; writers follow no settled convention in building paragraphs.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does this argument fit within one paragraph, part of one, or several?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: there are no settled conventions among writers about how to construct paragraphs.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Arguments cross writing units
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Look for an argument in a single sentence, part of a paragraph, one paragraph, or across several paragraphs.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Where does this argument begin and end in the text?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: This logical unit is not uniquely related to any recognizable unit of writing, as terms are related to words and phrases, and propositions to sentences.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Read non-argument paragraphs quickly
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Read quickly the paragraphs that only detail evidence, report how it was gathered, or digress.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is this paragraph part of an argument, or evidence and side remarks?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: It hardly needs to be said that they should be read rather quickly.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Construct arguments from sentences
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Find the paragraphs that state important arguments; if none, construct them by gathering sentences from different paragraphs into sequence.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I gathered the sentences, from wherever they are, that compose the argument?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: IF YOU CAN THE PARAGRAPHS IN A BOOK THAT STATE ITS IMPORTANT ARGUMENTS

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Write out the argument
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Write out on paper the propositions that together form an argument.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I write the argument's propositions in order?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: You can do it by actually writing out on a piece of paper the propositions that together form an argument.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Number sentences in margin
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Put numbers and other marks in the margin to show which sentences should be tied together in a sequence.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do my margin numbers trace the argument's sequence?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: is to put numbers in the margin, together with other marks

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Search the whole chapter
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: In loosely constructed books, search through all the paragraphs of a chapter to find the sentences that make one argument.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I searched the whole chapter for this argument's pieces?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: You often have to search through all the paragraphs of a chapter to find the sentences you can construct into a statement of a single argument.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Use the author's summaries
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Use the author’s summaries at the ends of chapters or sections, looking back over the pages to find the materials summarized.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I trace each point in the summary back to the text?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: you should be able to look back over the preceding pages and find the materials he has brought together in the summary.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Locate summaries by inspection
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Inspect the book before analytical reading so you know whether summary passages exist and where they are.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do I know where the book's summary passages are?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: if you have inspected the book well before beginning to read it analytically, you will know whether the summary passages exist and if they do, where they are.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Make every step explicit
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Make every step of an argument explicit, supplying omitted propositions, since omissions can mislead.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I spelled out any steps the author left unsaid?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: it is nevertheless a sound maxim of careful reading to make every step in an argument explicit.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.mistake: Missing unstated premises, the propagandist's trick of leaving challengeable things unsaid.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Put it in a nutshell
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Know each argument in the book well enough to put it into a nutshell.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I state this argument in a nutshell?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: If the book contains arguments, you must know what they are, and be able to put them into a nutshell.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Find single arguments
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Find the single arguments, the units of reasoning; then the larger chains built on them will not be missed.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I identified each single argument within the larger chain?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The units of reasoning, however, are single arguments.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: No logician required
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Do not hold back for lack of formal logic; if your mind works while reading and reaches terms and propositions, it will see arguments.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I come to terms and found propositions, so the arguments appear?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: No great logical competence is needed to read these books.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Conclusion, then reasons
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: If you find the conclusion first, look for the reasons; if you find the reasons first, see where they lead.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I matched each conclusion with its reasons?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: If you find the conclusion first, then look for the reasons. If you find the reasons first, see where they lead.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Facts vs. general statements
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Discriminate arguments from particular facts to a generalization (inductive) from those using general statements to prove generalizations (deductive).
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does this argument rest on particular facts or on general statements?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: What is important is the ability to discriminate between the two.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Reasoning vs. experiment
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: In science, note whether a proposition is proved by reasoning, established by experiment, or both.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is this conclusion demonstrated by reasoning, by experiment, or both?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: this distinction is observed whenever the difference is emphasized between the proof of a proposition by reasoning and its establishment by experiment.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Assumed, proved, self-evident
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Observe what the author says he must assume, what he says can be proved or evidenced, and what he treats as self-evident.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Which propositions are assumptions, which proved, which self-evident?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: observe what things the author says he must assume, what he says can be proved or otherwise evidenced, and what need not be proved because it is self-evident.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Find unstated assumptions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Find the author's assumptions yourself when he does not list them; not everything can be proved.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: What unstated assumptions does this argument start from?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Obviously, not everything can be proved, just as not everything can be defined.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Two starting points
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Identify whether a line of argument starts from assumptions agreed between writer and reader or from self-evident propositions.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does this argument start from agreed assumptions or self-evident truths?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: with assumptions agreed on between writer and reader, or with what are called self-evident propositions, which neither the writer nor reader can deny.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Tautology vs. self-evident truth
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Distinguish tautologies, true merely by definition of words, from self-evident truths about how things are.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is this proposition true only by verbal definition, or does it express understanding of things?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The former statement is a tautology; the proposition is contained in the definition of the words

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Self-evident: opposite obviously false
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Treat a proposition as self-evident when its opposite is immediately seen to be false.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Is the opposite of this proposition immediately seen to be false?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: The statement is axiomatic or self-evident in the sense that its opposite is immediately seen to be false.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Self-evident can instruct
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Do not dismiss all self-evident propositions as empty tautologies; some add to our knowledge.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Does this 'tautology' actually teach me something about things?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: They do not see that some of the propositions they call “tautologies” really add to our knowledge, while others, of course, do not.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Find the author's solutions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Find out what the author’s solutions are, checking which of his problems he solved.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Which of the problems that the author tried to solve did he succeed in solving?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Which of the problems that the author tried to solve did he succeed in solving?

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Did he raise new problems?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Ask whether, in solving his problems, the author raised any new ones.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: In the course of solving these, did he raise any new ones?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: In the course of solving these, did he raise any new ones?

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Did he know he failed?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Of the problems the author failed to solve, old or new, decide which he himself knew he had failed on.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Of the problems that he failed to solve, old or new, which did the author himself know he had failed on?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Of the problems that he failed to solve, old or new, which did the author himself know he had failed on?

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Check against stated problems
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: After grasping terms, propositions and arguments, check them against the problems you identified under Rule 4.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Do my findings answer the problems I identified earlier?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: it ties together the first stage of analytical reading (outlining the structure) and the second stage (interpreting the contents).

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Follow before arguing
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Keep following the author with mind open and mouth shut until you understand; only then argue with him.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I fully understood before starting to criticize?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Up to this point, you have been following the author.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: What is said, how?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Use rules 5 to 8 to answer the second basic question: what is being said in detail, and how?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: What is being said in detail, and how?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: What is being said in detail, and how?

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Interpret key words
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Come to terms with the author by interpreting his key words.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I interpreted the author's key words?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Come to terms with the author by interpreting his key words.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Grasp leading propositions
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Grasp the author’s leading propositions by dealing with his most important sentences.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I grasped the leading propositions?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Grasp the author’s leading propositions by dealing with his most important sentences.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Know the arguments
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Know the author’s arguments by finding them in, or constructing them out of, sequences of sentences.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Can I state each argument from its sequence of sentences?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Know the author’s arguments, by finding them in, or constructing them out of, sequences of sentences.

analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.title: Solved and unsolved problems
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.action: Determine which problems the author solved and which not, and of the latter, which he knew he failed to solve.
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.check: Have I sorted the problems into solved, unsolved, and knowingly unsolved?
analytical/determining-an-authors-messag.quote: Determine which of his problems the author has solved, and which he has not; and as to the latter, decide which the author knew he had failed to solve.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.title: Talk back to the author
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.action: Treat reading as a conversation: once the author has had his say, take your turn and respond to him.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.check: Have I actually answered the author, or did I only listen?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.quote: As a matter of fact, the reader is the one who has the last word.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.title: Observe intellectual etiquette
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.action: Talk back with intellectual etiquette, so the exchange is profitable communication rather than bickering.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.check: Is my response to the book a disciplined exchange or just bickering?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.quote: Without it, conversation is bickering rather than profitable communication.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.title: Give a considered judgment
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.action: Respect the author's effort to teach by giving a considered judgment; if you cannot agree, have grounds for disagreeing or suspending judgment.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.check: If I don't agree, can I state my grounds for disagreeing or suspending judgment?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.quote: The reader owes him a considered judgment.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.title: Finish with judging
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.action: Do not stop at understanding what the book says; complete your active reading with the work of criticism.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.check: After understanding the book, did I go on to judge it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.quote: It must be completed by the work of criticism, the work of judging.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.title: Don't dismiss by forgetting
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.action: Do not dismiss a book by putting it aside and forgetting it; give it critical consideration.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.check: Did I give this book any critical consideration before shelving it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.quote: Worse than faintly praising it, he damns it by giving it no critical consideration whatever.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/rea.mistake: Putting the book aside and forgetting it, with no judgment at all.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Talking back is stage three
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Recognize talking back as the third stage of analytical reading, governed by maxims of etiquette and criteria for criticism.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Do I know which rules govern the critical stage of reading?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: It is the third stage in the analytical reading of a book; and there are rules here as in the case of the first two stages.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Weigh and consider
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Read neither to contradict nor to believe blindly nor to find talk, but to weigh and consider what is said.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Am I weighing the book, or reading to refute it or swallow it whole?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: Read not to contradict and confute; nor to believe and take for granted; nor to find talk and discourse; but to weigh and consider.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: No book is above criticism
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Do not treat a good book as above your criticism; look for its faults once you understand it.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Am I holding back judgment only out of false piety toward the author?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: It is more certain that there is no book so good that no fault can be found with it.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.mistake: False piety: assuming a great book cannot be criticized by an ordinary reader.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Understand a superior book first
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Do not criticize a book that can enlighten you until you understand it.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Do I understand this book well enough to have earned the right to judge it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: should not be criticized by them until they understand it.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Act as the author's peer
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Once you understand the book, exercise your critical faculties and talk back as the author's peer; otherwise you do him an injustice.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Having understood, have I actually engaged the author as an equal?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: Unless they exercise their critical faculties now, they are doing the author an injustice.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Teachability is active
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Treat teachability as an active virtue, not as being passive and pliable before the author.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Am I being taught, or merely pliable and subservient?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: Teachability is often confused with subservience.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.mistake: Confusing teachability with passivity and subservience.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Make up your own mind
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Exercise your independent judgment and make the greatest effort to make up your own mind on the matters the author discusses.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Have I reached my own position on the author's questions?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: The most teachable reader is, therefore, the most critical.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Hear the teacher fully
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Let the author be fully heard and understood before you judge him.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Have I heard the whole book out and understood it before judging?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: teachability requires that a teacher be fully heard and, more than that, understood before he is judged.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.title: Effort is not enough
