analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.action: Learn how to judge a book, as you learned how to understand it; sheer effort does not make you a good critic.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.check: Am I applying the rules for judging, or just trying hard?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/tea.quote: sheer amount of effort is not an adequate criterion of teachability.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Reader's rhetorical skill
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Develop the reader's rhetorical skill: knowing how to react to anyone who tries to convince or persuade you.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Do I know how to respond to the author's attempt to convince or persuade me?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: rhetorical skill is knowing how to react to anyone who tries to convince or persuade us.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Convince vs persuade
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Distinguish whether the author is trying to convince you about theoretical matters or persuade you about action or feeling.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Is the author trying to convince me of a truth or persuade me to act or feel?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: to convince about theoretical matters and to persuade about matters that ultimately affect action or feeling.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Be a responsive reader
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Be responsive: follow what the author says and note the intention that prompts it.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Can I say what the author said and why he said it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: You are responsive to the extent that you follow what has been said and note the intention that prompts it.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Take your own position
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Be responsible as well as responsive: take a position on what the author says, one that is yours.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: What is my own position on the author's claims?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: But you also have the responsibility of taking a position.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Own your judgment
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Hold yourself, not the author or anyone else, responsible for your judgment.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Is this judgment mine, or am I borrowing someone else's?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: To regard anyone except yourself as responsible for your judgment is to be a slave, not a free man.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.mistake: Letting the author or an authority decide for you.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Understanding precedes reaction
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Use your grammatical and logical skill to understand what is said as the preparation for your critical reaction.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Is my critical reaction built on a grammatical and logical understanding of the text?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: grammatical and logical skill, which enables us to understand what is being said, prepares the way for a critical reaction.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Three arts, three stages
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Recognize that the first two stages rest on grammar and logic, and the third stage on rhetoric.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Which art am I using at this stage of reading?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: Skill in the third stage depends on the remaining art.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Understand before you judge
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Do not begin to talk back until you have listened carefully and are sure you understand the book.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Can I say, with reasonable certainty, “I understand,” before I say I agree, disagree, or suspend judgment?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: Do not begin to talk back until you have listened carefully and are sure you understand.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.mistake: Criticizing a book before completing the outline and interpretation.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Earned right, and duty
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Once you are honestly satisfied that you have done the first two stages, criticize: it is now your duty as well as your right.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Having understood, have I gone on to criticize?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: When you have, you not only have earned the right to turn critic; you also have the duty to do so.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Criticism comes last
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Always do the third stage after the first two in time, even though the first two stages can be combined.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Did I finish outlining and interpreting before starting to criticize?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: the third stage of analytical reading must always follow the other two in time.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Agree, disagree, suspend
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Choose one of the three critical positions open to you: agree, disagree, or suspend judgment.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Which of the three positions am I taking, and do I understand enough to take it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: These three remarks exhaust all the critical positions you can take.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Criticizing isn't only disagreeing
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Do not equate criticism with disagreement; agreeing is just as much a critical judgment, and can be just as wrong.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Have I treated agreement as a judgment that needs as much care as disagreement?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: We hope you have not made the error of supposing that to criticize is always to disagree.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.mistake: Thinking that to criticize is always to disagree.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: No judgment without understanding
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Neither agree nor disagree with what you do not understand.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Could I state, in my own words, the position I'm agreeing or disagreeing with?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: To agree without understanding is inane. To disagree without understanding is impudent.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Suspending judgment is criticism
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Treat suspending judgment as a critical position: you are saying the case has not been shown either way.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: When I suspend judgment, do I know what has not been shown?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: It is taking the position that something has not been shown.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Restate the position
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Test understanding by restating the author's position in your own words; criticism by someone who cannot do so is irrelevant.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Can I repeat what the author said in my own words, satisfactorily?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: if they cannot repeat what you have said in their own words, you know that they do not understand

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Hesitate before “I understand”
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: With a good book, hesitate before saying you understand; expect much work first and judge yourself strictly.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Have I done enough work to declare honestly and with assurance that I understand?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: If you are reading a good book, you ought to hesitate before you say, “I understand.”

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Concede your own fault
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: When you say you don't understand, concede it may be your fault, since the presumption favors a good book.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Have I tried my hardest before blaming the book for being unintelligible?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: When you say “I don’t understand,” watch your tone of voice.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.mistake: Blaming a good book for your own failure to understand.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Part of a book
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: If you have read only part of a book, be more hesitant to criticize.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Have I read the whole book, or only part of it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: If you are reading only part of a book, it is more difficult to be sure that you understand, and hence you should be more hesitant to criticize.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Author's other works
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: When a book depends on the author's other books, be slower to claim understanding or to criticize it.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Does this book rely on other works by the same author that I haven't read?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: you should be more circumspect about saying “I understand,” and slower to raise your critical lance.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.mistake: Judging Kant's first Critique without his second, or Aristotle's Poetics alone.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Disagree reasonably
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: When you disagree, do so reasonably, not disputatiously or contentiously.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Am I disagreeing to find the truth, or to win the argument?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: There is no point in winning an argument if you know or suspect you are wrong.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.mistake: Treating the conversation with the book as a battle to win.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Honor truth first
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Put the truth ahead of winning and ahead of loyalty to persons or positions dear to you.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Would I give up a cherished view if the truth required it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: piety requires us to honor truth above our friends.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Concede to truth
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: When you cannot refute the author, acknowledge that it is the truth you cannot refute.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: When I can't answer the author, do I admit that he may simply be right?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: Say rather, Agathon, that you cannot refute the truth; for Socrates is easily refuted.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Don't hunt for quarrels
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Do not read a book only to find something you can disagree with.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Am I reading to learn, or searching for a bone to pick?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: The reader who approaches a book in this spirit reads it only to find something he can disagree with.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: No empty victories
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Do not seek the empty satisfaction of seeming to show up an author who cannot defend himself.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Am I scoring points against an absent author rather than learning?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: If all he wants is the empty satisfaction of seeming to show the author up, the reader can get it readily.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Win by gaining knowledge
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Measure the profit of your reading by what you learn, not by knocking the author down.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: What have I learned from this author?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: you win only by gaining knowledge, not by knocking the other fellow down

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Be ready to agree
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Be as prepared to agree as to disagree, and let only the facts and the truth decide which.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Is my verdict driven by the facts, or by a wish to agree or disagree?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: he should be as prepared to agree as to disagree.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.title: Agreeing is not losing
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.action: Admit a point when you see it, and do not feel beaten when you must agree with the author.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.check: Do I feel defeated when I have to agree? If so, is my problem emotional?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.quote: But he also should not feel whipped by having to agree with an author, instead of dissenting.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/the.mistake: Feeling defeated by agreement: an emotional, not intellectual, problem.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Disagreements can be resolved
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Regard disagreements as capable of being resolved, and disagree in the hope of resolving the issue.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Am I disagreeing with the hope of reaching agreement?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: It recommends that you regard disagreements as capable of being resolved.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Don't disagree hopelessly
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Do not disagree hopelessly; remember that all rational men can agree, even when they do not.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Do I believe this disagreement could, in principle, be settled?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: this one warns you against disagreeing hopelessly.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Apparent disagreement
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Identify disagreements that come only from misunderstanding, and cure them by coming to terms.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Is this disagreement real, or does it come from misunderstanding?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: The sort of disagreement that is only apparent, the sort that results from misunderstanding, is certainly curable.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Disagreement from ignorance
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Recognize disagreements caused by inequality of knowledge, which instruction can cure.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Could this disagreement come from what one of us does not know?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: Inequality of knowledge is always curable by instruction.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Be open to change
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Be as prepared to have your own mind changed as to change the author's.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Am I willing to be changed by this book as much as to correct it?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: He should be as much prepared to have his own mind changed as seek to change the mind of another.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Disagreement teaches you too
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Keep in mind that you may misunderstand or be ignorant; treat disagreement as an occasion for being taught.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Have I considered that I may be the one who misunderstands or is ignorant?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: No one who looks upon disagreement as an occasion for teaching another should forget that it is also an occasion for being taught.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Not just a matter of opinion
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Do not treat every question as a matter of private opinion that discussion cannot settle.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Am I hiding behind “it's just my opinion” where knowledge is at stake?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: They think that everything is just a matter of opinion.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.mistake: Treating conversation as a ping-pong game of opinions where nobody learns.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Be patient for the long run
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Be patient: real issues of knowledge can be resolved, in the long run, by appeals to fact and reason.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Am I expecting an instant resolution instead of working by fact and reason?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: The maxim of rationality concerning disagreements is to be patient for the long run.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: First rule out misunderstanding
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: When you disagree with the book, first make sure the disagreement is not owing to misunderstanding.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Have I confirmed that I really understood the point I disagree with?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: It requires him first to be sure that the disagreement is not owing to misunderstanding.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Knowledge vs opinion
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Distinguish genuine knowledge from mere opinion, and treat an issue of knowledge as one that can be resolved.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Is the point at issue a matter of knowledge or mere opinion?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: This maxim then requires him to distinguish between genuine knowledge and mere opinion

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Judge the book, not the man
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Treat unreasoned assertions as the author's personal opinions, and judge the book's reasoned claims rather than the author's personality.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Am I judging the book's reasoned statements or merely the author as a person?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: He does not judge the book but the man.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Give reasons for judgments
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Respect the difference between knowledge and mere personal opinion by giving reasons for any critical judgment you make.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Can I give my own grounds for this disagreement?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: But when he disagrees, he must give his own grounds for doing so.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.mistake: Treating a matter of knowledge as if it were opinion.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Share the reasons you accept
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: When you agree, actively share the author's reasons for the point on which you agree.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Do I agree for the author's reasons, and can I state them?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: it suffices if he actively shares the author’s reasons for the point on which they agree.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Opinion is unsupported judgment
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Count as knowledge only opinions you can defend with evidence; treat unsupported judgments as mere opinion.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: What evidence would other reasonable people accept for my judgment?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: Opinion, in the sense in which we have been employing the word, is unsupported judgment.

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Knowledge is correctable
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Hold your knowledge subject to correction by new evidence, while still distinguishing it from opinion.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Is my claim supported by the weight of the evidence, and open to correction?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: What we know, we know subject to correction

analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.title: Define the issue
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.action: Give reasons for your disagreements so that the issues are not merely stated but defined.
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.check: Have my reasons defined the issue clearly enough for it to be resolved?
analytical/criticizing-a-book-fairly/on-.quote: It also commands him to give reasons for his disagreements so that issues are not merely stated but also defined.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Not understood? Go back
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: If you do not understand, say nothing critical and go back to work on the book.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Can I honestly say I understand? If not, have I gone back to the book?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: If he does not understand, he should keep his peace and go back to work on the book.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Support “I don't understand”
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: To make “I don't understand” a criticism, locate the sources of trouble in the book itself.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Can I show disorderly structure, parts that don't hang together, irrelevance, or equivocation in key words?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: If the fault is with the book rather than himself, the reader must locate the sources of trouble.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Full agreement ends the work
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: If you understand and agree thoroughly, consider the analytical reading done; further steps apply only to disagreement or suspended judgment.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Do I fully agree, or are there points where I disagree or suspend judgment?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: If, in addition to understanding the book, you agree thoroughly with what the author says, the work is over.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Meet the arguments
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Do not merely follow the author's arguments; meet them, using the principles of civil, intelligent controversy.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I engaged the arguments themselves, not just traced them?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Not simply by following an authors arguments, but only by meeting them as well, can the reader ultimately reach significant agreement or disagreement with his author.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Two senses of agreement
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Distinguish agreement about the use of words (understanding) from agreement about the facts (judgment).
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Is my agreement about what the author means, or about whether he is right?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: they fail to distinguish between two senses of “agreement.”
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.mistake: Thinking all disagreement is merely misunderstanding.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Find the real issue
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Make sure you share a common understanding of the author's words before you treat a disagreement as a real issue.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Do we agree about the meaning of the words, so that the issue is real?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Agreement about the use of words is the indispensable condition for genuine agreement or disagreement about the facts being discussed.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Misread means irrelevant
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Discard any disagreement that rests on a misapprehension of the author's meaning.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Did I take the author's words in the sense he meant?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Because we misapprehended your meaning, our disagreement was irrelevant.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Disagree on showable grounds
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Disagree only because you think the author can be shown wrong on some point, not to voice prejudice or emotion.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Can I show where the author is wrong, or am I only reacting?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: You are not simply voicing your prejudice or expressing your emotions.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Acknowledge your emotions
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Acknowledge the emotions you bring to a dispute, or that arise during it, so you state reasons rather than vent feelings.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: What feelings am I bringing to this book?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: it is necessary to acknowledge the emotions you bring to a dispute, or those that arise in the course of it.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Feelings aren't reasons
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Check that what you take for reasons are not just strong feelings.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Are these reasons, or strong feelings dressed up as reasons?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: You may even think you have reasons, when all you have are strong feelings.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: State your assumptions
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Make your own assumptions, your prejudgments, explicit so you can admit the author may be entitled to different ones.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: What are my own prejudices on this subject?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Second, you must make your own assumptions explicit.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Grant the author's assumptions
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Honor an author's explicit request to take something for granted, even if the opposite could also be assumed.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Am I quarrelling about assumptions instead of the argument?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Good controversy should not be a quarrel about assumptions.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Try impartiality
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Attempt impartiality by trying to take the author's point of view.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I tried to see the matter from the author's side?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: each of the disputants should at least try to take the other fellow’s point of view.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Read sympathetically
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Read the book sympathetically before disagreeing, so that your disagreement is civil rather than contentious.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Was I able to read this book sympathetically?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: If you have not been able to read a book sympathetically, your disagreement with it is probably more contentious than civil.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Criticize, don't attack
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Criticize the book rather than attacking it; don't knock over straw men or proclaim prejudices.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Am I criticizing the author's actual position or a straw man?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: We have caught ourselves attacking a book rather than criticizing it, knocking straw men over
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.mistake: Denouncing where you cannot support denials.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Four adverse criticisms
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Confine adverse criticism to four remarks: the author is uninformed, misinformed, illogical, or his analysis is incomplete.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Which of the four points am I making against the author?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: (1) “You are uninformed”; (2) “You are misinformed”; (3) “You are illogical—your reasoning is not cogent”; (4) “Your analysis is incomplete.”

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Points can combine
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Make any or all of the four points as they apply; the defects are not mutually exclusive.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I considered every one of the four points, not just one?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Each and all can be made, because the defects they refer to are not mutually exclusive.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Be definite and precise
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Specify exactly in what respect the author is uninformed, misinformed, or illogical.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I named the precise point where the author goes wrong?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: A book cannot be uninformed or misinformed about everything.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Support each criticism
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Give reasons supporting each critical point you make.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: What reasons back up my criticism?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: He must give reasons for saying what he does.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Show the author uninformed
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Show wherein the author lacks some piece of knowledge relevant to the problem he is trying to solve.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: What relevant knowledge does the author lack?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: To say that an author is uninformed is to say that he lacks some piece of knowledge that is relevant to the problem he is trying to solve.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: State the missing knowledge
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: To support the charge, state the knowledge the author lacks and show how it would change his conclusions.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Can I state the missing knowledge and show how it alters his conclusions?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: you must be able yourself to state the knowledge that the author lacks and show how it is relevant, how it makes a difference to his conclusions.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Only relevant gaps count
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Do not charge the author with ignorance of knowledge that would not have been relevant to his problem.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Would this missing knowledge actually have mattered to his argument?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: unless the knowledge, if possessed by the author, would have been relevant, there is no point in making this remark.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Science gains, philosophy can lose
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Expect later research to reveal gaps in science and history, but in philosophy look also for knowledge an author lost that earlier thinkers had.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Did this author ignore distinctions earlier thinkers had already established?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: There is just as likely to be loss as gain with the passage of time.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Show the author misinformed
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Show wherein the author asserts what is not the case, proposing as true what is false or less probable.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Where does the author assert something contrary to fact?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: To say that an author is misinformed is to say that he asserts what is not the case.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Argue the contrary
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: To support the charge, argue for the truth or greater probability of a position contrary to the author's.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Can I argue that the contrary position is true or more probable?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: to support the remark you must be able to argue the truth or greater probability of a position contrary to the author’s.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Only relevant errors count
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Point out a factual error only if it bears on the author's conclusions.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Does this error affect his conclusions, or is its relevance limited?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: This kind of defect should be pointed out, of course, only if it is relevant to the author’s conclusions.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Lack vs error
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Distinguish a lack of knowledge (blocks conclusions) from erroneous suppositions (lead to wrong conclusions).
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Is the defect a gap in knowledge or a positive error?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: But it makes a difference whether the defect is simply negative or positive as well.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Defects in premises
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Recognize that being uninformed or misinformed are both defects in the author's premises: his evidence is inadequate in quantity or quality.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Are my first two criticisms aimed at the author's premises?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Taken together, these two points charge an author with defects in his premises.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Show the author illogical
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Show wherein the author has committed a fallacy in reasoning.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Where exactly does the author's argument lack cogency?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: To say that an author is illogical is to say that he has committed a fallacy in reasoning.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Non sequitur
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Look for conclusions that simply do not follow from the reasons offered.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Does the conclusion actually follow from the reasons given?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: There is the non sequitur, which means that what is drawn as a conclusion simply does not follow from the reasons offered.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Inconsistency
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Look for two things the author has said that are incompatible with each other.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Does anything the author says elsewhere contradict this?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: And there is the occurrence of inconsistency, which means that two things the author has tried to say are incompatible.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Target major conclusions
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Show the precise respect in which the argument fails, and only where the major conclusions are affected.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Does this fallacy affect the author's major conclusions?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: A book may safely lack cogency in irrelevant respects.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Read penetratingly for slips
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Read penetratingly, since fallacies in good books are usually elaborately concealed.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I looked closely for concealed slips in reasoning?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: When they do occur, they are usually elaborately concealed, and it requires a very penetrating reader to discover them.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Bad reasoning, good grounds
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Focus the charge of illogic on poor reasoning from good grounds, rather than on reasoning from untrue premises.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Are the premises sound, so that the fault lies in the reasoning itself?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: But we are here concerned primarily with the case in which he reasons poorly from good grounds.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Otherwise you must agree
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: If you cannot show the author uninformed, misinformed, or illogical on relevant matters, agree with him as far as he has gone.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I supported any of the first three points? If not, have I admitted agreement?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: If you have not been able to show that the author is uninformed, misinformed, or illogical on relevant matters, you simply cannot disagree.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Disliking isn't disagreeing
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Do not reject conclusions whose premises and reasoning you cannot fault; that is only dislike, emotion, or prejudice.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Am I rejecting a conclusion I simply don't like?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: All you can possibly mean by saying something like that is that you do not like the conclusions.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.mistake: “I find nothing wrong with your premises … but I don't agree with your conclusions.”

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Recheck your understanding
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: If you remain unconvinced without being able to support any criticism, question whether you really understood.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: If I can't fault the book yet feel unconvinced, did I really understand it?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: perhaps you should not have said you understood in the first place.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Elements vs whole
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Aim the first three criticisms at terms, propositions and arguments, and the fourth at the structure of the whole.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Is my criticism about the parts of the argument or the whole work?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: The fourth remark—that the book is incomplete—bears on the structure of the whole.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Show the analysis incomplete
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Show wherein the author failed to solve all his problems, use his materials fully, see their implications, or make relevant distinctions.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Which problems, implications, or distinctions has the author missed?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: To say that an author’s analysis is incomplete is to say that he has not solved all the problems he started with

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Define the incompleteness
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Define the inadequacy precisely, by your own knowledge or with help from other books, rather than just calling the book incomplete.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Can I say exactly what is missing from the author's account?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: It is not enough to say that a book is incomplete. Anyone can say that of any book.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Incompleteness isn't disagreement
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Treat incompleteness as marking the limits of the author's achievement, not as grounds for disagreement.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Am I treating incompleteness as if it made the author wrong?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: This fourth point is strictly not a basis for disagreement.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Suspend judgment on the whole
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Agree in part where you find no other fault, but suspend judgment on the whole if the analysis is incomplete.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Do I agree in part yet suspend judgment on the whole?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Suspended judgment on the reader’s part responds to an author’s failure to solve his problems perfectly.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Compare books by the criteria
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Compare related books in the same field by the four criteria; the best treats its subject most adequately.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Which book speaks more truth and makes fewer errors?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Related books in the same field can be critically compared by reference to these four criteria.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Count valid distinctions
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Measure completeness by the number of valid and significant distinctions an account makes, which matches its number of terms.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: How many valid, significant distinctions does each account contain?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: The measure of such completeness is to be found in the number of valid and significant distinctions that the accounts being compared contain.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Completeness ties the stages
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Judge completeness by checking how well the author stated his problems (outline) and how far he solved them (interpretation).
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: How adequately did he state his problems, and how satisfactorily did he solve them?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: The final step of criticism is the point about completeness.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Three criteria to disagree
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Use only the first three criteria as grounds for disagreement; failing them, agree at least in part.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I met one of the first three criteria before disagreeing?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Of these last four, the first three are criteria for disagreement.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Rules 9-15 answer Q3 and Q4
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Apply rules 9 to 15, the maxims of etiquette and the criteria of criticism, to answer: Is it true? What of it?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I applied the last seven rules to judge truth and significance?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: the last seven rules of reading—the maxims of intellectual etiquette and the criteria for points of criticism—help you to answer the third and fourth basic questions you must ask.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Is it true?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Ask of anything you read whether it is true, in the relevant sense of truth.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Is it true, in whole or part, in the sense appropriate to this kind of writing?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: The question, Is it true? can be asked of anything we read.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Judge by truth
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Judge books by their truth, clarity and power to enlighten, not by novelty or sensationalism.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Am I praising this book for its truth or for its novelty?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: their novelty, their sensationalism, their seductiveness, their force, and even their power to bemuse or befuddle the mind, but not their truth, their clarity, or their power to enlighten
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.mistake: Praising books for flouting truth outrageously.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: What of it?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: If what you read is true in some sense, go on to ask what follows from it.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: If it is true, what significance does it have?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: Unless what you have read is true in some sense, you need go no further. But if it is, you must face the last question.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Find the significance
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Determine what significance is, or should be, attached to the facts presented.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: What significance should these facts have?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: You cannot read for information intelligently without determining what significance is, or should be, attached to the facts presented.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Go beyond information
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: When the material is primarily informational, go further and seek enlightenment; keep searching for significance.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I moved from information to understanding?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: When the material you have read is itself primarily informational, you are challenged to go further and seek enlightenment.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Four questions sum it up
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Treat the four questions as summarizing all your obligations as a reader.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I answered all four basic questions about this book?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: These four questions, as we have already pointed out, summarize all the obligations of a reader.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Approximate the ideal
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Use the rules as an ideal performance to approximate; your skill is measured by how near you come.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: How close did my reading come to the ideal the rules describe?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: You are a good reader to the degree in which you approximate it.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Quality over quantity
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Judge being well-read by the quality of reading, not the number of books read.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Have I read this book well, or just added it to my count?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: A person who has read widely but not well deserves to be pitied rather than praised.

analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.title: Read each book by merit
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.action: Use your skill with discrimination: read well the books worth it and only inspect the many others.
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.check: Does this book deserve analytical reading or only inspection?
analytical/agreeing-or-disagreeing-with-.quote: by reading every book according to its merits.

general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.title: Intrinsic vs extrinsic
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.action: Distinguish reading a book in itself (intrinsic) from reading it in the light of other books and aids (extrinsic).
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.check: Am I working on the book alone, or using outside aids?
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.quote: By “extrinsic reading” we mean reading a book in the light of other books.

general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.title: Bring what you know
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.action: Measure the author's statements against your experience of other books and of life.
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.check: Have I brought my own experience and other reading to bear on this book?
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.quote: no book should be, because no book can be, read entirely and completely in isolation.

general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.title: Do your best alone first
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.action: Do all you can by yourself before seeking outside help; you will then need less and less of it.
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.check: Have I exhausted my own efforts before turning to aids?
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.quote: On the whole, it is best to do all that you can by yourself before seeking outside help

general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.title: Don't lean on aids
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.action: Do not depend slavishly on extrinsic aids.
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.check: Am I reaching for help before I have tried?
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.quote: many readers depend on them too slavishly

general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.title: Four kinds of aids
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.action: Know the four kinds of extrinsic aids: relevant experience, other books, commentaries and abstracts, and reference books.
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.check: Which kind of aid fits my difficulty?
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.quote: first, relevant experiences; second, other books; third, commentaries and abstracts; fourth, reference books.

general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.title: When to seek help
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.action: Seek outside help when the book remains unintelligible, in whole or part, after you have done your best with the rules of intrinsic reading.
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.check: Have I applied the intrinsic rules fully, and is the book still unclear?
general/aids-to-reading/intrinsic-and-ex.quote: outside help should be sought whenever a book remains unintelligible to you, either in whole or part

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: Common vs special experience
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: Distinguish common experience, available to anyone alive, from special experience that must be actively sought, as in a laboratory.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Does this book draw on common experience or special experience?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: Special experience must be actively sought and is available only to those who go to the trouble of acquiring it.

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: Common is not universal
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: Count experience as common if most people share it in ordinary life, even if not everyone does.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Is this experience shared by most people, even if not by all?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: Common is not the same as universal.

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: Test fiction by life
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: Judge a novel's verisimilitude by your common experience of life as most people live it.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Is this story true to my experience of life?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: Judgments concerning the verisimilitude of a novel are almost wholly based on common experience

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: Test philosophy by common sense
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: To understand and test a philosopher's principles, refer to your own common sense and daily observation.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Does the philosopher's principle hold up against my ordinary observation?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: He refers you to your own common sense and your daily observation of the world in which you live.

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: Follow the scientist's evidence
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: To judge a scientific book's inductive arguments, follow the special experience it reports, helped by descriptions, illustrations and diagrams.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Can I follow the evidence on which the scientist bases his argument?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: To understand and judge the inductive arguments in a scientific book, you must be able to follow the evidence that the scientist reports as their basis.

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: History needs both
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: Bring common experience to history as story, and attend to the special experience (documents, research) the historian relies on.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Am I reading this history both as story and as research?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: Both common and special experience are relevant to the reading of history books.

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: Give a concrete example
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: Test your use of experience by giving a concrete example of a point you think you understand.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Can I give a concrete example of this point, beyond the author's own?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: ask yourself whether you can give a concrete example of a point that you feel you understand.

general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.title: No example? Reread
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.action: If you cannot supply an example of the author's point, go back and read the discussion again.
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.check: Could I supply my own example? If not, have I reread?
general/aids-to-reading/the-role-of-rele.quote: If not, you should go back and read his discussion again.

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Don't start mid-conversation
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: Do not expect to understand a great book without first reading the books closely related to it.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: Have I read the books this one responds to?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: they think they should be able to understand the first book they pick up, without having read the others to which it is closely related.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.mistake: Reading The Federalist Papers without the Articles of Confederation and the Constitution.

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Read related books in order
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: Read related books in relation to one another and in an order that makes the later ones more intelligible.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: Am I reading these books in an order that clarifies the later ones?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: Reading related books in relation to one another and in an order that renders the later ones more intelligible is a basic common-sense maxim of extrinsic reading.

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Read the earlier writer first
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: Read the earlier writer who influenced a later one first, to help you understand the later.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: Who influenced this author, and have I read him?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: If you read the earlier writer first, he may help you to understand the later one.

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Related books as context
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: Use related books as a larger context for interpreting a book, as you use the whole book to interpret its parts.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: What do related books reveal about this book's meaning?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: Just as the whole book is the context for any of its parts, so related books provide an even larger context

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Read what they read
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: To understand a great author, read the books he read.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: Which books was this author in conversation with?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: one way to understand them is to read the books they read.

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Respect chronology
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: Join the great conversation by reading the books in an order that respects chronology, from past to present or present to past.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: Does my reading order respect when these books were written?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: The books can be read from the present into the past or from the past into the present.

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Most needed for philosophy
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: Read philosophy and history especially in relation to other books, since philosophers are great readers of each other.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: Have I read the philosophers this one is answering?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: It is most important in the case of philosophy, because philosophers are great readers of each other.

general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.title: Least needed for fiction
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.action: Feel free to read good novels and plays in isolation; related reading matters least for them.
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.check: Does this novel or play stand on its own?
general/aids-to-reading/other-books-as-e.quote: It is probably least important in the case of novels or plays, which, if they are really good, can be read in isolation

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Use commentaries sparingly
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Use commentaries and abstracts wisely, which means sparingly.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Am I relying on commentary more than on the book?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: such works should be used wisely, which is to say sparingly.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Commentators can be wrong
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Remember that commentators, and especially student handbooks, can be wrong in their interpretations.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Have I checked the commentary against the book itself?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: The first is that commentators are not always right in their comments on a book.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Commentaries limit you
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Remember that even a correct commentary is not exhaustive and may keep you from finding other important meanings.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Am I seeing only the points the commentator made?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: Reading a commentary, particularly one that seems very self-assured, thus tends to limit your understanding of a book

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Book first, commentary after
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Do not read someone else's commentary or introduction until after you have read the book.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Did I read the book itself before the commentary?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: you should not read a commentary by someone else until after you have read the book.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.mistake: Reading a scholarly introduction first and seeing only the scholar's points.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Ask it remaining questions
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: After doing your best with the book, turn to the commentary only for answers to questions that still puzzle you.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: What specific questions am I bringing to the commentary?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: then and only then apply to them for answers to questions that still puzzle you.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Reading it first distorts
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Avoid reading critical introductions first, since they tend to distort your reading of the book.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Has an introduction shaped what I noticed in the book?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: If you read them first they are likely to distort your reading of the book.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Meet commentators as equals
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Approach a commentator on equal terms, having read and understood the book yourself.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Can I judge where this commentator is right or wrong?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: If you read his introduction before reading the book, however, you are at his mercy.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Never skip the original
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Never let a handbook replace reading the original book.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Have I actually read the original book?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: But if you depend wholly on the handbook, and never read the original book, you may be in bad trouble.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Dependence weakens you
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Do not form the habit of depending on commentaries and handbooks; it makes you a worse reader in general.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Could I read this book well with no commentary at hand?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: You may be able to understand a particular book with the help of a commentary, but in general you will be a worse reader.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Abstracts jog memory
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Use an abstract or digest only to jog your memory of a book you have already read, ideally one you made yourself.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Have I already read the book this abstract summarizes?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: First, they can help to jog your memory of a book’s contents, if you have already read it.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Make your own abstract
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: Make your own abstract of a book while reading it analytically.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Did I write my own abstract during analytical reading?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: Ideally, you made such an abstract yourself, in reading the book analytically

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.title: Abstracts screen books
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.action: In syntopical reading, use abstracts to decide whether a work is germane, never as a replacement for reading it.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.check: Does this abstract tell me whether I need to read the book?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-comme.quote: An abstract can never replace the reading of a book, but it can sometimes tell you whether you want or need to read the book or not.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Reference books need knowledge
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Do not expect a reference book to cure total ignorance or think for you; you must already know a good deal.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Do I know enough to use this reference book well?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: It cannot do your thinking for you.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Know what you want
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Have some idea of what you want to know, so you can ask the reference book an intelligible question.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Can I state my question to the reference book clearly?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: you must be able to ask a reference book an intelligible question.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Know where to look
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Know what kind of question you are asking and which kind of reference book answers it.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Which type of reference book answers this kind of question?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: You must know what kind of question you are asking, and which kinds of reference books answer that kind of question.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Learn the reference types
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Get a fair overall knowledge of the major types of reference books before relying on any one type.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Do I know the major types of reference books and what each covers?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: you must have a fair overall knowledge of all of the major types of reference books before you can use any one type effectively

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Know how it's organized
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Learn how the particular reference work is organized by reading the editor's advice on how to use it first.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Have I read the preface or instructions for using this work?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: Do not try to use a reference book before getting the editor’s advice on how to use it.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Know what is knowable
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Look in reference books only for things on which people generally and conventionally agree.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Is my question one that the compilers consider knowable?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: Only those things about which men generally and conventionally agree are to be found in reference books.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: No moral or future answers
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Do not look in reference books for answers to moral questions or questions about the future.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Is this a moral or future question no reference book can settle?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: We do not agree on moral questions or on questions about the future, and so these sorts of things are not to be found in reference books.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Four reference questions
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Before using a reference work, check: what you want, which work has it, how to find it there, and whether it is considered knowable.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Do I know what I want, where it is, how to find it, and that it is knowable?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: You must know what you want to know; you must know in what reference work to find it; you must know how to find it in the reference work

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.title: Not guides to the perplexed
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.action: Do not turn to reference books when you know nothing about a subject; they are useless then.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.check: Do I have enough light around my darkness to use this book?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-refer.quote: Reference books are useless to people who know nothing.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Know the dictionary's kind
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Apply the first rule of reading to the dictionary: know it is primarily an educational instrument.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Do I understand what a dictionary is for?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: the dictionary, however constructed, is primarily an educational instrument.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: More than spelling
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Do not use a dictionary merely as a spelling book or pronunciation guide.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Am I using the dictionary only to spell and pronounce?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: If you look upon a dictionary merely as a spelling book or guide to pronunciation, you will use it accordingly, which is to say not well.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Note order of meanings
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Attend not only to the variety of meanings under a word but also to their order and relation.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: How are this word's meanings ordered and related?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: you will pay attention, not merely to the variety of meanings listed under each word, but also to their order and relation.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Use it for hard vocabulary
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Use the dictionary to read books with technical words, archaic words, literary allusions, or familiar words in obsolete senses.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Is this word technical, archaic, an allusion, or used in an obsolete sense?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: because their vocabulary includes technical words, archaic words, literary allusions, or even familiar words used in obsolete senses.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Don't look up too much
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: On a first reading of a difficult book, do not sit with the dictionary in hand looking up many words.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Am I losing the book's unity by stopping too often for words?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: If you have to look up too many words at the beginning, you will certainly lose track of the book’s unity and order.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Look up only key words
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: During a first reading, look up even new or technical words only if they seem important to the author's general meaning.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Is this word important to the author's general meaning?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: unless they seem to be important to the author’s general meaning.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Don't settle arguments by it
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Do not try to settle arguments about ideas like justice or freedom by quoting the dictionary.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Am I treating the lexicographer as an authority on things rather than words?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: Lexicographers may be respected as authorities on word usage, but they are not the ultimate founts of wisdom.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Don't swallow the dictionary
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Do not memorize lists of words whose meanings are unconnected with any actual experience.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Are these words connected to my experience, or merely memorized?

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: About words, not things
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Remember the dictionary is a book about words, not about things.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Is my question about a word or about a thing?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: do not forget that the dictionary is a book about words, not about things.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Words as physical things
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Ask how a word is spelled and pronounced, remembering that variations occur.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: How is this word spelled and pronounced?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: There must, therefore, be uniform ways of spelling and pronouncing them

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Words as parts of speech
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Ask what grammatical role the word plays and how it shifts between parts of speech.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: What part of speech is this word here?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: Each single word plays a grammatical role in the more complicated structure of a phrase or sentence.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Words as signs
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Ask what the word's many meanings are and how they relate: synonyms, antonyms, proper or common, concrete or abstract.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Which of its meanings fits here, and how does it relate to other words?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: They have meanings, not one but many.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Words as conventions
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Ask the word's history: its etymology, changes in form, and which meanings are archaic, current, idiomatic, colloquial or slang.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Where does this word come from, and is this sense current or obsolete?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: That is why every word has a history

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Know what to ask
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Practice the art of using a dictionary: know what questions to ask about words and how to find the answers.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Which of the four kinds of question am I asking?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: The art of using a dictionary consists in knowing what questions to ask about words and how to find the answers.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.title: Read the explanatory notes
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.action: Consult the dictionary's explanatory notes and list of abbreviations before using it.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.check: Have I read the explanatory notes and abbreviations list?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-a-dic.quote: fails to consult the explanatory notes and the list of abbreviations at the beginning of a dictionary

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Don't read it through
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Do not try to read an encyclopedia through or learn it by heart.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Am I using the encyclopedia as an aid or trying to absorb it whole?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: But it is just as vain to try to read an encyclopedia through as a dictionary.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: More than dates and places
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Do not use an encyclopedia only to look up dates, places and simple facts; it is an educational tool too.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: But this is to under-use, or misuse, an encyclopedia.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Seek facts in relation
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Look for the underlying arrangement of knowledge and the relations among facts, not facts in isolation.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: How does this fact relate to other facts in the encyclopedia?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: But he should not be content with facts in isolation.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Follow the editors' directions
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Read and follow the encyclopedia's directions for use, which often send you to the index first.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Have I read the directions on how to use this encyclopedia?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: Any good encyclopedia includes directions about how to use it effectively, and these should be read and followed.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Use the index
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Use the index to gather widely separated discussions of one subject and to see how knowledge is arranged.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Did I start from the index rather than a single article?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: any reader who fails to use the index has only himself to blame if the work does not serve his needs.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Not for opinion disputes
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Do not use encyclopedias to settle arguments based on differences of opinion, nor enslave yourself to one.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Is this dispute about opinion rather than fact?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: encyclopedias are not to be used for the settling of arguments where these are based on differences of opinion.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: End factual disputes
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Use an encyclopedia to end disputes about matters of fact quickly and permanently.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Is this a question of fact that I can simply look up?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: Facts should never be argued about in the first place.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Consult several
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: If depending on encyclopedias for a subject, read more than one, preferably written at different times.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Have I compared more than one encyclopedia's account?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: Read more than one, and preferably ones written at different times.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Facts are propositions
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Ask not only what the fact is but what its significance is and how it affects the truth you seek.
