general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: What is the significance of this fact for my question?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: You do not know much if all you know is what the fact is.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Facts are “true” propositions
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Ask whether a statement is generally agreed fact or an opinion, which an encyclopedia must clearly label.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Is this generally agreed, or is it labeled as opinion?

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Facts reflect reality
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Ask whether a statement is an agreed reflection of reality or merely a theory or speculation.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Is this generally agreed to be correct, or only a theory?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: an explanation of reality (or of part of it) is not a fact until and unless there is general agreement that it is correct.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Facts are partly conventional
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Ask whether a fact belongs to a particular epoch or culture and could be revised by better observation.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Might this fact be revised by later investigation or differ across cultures?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: almost any given proposition that we take to be true can be falsified by more patient or more accurate observation and investigation.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Ask proper questions of facts
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Practice the art of using an encyclopedia: ask the proper questions about facts.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Which of the four kinds of question about facts am I asking?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: The art of using an encyclopedia as an aid to reading is the art of asking the proper questions about facts.

general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.title: Not for understanding
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.action: Do not pursue understanding mainly in an encyclopedia; it lacks arguments and imaginative literature.
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.check: Do I need arguments or imaginative works that an encyclopedia cannot give?
general/aids-to-reading/how-to-use-an-en.quote: You should also remember that an encyclopedia is not the best place to pursue understanding.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.title: Adapt rules to the book
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.action: Apply the general rules of analytical reading flexibly, adapting them to the particular kind of book in front of you.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.check: Have I adjusted the rules to the sort of book this is, rather than applying them mechanically?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.quote: Hence, you must have some flexibility and adaptability in following the rules.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.mistake: Treating the rules as if you could read a book in general.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.title: Ask the four questions
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.action: Ask the four basic questions of whatever you read, fiction or nonfiction alike.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.check: Did I ask what the book is about, what it says, whether it is true, and what of it?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.quote: These four questions are relevant to any book, whether fiction or nonfiction, whether poetry or history or science or philosophy.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.title: Fifteen rules exclude fiction
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.action: Do not apply the fifteen expository rules unchanged to fiction and poetry; use the parallel rules for imaginative literature instead.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.check: Am I looking for terms, propositions and arguments in a novel, play or poem?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/a.quote: Novels and plays and poems do not proceed by terms, propositions, and arguments

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Action alone solves
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Remember that a practical book cannot solve its problem for you; only your own action in the world can.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Am I treating reading the book as if it had solved the practical problem?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: But a practical problem can only be solved by action itself.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.mistake: Thinking the problem is solved once the book is read.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Apply rules to your case
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Add your knowledge of your particular situation and your judgment of how the book's general rules apply to it.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Have I worked out how each general rule fits my concrete circumstances?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: the reader himself must add something to the book to make it applicable in practice.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Recognize a practical book
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Classify a book as practical if it gives rules or deals with a field of human behavior where people can do better or worse.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Does the book's problem concern action in a field where one can do better or worse?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: It is always about a field of human behavior in which men can do better or worse.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.mistake: Taking a book of practical principles for a purely theoretical one.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Rules vs. principles books
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Decide whether the practical book mainly presents rules (like a cookbook) or mainly the principles that generate rules (like economics, politics, morals).
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Is the emphasis on prescriptions to follow, or on the principles behind them?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: Practical books thus fall into two main groups.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Find rules as propositions
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: In a rule-book, treat the rules as the major propositions to find.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Can I list the book's main rules?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: In reading a book that is primarily a rule-book, the major propositions to look for, of course, are the rules.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Spot rules in any form
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Recognize a rule, whether imperative or declarative, by its recommending something as worth doing to gain an end.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Does this sentence, however phrased, recommend something as worth doing for some end?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: you can always recognize a rule because it recommends something as worth doing to gain a certain end.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Find both kinds of argument
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Look for both the appeal to principles and the illustration by concrete cases as arguments that the rules are sound.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Have I found where the author argues from principles and where from examples?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: Look for both sorts of arguments.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Read between the lines
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: In a book of practical principles, derive the unstated rules from the principles and work out how they would be applied in practice.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: What rules follow from these principles, and how would I apply them?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: He tries to see the rules that may not be expressed but that can, nevertheless, be derived from the principles.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Read it as practical
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Read a practical book as practical, looking for the actions its principles lead to.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Have I connected the book's principles to the actions they recommend?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: To fail to read a practical book as practical is to read it poorly.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.mistake: Reading a practical book as mere theory.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Two tests of practical truth
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Judge a rule of conduct practically true only if it works and its working leads to an end you rightly desire.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Does the rule work, and does it lead to the right end?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: one is that it works; the other is that its working leads you to the right end, an end you rightly desire.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Judge by the ends
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Make your main judgment of a practical book about its ends, not its means.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Do I share the author's goal, whatever I think of his means?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: Your main judgment will always be in terms of the ends, not the means.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Author's objectives?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Ask what the author's objectives are.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: The first is: What are the author’s objectives?

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Means proposed?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Ask what means the author proposes for achieving those objectives.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: “What means for achieving them is he proposing?”
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: The second is: What means for achieving them is he proposing?

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Expect persuasion
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Expect every practical book to contain some oratory or propaganda aimed at winning you to its ends.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Where is the author trying to persuade me, not just inform me?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: There is an admixture of oratory or propaganda in every practical book.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Recognize propaganda
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Protect yourself from propaganda by recognizing it for what it is.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Can I point to the passages that are working on my emotions?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: The best protection against propaganda of any sort is the recognition of it for what it is.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.mistake: Letting hidden oratory reach the heart without passing through the mind.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Spot emotive words
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Use your grasp of the book's terms, propositions and arguments to spot passages that use words emotively.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Which passages make an emotive use of words?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: He will spot the passages that make an “emotive use of words.”

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Weigh the appeals
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: Keep sales resistance against hasty, thoughtless acceptance, but do not make yourself deaf to all appeals.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: Am I weighing the appeals rather than swallowing or rejecting them all?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: Sales resistance is good when it prevents you from buying hastily and thoughtlessly.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.mistake: Being totally deaf to all appeals, or wholly unaware of them.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.title: Know the author's life
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.action: For moral, political or economic books, learn something of the author's character, life and times.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.check: What do I know of the author's situation that bears on his recommendations?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/t.quote: you should know something about the character of the writer, something about his life and times.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: Still outline the book
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: Outline the structure of a practical book as you would any expository book.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: Have I made an outline of the book's structure?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: it is still necessary, in the course of answering this first question, to make an outline of the book’s structure.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: What he wants you to do
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: Find out what the author wants you to do; this adaptation of Rule 4 becomes the dominant task.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: Can I state what the author wants me to do?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: knowing what he wants to do comes down to knowing what he wants you to do.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: How he proposes you do it
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: Find out how the author proposes that you do it, discovering and understanding the means he recommends.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: Can I state the means the author recommends for reaching his end?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: You must discover and understand the means the author recommends for achieving what he is proposing.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: Right ends, best means?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: Ask whether the author's ends and means accord with your conception of what is right to seek and the best way of seeking it.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: Do I think his end is right to seek, and his means the best way to it?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: accord with your conception of what it is right to seek, and of what is the best way of seeking it.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: Agreement implies action
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: If you accept both the author's ends and his means, act as he recommends.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: Having agreed with the ends and means, have I begun to act on them?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: Agreement with a practical book, however, does imply action on your part.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: Inaction reveals disagreement
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: If you fail to act, recognize that you do not really agree with the ends or accept the means.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: If I have not acted, which did I not really accept, the end or the means?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: If he did both, he could not reasonably fail to act.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: Universal vs. selective ends
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: Decide whether the author's end applies to everyone or only to a class, and whether you honestly belong to that class.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: Is this end meant for all readers or for a group, and am I in it?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: If the end is selective, applying only to a certain class of human beings, then the reader must decide whether or not he belongs to that class.

analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.title: Beware excusing yourself
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.action: Be suspicious of deciding the end does not apply to you; you may be fooling yourself about your motives.
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.check: Am I really outside the class, or just reluctant to act myself?
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.quote: there is a strong possibility that the reader may be fooling himself, or misunderstanding his own motives
analytical/how-to-read-practical-books/w.mistake: Conceding end and means but leaving the action to someone else.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Pleases rather than teaches
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Recognize that imaginative literature aims primarily to please, and that knowing why it pleases is harder than being pleased.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Can I say why the work pleased me, not just that it did?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: Imaginative literature primarily pleases rather than teaches.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Go below the surface
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Read a novel fully enough that you can give an account of what you liked and what caused your pleasure.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Can I explain what in the book caused my enjoyment?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: Those who cannot say what they like about a novel probably have not read it below its most obvious surfaces.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.mistake: Being tongue-tied about why you enjoyed a novel.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Knowledge vs. experience
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Distinguish expository books, which convey knowledge, from imaginative ones, which communicate an experience to be enjoyed.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Is this book trying to tell me something, or to give me an experience?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: Imaginative ones try to communicate an experience itself —one that the reader can have or share only by reading

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Don't resist its effect
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Do not resist the effect a work of imaginative literature has on you.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Did I let the work act on me, or hold it at arm's length?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: Don’t try to resist the effect that a work of imaginative literature has on you.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.mistake: Reading fiction like a bird of prey ready to pounce.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Let it move you
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Read actively in a receptive way: open yourself and let the story move you and do its work on you.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Did I allow the story to move me?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: We must allow it to move us, we must let it do whatever work it wants to do on us.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Ambiguity and implication
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Expect imaginative writing to exploit multiple meanings and metaphor, and attend to what is implied as much as what is said.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Have I attended to what lies between the lines, not just the literal words?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: imaginative writing relies as much upon what is implied as upon what is said.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Don't seek terms or arguments
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Do not look for terms, propositions, and arguments in imaginative literature; they are logical, not poetic, devices.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I trying to extract a logical argument from a poem or story?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: Don’t look for terms, propositions, and arguments in imaginative literature.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.mistake: Reading a novel as a philosophical argument, or a lyric as a demonstration.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Think about the experience
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: To learn from imaginative works, do your own thinking about the vicarious experience they create.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: What have I thought out for myself from the experience the work gave me?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: In order to learn from such books, we have to do our own thinking about experience

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Don't judge by factual truth
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Do not criticize fiction by the standards of truth and consistency proper to communicating knowledge.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I faulting the story for facts it was never offering as a treatise?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: Don’t criticize fiction by the standards of truth and consistency that properly apply to communication of knowledge.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.mistake: Faulting a story for errors of geography or history it surrounds with plausibility.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Truth as verisimilitude
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Judge a story's truth by its verisimilitude: whether it is a likely story within the world the author created.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Could this have happened in the world the novelist created?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: The “truth” of a good story is its verisimilitude, its intrinsic probability or plausibility.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Test against experience
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Test an understood philosophical book against common experience by asking whether it is true and matches what you have felt and thought.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: “Is this true? Have we felt this? Have we always thought this without realizing it?”
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: We say, is this true? Have we felt this? Have we always thought this without realizing it?

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Don't test poetry that way
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Do not test a poem or play against your own experience as you would a philosophical theory; its world is unique.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I rejecting the work because its events differ from my own life?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: We cannot test Othello, say, against our own experience

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Classify by kind
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Classify a work of imaginative literature by its kind (lyric, novel, play) and recognize at once what kind you are reading.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Do I know whether this is a lyric, a novel or a play, and how that changes my receptivity?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: You must classify a work of imaginative literature according to its kind.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Lyric, novel, play differ
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Distinguish a lyric (a single emotional experience), a novel (complex plot, narrator may speak), and a play (actions and speeches only).
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Does the author tell the story in his own voice, or only through actions and speeches?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: The playwright can never speak in his own person, as the novelist can, and frequently does, in the course of a novel.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Grasp the unity
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Grasp the unity of the whole work, testing yourself by expressing it in a sentence or two.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Can I express the work's unity in a sentence or two?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: You must grasp the unity of the whole work.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Summarize the plot
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: State the unity of a story as a brief narration of its plot, not as a proposition or argument.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Can I summarize the plot briefly as a narrative?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: the unity of a story is always in its plot.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.mistake: Stating a story's unity as a thesis or argument.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Find how parts build plot
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Discover how the whole is built from its parts: where it begins, what it goes through, the crises, the climax, and the aftermath.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Can I name the beginning, the crises, the climax and what follows it within the story?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: You must know the various crises that lead up to the climax, where and how the climax occurs, and what happens in the aftermath.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Find the real beginning
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Locate where the narrative actually begins, which may not be the first page, and follow its temporal order.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Where does the story really begin?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: To know the structure of a narrative, you must know where it begins—which is not necessarily on the first page

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Parts need the whole
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Do not expect chapters, acts or verses of fiction to make sense read in isolation; read them within the whole.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I judging a chapter or stanza apart from the whole work?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: But the chapters of a novel, the acts of a play, or the verses of a lyric often become relatively meaningless when wrenched from the whole.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Know characters and incidents
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Become acquainted with the details of incident and characterization, the fictional analogue of coming to terms.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I familiar with the characters, and have I lived through the events?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: You have not grasped a story until you are familiar with its characters, until you have lived through its events.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Be at home in its world
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Become at home in the imaginary world as an observer and member of its population, sharing its characters' fortunes by sympathetic insight.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Do I know this world as if I were on the scene?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: become at home in this imaginary world; know it as if you were an observer on the scene

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Follow the plot's movement
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Follow the characters through their adventures, staying sensitive to the unfolding of the plot, the analogue of following an argument.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I following the plot's development closely as it unfolds?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: To read a story well you must have your finger on the pulse of the narrative, be sensitive to its very beat.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Don't press the analogy
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Use the expository-to-fiction analogy loosely; do not examine it too closely.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I forcing the story into the expository rules point by point?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: we must caution you not to examine the analogy too closely.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Find the lyric's speaker
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Apply these rules to lyrics too: find the beginning, middle and end, and treat the speaker as at least one character.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Who is speaking in this poem, and how does the experience progress?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: there is always at least one character—namely, the speaker of the poem.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Appreciate before criticizing
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Do not criticize imaginative writing until you fully appreciate what the author tried to make you experience.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Have I had the experience the author tried to produce in me?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: don’t criticize imaginative writing until you fully appreciate what the author has tried to make you experience.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Grant the author's world
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Accept the world the author creates; criticize only what he makes of it.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I objecting to the setting itself rather than to what the author does with it?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: The good reader of a story does not question the world that the author creates
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.mistake: Objecting the story should be set in Minneapolis rather than Paris.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Like, not agree
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Judge fiction by whether you like it and by its beauty, not by agreeing or disagreeing.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Am I judging beauty, or treating the story as a claim to agree with?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: we do not agree or disagree with fiction. We either like it or we do not.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Read actively to appreciate
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Perform all the acts of analytical reading on a novel, reading it passionately, before judging it.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Did I read actively enough to have the experience before judging?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: you cannot appreciate a novel by reading it passively

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Objectify your reactions
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: After saying what you like and why, point to the things in the book that caused your reactions.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Can I point to what in the book caused my liking or disliking?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: you must objectify your reactions by pointing to those things in the book that caused them.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.mistake: Giving reasons that describe your own prejudices rather than the book.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Say what is good or bad
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Move from saying what you like or dislike and why to saying what is good or bad about the book and why.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: Have I said what is good or bad in the book itself, and why?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: You must pass from saying what you like or dislike and why, to saying what is good or bad about the book and why.

analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.title: Discern causes of pleasure
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.action: Reflect on the causes of your pleasure in fiction and poetry so you gradually develop a standard of criticism.
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.check: What artistic virtues in the work account for my pleasure?
analytical/how-to-read-imaginative-liter.quote: the nearer you will come to knowing the artistic virtues in the literary work itself.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: What is it about?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Answer the first question by describing the unity of the plot of the story, play or poem.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Can I describe the unity of the plot, including the movement of a lyric?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: The first question is answered when you are able to describe the unity of the plot of a story, play, or poem

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: What is being said?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Answer the second question by discerning the role of the characters and recounting the key incidents in your own words.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Can I recount the key incidents and each main character's role in my own words?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: The second question is answered when you are able to discern the role that the various characters play

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Is it poetically true?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Answer the third question with a reasoned judgment of poetical truth: likely story, satisfying heart and mind, beautiful.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: “Is it a likely story? Does the work satisfy your heart and your mind? Do you appreciate the beauty of the work?”
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Is it a likely story? Does the work satisfy your heart and your mind? Do you appreciate the beauty of the work?

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Can you say why?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: For each of these judgments, give your reasons.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: “In each case, can you say why?”
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: In each case, can you say why?

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: No action required
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Treat the fourth question, What of it?, as largely irrelevant: once you answer the first three, your duty as reader is done.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I answered the first three questions well, without demanding a practical upshot?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Strictly speaking, no action whatever is called for on your part when you have read a novel, play, or poem well

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Trace the impulse to act
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: If a story or poem moves you to act, ask whether an implied statement in it produced the feeling.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Is my urge to act a response to a buried statement rather than the work itself?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: ask yourself whether the work contains some implied statement that has produced this feeling.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Experience the work
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: To read a story or poem well, simply experience it as an end in itself.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I experience the work for its own sake?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: To read it well, all you have to do is experience it.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read quickly, fully immersed
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read a story quickly and with total immersion.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I read it fast enough to keep the plot whole, and intensely enough to catch details?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Read it quickly and with total immersion.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Aim for one sitting
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read a story at one sitting, or compress the reading into as short a time as feasible, so you do not lose the plot's unity.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I spread the reading out so long that I forgot what happened?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Ideally, a story should be read at one sitting

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Don't draw it out
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not draw out the reading of a novel you love; you may be indulging unconscious feelings rather than reading.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I prolonging the book to satisfy feelings about the characters?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: they are probably not so much reading the book as satisfying their more or less unconscious feelings about the events and the characters.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Let the characters in
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Let the characters into your mind and heart, and suspend your disbelief about the events.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I let the characters in and set aside my disbelief?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Let the characters into your mind and heart; suspend your disbelief, if such it is, about the events.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Understand before disapproving
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not disapprove of what a character does before you understand why he does it.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Do I understand why the character acted, before condemning it?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Do not disapprove of something a character does before you understand why he does it—if then.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Live in his world
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Try as hard as you can to live in the character's world, not yours, and do not judge that world until you have lived in it.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I judging the story's world by my world's standards too soon?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Try as hard as you can to live in his world, not in yours

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Speed for unity, intensity for detail
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read quickly to see the unity of the story and intensely to see its details.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I see both the story's unity and its details?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Unless you read it quickly you will fail to see the unity of the story. Unless you read intensely you will fail to see the details.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Don't fear many characters
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not give up on a big novel because of many characters; expect the important ones to emerge as at a party.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I trying to remember every background character instead of letting the main ones emerge?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: We should not expect to remember every character
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.mistake: Abandoning a big novel because of its many names.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Tolerate early confusion
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not be anxious if all is not clear at the start; understand the relation of events looking back after you finish.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I demanding full clarity before the story has unfolded?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: you should not be anxious if all is not clear from the beginning.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Finish the story
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Finish a story before you claim to have read it well.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I read to the end before judging?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: you must finish a story in order to be able to say that you have read it well.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Don't extend beyond the book
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not speculate about what happens to characters before the first page or after the last.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I spending effort imagining events outside the book?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Actually, all such speculations are meaningless.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Personal vs. universal needs
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: In criticizing fiction, distinguish books that satisfy your own particular unconscious needs from those that satisfy the deep needs of almost everybody.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Do I like this book for private reasons I can't explain, or for what it gives everyone?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: we must be careful to distinguish those books that satisfy our own particular unconscious needs
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.mistake: Overrating a book because sympathetic characters get what we secretly want.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Poetic justice
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Notice whether the story convinces you that its characters are rewarded or punished according to their true merit.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Does the story convince me that justice has been done?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: He is able to convince us that justice—poetic justice, we call it—has been done.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Epics demand great effort
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Expect the major epics to demand great attention, involvement and imagination, and give them that effort.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I giving the epic the attention and imagination it demands?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Any of these major epics exerts enormous demands on the reader—demands of attention, of involvement, and of imagination.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read epics analytically
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read the epics well, analytically; their rewards come only to readers who do a good job.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I reading the epic analytically, or skimming it?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: these rewards are not gained by readers who do less than a good job on these books.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read the five great epics
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Try to read the Iliad, the Odyssey, the Aeneid, the Divine Comedy and Paradise Lost all the way through.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I read all five great epics through?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: We hope that you will take a stab at reading these five great epic poems

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read it like a story
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read a play as a story, being more active in creating the background since plays lack description.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I imagined the world the characters live in, which the play does not describe?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: A play is fiction, a story, and insofar as that is true, it should be read like a story.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: A read play is incomplete
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Remember that a play on the page is not the complete work; you must supply the physical dimension of performance.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I reading only the words, without imagining them performed?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: When you read a play, you are not reading a complete work.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Imagine it acted
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Supply the missing dimension by pretending to see the play acted.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I pictured the play on a stage?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: The only way to do that is to make a pretense of seeing it acted.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Direct the play
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: After answering the usual questions, try directing the play in your mind: tell actors how to say lines and play scenes.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Could I tell actors how to say this line and why that action is the climax?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: then try directing the play.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Coach imagined actors
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Imagine actors before you and explain how to say each line, how to play each scene, and the importance of key words.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Can I explain how each key line should be delivered?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Tell them how to say this line, how to play that scene.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Decide what's unstated
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Where the playwright leaves no stage directions, decide for yourself what happens, since the decision shapes your understanding.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I decided the open staging questions, such as what a character overheard?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Your own decision will be central to your understanding of the play.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Unstaged means partial
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Treat a play you have not mentally staged as only partially read.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I pretended to put this play on the stage?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Probably you have not read a play really well until you have pretended to put it on the stage in this way.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read Shaw's prefaces
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: When reading Shaw, read the preface he wrote for the play.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I read the playwright's preface where one exists?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: To read a Shavian play without reading the preface Shaw wrote for it is to turn one’s back intentionally on an important aid to understanding.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read plays at one sitting
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read a play through, as nearly as possible at one sitting, to get a feel for the whole.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I read the play through quickly enough to feel its whole?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: the importance of reading the plays through, as nearly as possible at one sitting

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read puzzling verse aloud
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read an opaque passage of verse drama out loud, slowly and with expression, as if an audience were listening.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I try speaking the passage aloud with expression?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Read slowly, as if an audience were listening, and with “expression”

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Glossary only after
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Turn to the glossary or notes only after reading a puzzling passage aloud has failed.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I try reading aloud before consulting the notes?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Only after it has failed should you turn to the glossary or notes.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.mistake: Running to the notes before trying to read the passage aloud.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Greek tragedy is hardest
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Expect Greek tragedy to be hard: lost companion plays, unknown staging, and stories the audience knew but we do not.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I aware of what the original audience knew that I do not?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Greek tragedy is probably the toughest nut to crack for beginning readers.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Tragedy is lack of time
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Remember that the essence of tragedy is time, or rather the lack of it.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Where does the lack of time force a hasty, wrong decision?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: remember that the essence of tragedy is time, or rather the lack of it.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Would you see in time?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: In reading any Greek tragedy, ask whether you would have seen in time what should have been done.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: “Would we have been able to see in time?”
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: It is easy for us to see what should have been done, but would we have been able to see in time?

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Chorus at your stature
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Imagine the chorus's words spoken by people of your own stature, and the protagonists' words by giants, larger than life.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Do I picture the chorus as ordinary people and the protagonists as giants?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: you should always imagine, when you read the words of the chorus, that the words are spoken by persons of your own stature

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: What counts as poetry
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Take lyric poetry as words arranged in an orderly, disciplined way, avoiding definitions that are too broad or too narrow.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I using an over-broad or over-narrow notion of what a poem is?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: poetry, for us, consists of words, and what is more, of words that are arranged in a more or less orderly and disciplined way.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: It's less work than feared
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not assume lyric poetry, even modern poetry, is too difficult; read it the right way and it demands less work.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I giving up because I assume poems are too obscure?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: lyric poetry, even modern poetry, does not always demand as much work as you may think if you go about reading it in the right way.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read through without stopping
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read a lyric through without stopping, whether you think you understand it or not.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I read the whole poem through before puzzling over lines?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: The first rule to follow in reading a lyric is to read it through without stopping, whether you think you understand it or not.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.mistake: Stalling on the first line or stanza and giving up.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Don't expect instant understanding
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not expect to understand the first line or stanza immediately and entirely; the essence lies only in the whole.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I demanding full understanding of the opening before reading on?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: the essence of a poem is almost never to be found in its first line, or even in its first stanza.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Reread it aloud
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read the poem through again, out loud.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did I read the poem aloud at least once?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Read the poem through again—but read it out loud.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Let speech test meaning
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Use speaking aloud to catch misunderstood phrases and misplaced emphasis, letting rhythm and rhyme guide where emphasis belongs.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Did speaking it reveal phrases I had glided over?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: You cannot glide over a misunderstood phrase or line quite so easily if you are speaking it.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Then question the poem
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Once you have grasped the poem's unity, even vaguely, begin asking it questions.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Do I have a sense of the whole before questioning details?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: once you have apprehended a poem in its unity, even if this apprehension is vague, you can begin to ask it questions.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Discover the key words
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Discover the poem's key words by rhetorical rather than grammatical discernment.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Which words stand out, and what makes them stand out?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: You do not come to terms with a poem; but you must discover the key words.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Why do words pop out?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Ask why certain words leap out of the poem.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: “Why do certain words pop out of the poem and stare you in the face?”
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Why do certain words pop out of the poem and stare you in the face?

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Rhythm, rhyme, repetition?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Ask whether rhythm, rhyme or repetition marks the key words.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: “Is it because the rhythm marks them? Or the rhyme? Or are the words repeated?”
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Is it because the rhythm marks them? Or the rhyme? Or are the words repeated?

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Do stanzas form a sequence?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Ask whether several stanzas share ideas and whether those ideas form a sequence.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: “Do several stanzas seem to be about the same ideas; if so, do these ideas form any kind of sequence?”
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: Do several stanzas seem to be about the same ideas; if so, do these ideas form any kind of sequence?

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Find the conflict
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Look for the conflict in the lyric, between people, images or ideas, whether named or only implied.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: What two things are in conflict in this poem?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: In most good lyrics there is some kind of conflict.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Look for implied conflict
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Seek the implied conflict, such as love and time or life and death, even when those words never appear.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Is there an unstated conflict such as love versus time?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: But often the conflict is only implied and not stated.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read the title too
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Use the title along with the poem itself to find its subject or conflict.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Does the title point to a theme the poem never names?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: the combination of the poem itself and its title invokes the same conflict

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Don't lean on context
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Do not assume you need extensive knowledge of the poet's life and times; read the poem itself, over and over.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Am I reading commentaries instead of reading the poem?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: readers of such works feel that they must know more about the authors and their times than they really have to.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.mistake: Putting faith in commentaries and biographies out of doubt about your own reading.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Read it repeatedly
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Read a great lyric over and over, returning to it many times.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: Have I returned to this poem more than once?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: To be understood it must be read—over and over.

analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.title: Keep working at it
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.action: Keep working at, rereading and thinking about a good poem; it will keep yielding new things.
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.check: What new thing did I find on this return visit?
analytical/suggestions-for-reading-stori.quote: A good poem can be worked at, re-read, and thought about over and over for the rest of your life.

analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.title: History as narrative
analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.action: Take history to mean a narrative account, presented more or less formally, of a past period, event or series of events.
analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.check: Is this a narrative account of the past?
analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.quote: we want to restrict ourselves to essentially narrative accounts, presented in a more or less formal manner, of a period or event or series of events in the past.

analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.title: Essence is narration
analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.action: Read history as a story; even a collection of documents implicitly tells one.
analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.check: What story does this history tell, explicitly or implicitly?
analytical/how-to-read-history/what-hist.quote: the essence of history is narration

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.title: Historical facts are elusive
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.action: Remember that historical facts are among the most elusive things in the world; do not take them as solid.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.check: How sure can anyone really be about this fact?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.quote: A historical fact, though we may have a feeling of trust and solidity about the word, is one of the most elusive things in the world.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.title: Witnesses aren't cross-examined
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.action: Bear in mind that historical witnesses are usually dead, uncross-examined, and may guess or not know what they are talking about.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.check: What kind of witness is this source, and how would I know if they erred?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.quote: And there is no guarantee whatever that they know what they are talking about.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.title: Keep some doubt
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.action: Like a juror, accept that you will not be absolutely sure what happened, and allow for doubt.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.check: Am I more certain about this event than the evidence allows?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.quote: The law assumes that you will not be absolutely sure.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.title: Why, and does it matter?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.action: Beyond the date of an event, ask why it happened and whether it is significant.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.check: “But why was Sumter fired on?” Why did this happen, and why do we care?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.quote: But why was Sumter fired on? That is an obvious next question.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-elusi.mistake: Thinking you know much because you know exact dates.

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: Closer to fiction
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Classify history as lying between fiction and science, but closer to fiction.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: Am I reading this history with the expectations of a story as well as of a report?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: it is usually admitted that history is closer to fiction than to science.

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: Historian supplies something
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Remember that every historian must make up something: a pattern in events or the motives behind actions.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: What has the historian supplied that the record itself does not give?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: the historian must always make up something.

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: Pattern vs. assigned causes
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Distinguish historians who impose or find a general pattern from those who report events but assign causes and motives.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: Does this historian fit events to a theory, or assign causes event by event?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: He must either find a general pattern in, or impose one on, events; or he must suppose that he knows why the persons in his story did the things

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: Recognize his method
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Recognize which way the historian you are reading is operating.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: Which way is this historian working: pattern, motives, or no pattern at all?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: It is essential to recognize which way the historian you are reading is operating.

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: The no-pattern theory
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Recognize the third position, held by Tolstoy and many moderns, that causes are unknowable and history has no pattern.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: Does this author hold that why things happen cannot be known?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: that there is no pattern to history at all.

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: Read more than one account
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Because theories differ and shape accounts, read more than one account of an event or period you want to understand.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: Have I read more than one historian on this event?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: it is necessary to read more than one account of the history of an event or period if we want to understand it.

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: Especially when it matters
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Take special care to read several accounts when the event has practical significance for you.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: Does this event affect my life, and have I read more than one side?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: And it is all the more important if the event in which we are interested has practical significance for us.

analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.title: Seek several viewpoints
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.action: Accept that every history has a point of view, and look at the event from more than one viewpoint to get at the truth.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.check: From whose point of view is this written, and have I seen another?
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.quote: But to get at the truth, we ought to look at it from more than one viewpoint.
analytical/how-to-read-history/theories-.mistake: Seeing an event through the eyes of only one man, side or faction.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: Between pro and amateur
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: Read history as a lay reader, between the professional who checks every source and the amateur reading only for amusement.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: Am I reading responsibly, without needing to cross-examine every source?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: We, as lay readers of history, stand somewhere between the professional historian, on the one hand, and the irresponsible amateur

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: One account limits truth
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: When you can read only one history of an event, admit you have little chance of learning what really happened.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: Am I claiming to know what happened from a single account?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: When we are not, we must admit that we do not have much chance of learning the truth of the matter in question

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: Read influential histories
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: Read influential histories like Thucydides because they shaped what happened afterward and help you understand the present.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: How has this history influenced later events and leaders?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: we read Thucydides not because he described perfectly what happened before he wrote his book, but because he to a certain extent determined what happened after.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: Good history is universal
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: Look for what is universal in a good history, the human mistakes and actions meaningful beyond its time and place.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: What does this history show that applies beyond its own time and place?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: But any good history is also universal.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: Not only what happened
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: Do not go to history only to discover what really happened, or you will miss the main thing a good historian teaches.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: Am I reading only for the facts and missing the lessons about human conduct?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: If your view of history is limited, if you go to it to discover only what really happened, you will not learn the main thing

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: Read toward the present
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: Read history as the story of what led up to now, to learn about the present and the future.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: What does this history tell me about the present and future?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: History is the story of what led up to now.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: Read several histories
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: If you can, read more than one history of an event or period that interests you.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: Have I read more than one history of this event or period?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: The first is: if you can, read more than one history of an event or period that interests you.

analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.title: Learn how men act
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.action: Read a history not only to learn what happened then and there, but to learn how people act in all times and places, especially now.
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.check: What have I learned about how people act, especially today?
analytical/how-to-read-history/the-unive.quote: but also to learn the way men act in all times and places, especially now.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: Read history as expository
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Read histories as expository works, asking the same questions as of any expository book, adapted to history.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Have I asked the four questions of this history?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: they can be read as expository works, and therefore they should be.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: What is it about, and not?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Find the history's particular subject and the limits the author sets: what it is about and what it is not about.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Can I say exactly what this history covers and what it leaves out?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: it is necessary to know precisely what it is about and what it is not about.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.mistake: Failing to note the limitations the author sets himself.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: Don't blame what wasn't tried
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Do not criticize a historian for not doing what he did not try to do.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Is my objection about something outside the author's stated scope?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: An author cannot be blamed for not doing what he did not try to do.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: How is the story told?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Find how the historian has chosen to tell his story, since there is more than one way to tell it.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: How has the historian organized and told the story?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: there is more than one way to tell a story, and we must know how the historian has chosen to tell his.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: How is it divided?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Ask whether chapters follow years, decades or generations, or rubrics such as economics, wars, religion and literature.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: “Does he divide his work into chapters that correspond to years or decades or generations?”
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: Does he divide his work into chapters that correspond to years or decades or generations?

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: What's most fundamental?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Determine which aspect of the story the historian considers most fundamental.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Which aspect of the story seems most basic to this historian?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: if we can say which aspect of the story he is telling seems to him most fundamental, we can understand him better.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: Judge verisimilitude
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Only after understanding, judge whether the history lacks verisimilitude, whether people really act as it says.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Do people really act the way this history says they did?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: We can judge—but only, as always, after we understand what is being said—that a historian’s work lacks verisimilitude.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: Judge use of sources
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Judge, especially with special knowledge, whether the historian has misused his sources or is misinformed about the facts.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Has the historian misread, ignored or misused relevant sources?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: we may think, especially if we have some special knowledge of the subject, that the historian has misused his sources.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: Verisimilitude weighs more
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Give more weight to the criticism of verisimilitude than to criticism of the use of sources.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Have I judged the history's grasp of human nature, not just its sources?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: The first criticism is, however, more important.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: Storyteller and scientist
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Expect a good historian to know what is likely to have happened as well as what witnesses said happened.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: Does the historian combine a storyteller's sense of the likely with a scientist's care for evidence?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: A good historian must combine the talents of the storyteller and the scientist.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: What of it? Political action
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Answer What of it? for history in terms of practical, political action.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: What does this history suggest can be done again, or avoided?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: The main answer to the question, What of it?, therefore, lies in the direction of practical, political action.

analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.title: History shows the possible
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.action: Use history to see what is possible: what has been done may be done again, or avoided.
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.check: What does this history show was possible?
analytical/how-to-read-history/questions.quote: History suggests the possible, for it describes things that have already been done.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Story of a real person
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Treat a biography as a narrative of a real person's life with a mixed character, posing many of the same problems as history.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Am I reading this both as a story and as history?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: A biography is a story about a real person.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Purpose and criteria of truth
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Ask what the biographer's purpose is and what his criteria of truth are, besides the questions asked of any book.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: “What is the author’s purpose? What are his criteria of truth?”
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: what is the author’s purpose? What are his criteria of truth?

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Definitive: read as history
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Read a definitive biography as history, a slice of the history of a person and his times.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Is this a definitive biography, and am I reading it as history?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: A definitive biography is a slice of history—the history of a man and of his times, as seen through his eyes.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Authorized may be biased
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Read an authorized biography as possibly biased, showing how heirs and friends want the person known.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Who commissioned this biography, and what image do they want me to hold?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: the reader should understand that it may be biased
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.mistake: Trusting an authorized biography as you would a definitive one.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Learn the era from it
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Use an authorized biography to learn about the time it was written in, its customs and acceptable attitudes.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: What does this book show about what was acceptable when it was written?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: The reading of an authorized biography will thus often tell us much about the time in which it was written

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Don't expect private truth
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Do not expect an authorized biography to reveal what the person's private life really was.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Am I mistaking the sanctioned picture for the real life?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: we should not expect to know what the private life really was.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Gather and judge sources
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: To get at the truth of a life, read all sources, consult those who were there, and use your own mind on the muddle.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Have I compared sources and used my own judgment?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: To get at the truth we must read all the communiqués, ask people who were there, and use our own minds to make sense out of the muddle.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Expect accuracy, real life
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: From an ordinary biography, expect accuracy and the feeling of viewing a real person's life in another time and place.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Is the author accurate, and do I feel I see a real life?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: In such works, we expect the author to be accurate, to know his facts.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Didactic biography
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Read a didactic biography, like Plutarch's Lives, more for its view of life than for its biographical information.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Is this biography meant to teach moral lessons, and am I reading it for them?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: we do not read it so much for its biographical information as for its view of life in general.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: No wholly true autobiography
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Doubt that any autobiography is wholly true; knowing one's own life is harder than knowing another's, and it is incomplete.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: What might the author not know or not admit about himself?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: it is questionable whether anyone has ever written a true autobiography.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Temptation to distort
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Watch for an autobiographer telling less, or more, than the truth when no one can contradict him.
