analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Where might the author be concealing, or embellishing?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: The temptation to tell either less or more than the truth (the latter may be more common), when there is no one to contradict you, is almost irresistible.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Concealment reveals
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Read an autobiography for what it reveals of its author, including what he wants to conceal.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: What does this book reveal about its author, even unintentionally?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: every autobiography tells us something about its author, if only that there are things that he wants to conceal.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Author's character secondary
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Read any book partly to discover its author's character, but never make that the primary consideration.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Am I psychoanalyzing the author instead of reading what he says?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: This should never be the primary consideration, and it leads, when it is overdone, to the so-called pathetic fallacy.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: What he says plainly
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Do not spend so long hunting a writer's secrets that you miss what he says plainly.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Have I grasped what the author plainly says?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: we should not spend so much time trying to discover a writer’s secrets that we do not find out what he says plainly.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Read many biographies
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: To know the truth of a person's life, read as many biographies as you can find, including his own account.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Have I read several lives of this person, including any autobiography?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: you should read as many biographies of him as you can find, including his own account of his life, if he wrote one.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Biography as history and cause
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Read biography as history and as the cause of history.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: How did this life shape, and get shaped by, history?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Read biography as history and as the cause of history

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Autobiography with salt
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Take all autobiographies with a grain of salt.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Have I discounted the author's self-portrait appropriately?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: take all autobiographies with a grain of salt

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Understand before arguing
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Never argue with a biography until you fully understand what it is saying.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Can I state what the book says before disputing it?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: never forget that you must not argue with a book until you fully understand what it is saying.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: What of it? Moral action
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Answer What of it? for biography by considering how the life can inspire practical, moral action in your own.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: What does this life suggest for how I lead mine?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: biography, like history, can be a cause of practical, moral action.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Always ask four questions
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Even when full analytical reading is unnecessary, ask the four questions of newspapers, magazines and current-events books.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Did I ask the four questions of this article or report?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: although the rules of reading do not all always have to be applied, the four questions must always be asked of anything you read.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Try to understand now
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Accept your obligation as a person and citizen to try to understand the world around you.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Am I making an effort to understand current events, not just consume them?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: But we do have an obligation, as human beings and as citizens, to try to understand the world around us.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Reporters are filters
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Remember that a reporter's mind is not a clear glass but a filter that can be mistaken.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: What might this reporter's mind have filtered out or got wrong?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: But the human mind is not a clear glass.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Know who is writing
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Find out who is writing a report of current happenings, especially what kind of mind he has.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: What kind of filter is this reporter's mind?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Thus the most important thing to know, when reading any report of current happenings, is who is writing the report.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: What does he want to prove?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Ask what the author wants to prove, checking the blurb or preface for his thesis.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: “What does the author want to prove?”
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: What does the author want to prove?

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Check blurb and preface
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Assume a current-events book wants to prove something, and look in the blurb or preface for its main thesis.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Have I found the book's thesis in the blurb or preface?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: The blurb often states the main contention or thesis of such books.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Whom does he want to convince?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Ask whom the author wants to convince: insiders, a small group able to act, or everyone, and whether you are among them.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: “Whom does he want to convince?” Am I in that audience?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Whom does he want to convince?

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Skip if not for you
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: If you are not in the intended audience, consider not reading the book.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Is this book meant for readers like me?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: If you do not belong to the audience for which the book is intended, you may not want to read it.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: What does he assume?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Ask what special knowledge, opinion or prejudice the author assumes you share.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: “What special knowledge does he assume?”
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: What special knowledge does he assume?

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Written for those who agree
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Expect that many authors write only for readers who already agree with their assumptions.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Do I share the author's assumptions, and is that why I agree or bristle?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Many authors write only for readers who agree with them.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: See your own filter
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Try to see through the filter of your own mind and assumptions, as well as the reporter's.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Which of my own assumptions are doctrines I feel as facts?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Thus we must try to see through the filter not only of the author-reporter’s mind, but also of our own.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: What special language?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Ask what special language the author uses, noticing words that provoke charged responses.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: “What special language does he use?”
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: What special language does he use?

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Control charged reactions
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Control your responses to emotionally loaded words, or at least know when they occur.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Which words here trigger a reaction in me?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: We should try to control these responses, or at least know when they occur.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Does he really know?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Ask whether the author really knows what he is talking about and is privy to the facts and decisions he describes.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: “Does he really know what he is talking about?”
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Does he really know what he is talking about?

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Enough for a fair account?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Ask whether the reporter knows all he should to give a fair and balanced account.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: “Does he know all that he should know in order to give a fair and balanced account of the situation?”
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Does he know all that he should know in order to give a fair and balanced account of the situation?

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Reporters may be uninformed
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Consider not only the reporter's bias but that he may be uninformed about secret actions, possibly without knowing it.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Could the reporter be missing information he is unaware of?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: a reporter may still be “uninformed” with regard to secret actions, treaties, and so forth.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Same questions, restated
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Treat the five questions as variations on the questions of any expository book, e.g. knowing special language is coming to terms.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Can I map each of the five questions to the usual reading questions?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: Knowing an author’s special language, for example, is nothing more than coming to terms with him.

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Let the reader beware
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Read any contemporary material warily: Caveat lector, let the reader beware.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Have I read this with appropriate wariness?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: The warning is this: Caveat lector— “Let the reader beware.”

analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.title: Know the author's interest
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.action: Find out whether the author or his sources have an interest in your understanding things a certain way, and take it into account.
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.check: Who benefits if I understand this a certain way?
analytical/how-to-read-history/how-to-re.quote: You should know that interest, and take it into account in whatever you read.

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: Information about understanding
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: Recognize that sometimes you must read for information about understanding, to find how others have interpreted the facts.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: Am I reading for facts, or for how others interpreted them?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: sometimes we have to read for information about understanding—to find out how others have interpreted the facts.

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: The best can't be condensed
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: Do not settle for a digest of the very best writing; it cannot be condensed without loss.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: Is this piece good enough that I should read the original?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: the very best articles, like the best books, cannot be condensed without loss.

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: Let summaries lead you on
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: Use a summary of a great work only as an impulse to read the original.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: Has this summary led me to the original?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: A summary, in this case, would function well only if it impelled us to read the original.

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: Digests suit average articles
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: Accept a condensation for an average, mainly informational article.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: Is this article mainly informational, so a digest suffices?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: For the average article, however, a condensation is usually adequate

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: What was left out?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: The more condensed a digest, the more you should ask what has been left out.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: How much selection has occurred, and what may have been omitted?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: then the question of what has been left out becomes critical.

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: Know the condensor
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: The greater the condensation, the more you should learn the character of whoever condensed it.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: Who made this digest, and what are their leanings?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: the greater the condensation, the more important it is that we know something of the character of the condensor

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: Read between the lines
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: Infer what was left out from the condensation itself, since you cannot consult the original.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: What does the digest imply that it does not say?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: you must somehow infer this from the condensation itself.

analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.title: Digests are demanding
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.action: Treat digest reading as possibly the most demanding reading, requiring reading for understanding as well as information.
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.check: Am I reading this digest as carefully as its editors read the originals?
analytical/how-to-read-history/a-note-on.quote: Reading digests, therefore, is sometimes the most demanding and difficult reading that you can do.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Turn to good popularizations
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Since you cannot become expert in every field, rely on scientific popularizations for current science.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I using popular works to reach fields written only for experts?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: He must fall back, therefore, on scientific popularizations.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Tell good from bad
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Learn to tell good popularizations from bad ones, and read the good ones with understanding.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I say why this popularization is good, and have I understood it?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: it is also important to be able to read the good ones with understanding.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read scientific classics
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Try to read at least some of the great scientific classics; none is impossibly difficult if you make the effort.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I attempted a scientific classic rather than assuming it is beyond me?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: None of them is impossibly difficult
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.mistake: Assuming the great scientific books are too hard for a lay reader.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: State the author's problem
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: State as clearly as you can the problem the scientific author tried to solve.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I state, in one or two sentences, the problem this scientist was trying to solve?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: it is particularly relevant to works in the fields of science and mathematics.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read for history and philosophy
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read classical scientific books to understand the history and philosophy of science, not to master the subject in a contemporary sense.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I reading to understand the scientific enterprise rather than to pass an exam in the subject?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: you read them to understand the history and philosophy of science.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.mistake: Treating an old classic as a current textbook.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Know the problem's background
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Become aware of the problems the great scientists tried to solve and of the background of those problems.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Do I know what was known, and puzzling, when the author wrote?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: aware of the problems, and aware, also, of the background of the problems.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Trace facts, principles, proofs
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Follow the strands of scientific development, tracing how facts, assumptions, principles and proofs are interrelated.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I show how the author's facts, assumptions, principles and proofs connect?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: to trace the ways in which facts, assumptions, principles, and proofs are interrelated

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read to free the mind
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Treat the historical study of science as an exercise that frees the mind through the discipline of wonder.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Has this reading made science seem less unintelligible and stirred my wonder?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: the freeing of the mind through the discipline of wonder.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: What a scientific book is
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Classify a book as scientific if it reports findings or conclusions of experimental or observational research.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Does the book report findings from laboratory work or observation of nature?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: By a scientific book, we mean the report of findings or conclusions in some field of research

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Describe and interconnect phenomena
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Expect the scientific problem to be describing phenomena accurately and tracing interconnections between kinds of phenomena.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Which phenomena is the author describing, and which interconnections is he tracing?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: The scientific problem is always to describe the phenomena as accurately as possible

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Separate assumed from proved
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Detect the author's initial bias by distinguishing what he assumes from what he establishes through argument.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I list what the author takes for granted separately from what he proves?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: by distinguishing what the author assumes from what he establishes through argument.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Objectivity is confessed bias
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Judge a scientist's objectivity by how frankly he asks you to take things for granted, not by an absence of presuppositions.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Has the author openly told me what he is asking me to assume?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Scientific objectivity is not the absence of initial bias. It is attained by frank confession of it.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Spot technical terms
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Find the leading terms through the uncommon or technical words, and use them to grasp the propositions.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I identified the technical words that carry the author's key terms?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: The leading terms in a scientific work are usually expressed by uncommon or technical words.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Expect general propositions
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Look for main propositions that are general, saying how things generally are or behave, not tied to time and place.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Is each main proposition I found a general statement rather than a particular one?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: The main propositions are always general ones.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Recognize inductive argument
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Distinguish inductive arguments, which establish a general proposition from observable evidence, from deductive ones proved by other propositions.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Is this argument resting on observed cases or on previously established propositions?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Science is primarily inductive

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Follow the reported evidence
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: To understand inductive arguments, follow the evidence the scientist reports as their basis.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Do I understand the experiment or observations on which this conclusion rests?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: you must be able to follow the evidence that the scientist reports as their basis.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.mistake: Accepting conclusions without grasping the experimental basis.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Get first-hand experience
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: If the book alone cannot make the evidence clear, witness demonstrations, handle apparatus, or see specimens and models in a museum.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: When the text failed me, did I seek the special experience it describes?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: the reader has only one recourse, which is to get the necessary special experience for himself at first hand.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Know the crucial experiments
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Become acquainted through direct experience with the crucial experiments in the history of science, not only the texts.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I seen or done any of the classical experiments behind this book?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: There are classical experiments as well as classical books.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read key parts first
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Make a start without reading the whole classic in detail; read illuminating parts such as the preface on method.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I found the parts, like the preface, that give the book's main impression?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: you do not have to read the book through, and in detail, to receive these impressions of it.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Expect two main difficulties
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Expect two main difficulties in a scientific book: following the arguments and their evidence, and the mathematics.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Which difficulty am I stuck on: the evidence for an argument, or the mathematics?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: There are likely to be two main difficulties in reading a scientific book.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Do not fear mathematics
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Do not assume you cannot read mathematics at all; the fear is common but not justified.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I avoiding mathematics only because I expect to fail?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Many people are frightened of mathematics and think they cannot read it at all.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.mistake: Giving up on mathematical passages before trying.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Treat math as a language
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Approach mathematics as a written language you can learn like any other.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I learning the symbols as I would words of a new language?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: mathematics is a language, and that we can learn it like any other

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Learn its vocabulary and syntax
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Memorize mathematical symbols and their relations, learning its vocabulary, grammar and syntax at the elementary level.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Do I know what each symbol means and how symbols combine here?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: it has its own vocabulary, grammar, and syntax, and these have to be learned by the beginning reader.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Terms without emotional connotation
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read mathematical terms and equations as free of emotional connotation, which makes shared understanding possible.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I reading any emotional meaning into these terms that isn't there?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: There are no emotional connotations of mathematical terms, propositions, and equations when these are properly used.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Start with Euclid
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Begin with Euclid's Elements to see how lucid, beautiful and satisfying mathematics can be.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I worked through some of Euclid's opening propositions?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: You might start with Euclid, whose Elements of Geometry is one of the most lucid and beautiful works

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Construction versus theorem
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Tell construction problems, which require something to be done (Q.E.F.), from theorems, which require something to be proved (Q.E.D.).
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Is this proposition asking me to construct something or to prove something?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Construction problems require that some-thing be done, theorems require that something be proved.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Trace dependencies between propositions
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Ask why propositions come in their order and trace which earlier constructions each proof uses.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I name the earlier propositions this proof depends on?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: we see that these three constructions are needed for the sake of Proposition 5.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Postulate versus proved construction
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Note that postulates assume an operation is possible, while construction propositions prove it is possible.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Is this possibility assumed as a postulate or proved as a proposition?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: In the case of the postulates, the possibility is assumed; in the case of the propositions, it is proved.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read the if-then claim
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Understand a proved proposition as asserting only the if-then link between hypothesis and conclusion, not the truth of either alone.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I clear that what is proved is the connection, not the hypothesis itself?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: The proposition asserts this if-then relationship.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.mistake: Thinking a theorem asserts that its hypothesis or conclusion is simply true.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Check assumptions about reality
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Unlike in mathematics, examine assumptions about real things in syllogisms, since they may or may not be true.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Does this argument assume something about real things that I must verify?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: We have to examine our assumptions in a way that we do not have to do in mathematics.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Spend evenings with Euclid
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Spend several evenings with Euclid to overcome your fear of mathematics, then glance at Archimedes, Apollonius and Nicomachus.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I put in a few evenings on Euclid before deciding mathematics is beyond me?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: if you spent several evenings with the Elements you would overcome much of your fear of the subject.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Skip where needed
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: When reading other Greek mathematicians, skip what is too hard.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I letting difficult passages stop me instead of skipping ahead?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: They are not really very difficult, and besides, you can skip.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read math with pencil
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read a mathematical book for itself from beginning to end with a pencil, writing in margins and on scratch paper.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Am I working each step out on paper rather than only reading?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: with a pencil in your hand, for writing in the margins and even on a scratch pad is more necessary here

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Skip math in science
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: When the book is a scientific work containing mathematics rather than a mathematics book, skip mathematical detail freely.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Is my purpose the mathematics itself, or the scientific work that uses it?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: In this case, skipping is often the better part of valor.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Statement, then glance proof
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read each proposition's statement and glance down its proof to see how it is done, without working every proof first time.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Do I know what each proposition claims and roughly how it is proved?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Read the statement of the proposition, and glance down the proof to get an idea of how it is done

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read lemmas, corollaries, scholiums
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read the statements of lemmas and corollaries and the scholiums, which relate propositions to each other and to the whole.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I read the scholiums that explain how the parts fit the whole?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: read the statements of the so-called lemmas and corollaries; and read the so-called scholiums

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: See how the system is built
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Go through the whole work this way to see what comes first and second and how the parts fit together.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I outline the order of the system and how its parts connect?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: what comes first and what second, and how the parts fit together.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Find the main passages
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Avoid troublesome diagrams and glance at interstitial matter, but be sure to find and read the author's main points.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I located and read the passages where the author makes his main points?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: being sure to find and read the passages where Newton is making his main points.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Repeat the experiments yourself
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Where described experiments are simple, repeat some of them yourself.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I tried any of the book's experiments with my own hands?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: You can quite easily repeat some of these experiments yourself

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read the summing-up discussions
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read the theorem statements and the discussions at the end of each book where the author sums up discoveries and consequences.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I read the author's own summaries of discoveries and their consequences?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: where Newton sums up his discoveries and suggests their consequences.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Absence of math can hinder
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Expect works that avoid mathematics, such as scientific dialogues, to be harder to pin down; work to discover what is being said.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I state what this non-mathematical scientific dialogue actually claims?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: its absence from certain works may cause you even more trouble.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Understand the problem first
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Keep in mind that your primary obligation is to understand the problem, not to become competent in the subject.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Could I explain the problem this book addresses, even without mastering its content?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: your primary obligation is not to become competent in the subject matter but instead to understand the problem.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Popularizations skirt two problems
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Expect popularizations to report experimental results rather than describe experiments, and to contain little mathematics.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Is this popular work giving results without experiments or mathematics?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: they contain relatively few descriptions of experiments

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Beware filtering reporters
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Remember that in popular science articles you depend on reporters who filter the information for you.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: How far can I trust the reporter who filtered this science for me?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: In reading them, we are at the mercy of reporters who filter the information for us.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Read popular science actively
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Keep your mind awake: active reading matters more for popular science than almost anywhere else.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Was I actively questioning, or reading it like a story?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: the requirement that you read actively is more important here than almost anywhere else.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.mistake: Reading popular science passively, as if it were a story.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Identify the subject matter
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Identify the subject matter of the popular science work.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I name the subject this work is about?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Identify the subject matter.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Relate whole and parts
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Discover how the parts of the work relate to its whole.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I show how each part serves the whole?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Discover the relation between the whole and its parts.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Terms, propositions, arguments
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Come to terms with the author and plot his propositions and arguments.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Have I identified the key terms, propositions and arguments?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Come to terms and plot the propositions and arguments.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Understand before criticizing
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Work at achieving understanding before you criticize or assess the work's significance.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Can I say "I understand" before I judge?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Work at achieving understanding before you begin to criticize or to assess significance.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Short articles are informational
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read short popular articles mainly to follow the author's account; popular books demand more active thinking.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Is this short piece informational, or a book demanding deeper thought?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: Short articles are usually primarily informational, and as such they require less active thinking on your part.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Notice practical consequences
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Notice when a theoretical popular book has consequences for action, and consider what it implies you should do.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Does this theoretical book imply that I should act, or stop acting, in some way?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: has a significance that goes beyond the theoretical and into the realm of the practical.

analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.title: Stay informed on great achievements
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.action: Read theoretical works on the great scientific achievements of your age, knowing all you can about them.
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.check: Do I understand the major scientific developments that affect my world?
analytical/how-to-read-science-and-mathe.quote: An informed and concerned reader should know everything he can about the subject.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.title: Wonder as children wonder
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.action: Ask the profound why-questions children ask, looking at the world as they do.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.check: Am I asking why something is, not only whether it is so?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.quote: we must be able to see as children see, to wonder as they wonder, to ask as they ask.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.title: Simple questions, wise replies
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.action: Be childishly simple in your questions and maturely wise in your replies.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.check: Are my questions basic and my answers carefully reasoned?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.quote: we too must be childishly simple in our questions—and maturely wise in our replies.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.title: Ask why, not just whether
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.action: Avoid letting your curiosity shrink to matters of fact; ask why as well as whether.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.check: Have I asked only for information, or for reasons?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.quote: They want to know whether something is so, not why.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.mistake: Asking only for information, like most adults.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.title: Spot the child's question
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.action: Recognize that great philosophical books ask the same profound questions children ask, and look for them.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.check: What basic childlike question is this book really asking?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/philos.quote: they ask the same sort of profound questions that children ask.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Questions about existence
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: what is the difference between existing and not existing, and what is common to all things that exist?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book address what it means to exist and what all existing things share?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: What is the difference between existing and not existing?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Questions about modes of being
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: are there different modes of being; do some things exist only in the mind; does everything exist physically?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book ask about kinds of existence, mental versus extra-mental, material versus immaterial?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: Are there different ways in which things can exist—different modes of being or existence?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Questions about necessity, possibility
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: does anything change or is anything immutable; does anything exist necessarily; is the possible larger than the actual?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book ask about change versus immutability, necessity, and possible existence?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: Does anything exist necessarily, or must we say that everything that does exist might not have existed?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: What is involved in change
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: what is involved in any change, and does something endure unchanged through it?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book ask what persists and what alters in change?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: What is involved in any change?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Kinds of change
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: how many kinds of change are there, and do the same elements and causes enter into all of them?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book distinguish kinds of change such as coming to be, motion, growth and alteration?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: How many different kinds of change are there?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Causes of change and being
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: what is a cause of change, are there types of causes, and are causes of becoming the same as causes of being?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book ask about causes of change and relate becoming to being?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: Are the causes of change—of becoming—the same as the causes of being, or existence?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Other theoretical questions
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Recognize further theoretical questions: necessity and contingency, material and immaterial, freedom, powers of mind, extent of knowledge, free will.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Is the book's question among these speculative ones?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: about the nature and extent of human knowledge; about the freedom of the will.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Questions about good and evil
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: is there a universally valid distinction between good and evil, and are some things always good or bad?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book ask whether good and evil are universal or relative?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: Is there a universally valid distinction between good and evil?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Good/evil versus right/wrong
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Distinguish good and evil from right and wrong, and ask how to make the distinction precise.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Is the author using good/evil and right/wrong as distinct pairs?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: Good and evil, of course, are not the same as right and wrong

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Questions about ordering goods
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Ask: can the many goods be ordered; are some more important; do some depend on others; can goods conflict?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book ask how goods rank, depend on, or conflict with one another?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: Is it possible to order the goods?

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Other practical questions
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Recognize further normative questions: duties, virtues and vices, happiness, justice and rights, the state and individual, the good society, war and peace.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Is the book's question among these practical ones?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: about the state and its relation to the individual

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Speculative versus normative philosophy
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Classify a philosophical book as theoretical (what is or happens) or normative (what ought to be done or sought).
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Is the author asking what is, or what ought to be?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: and is more accurately called normative.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Normative versus how-to books
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Distinguish normative philosophy, which argues for goals all should seek and prescribes means universally, from how-to books that assume your goal.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Does the book argue that I ought to seek a goal, or assume I want it?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: they go no further than prescribing in the most universal terms the means that ought to be employed

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Metaphysics, nature, epistemology
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Classify a theoretical work as metaphysics (being), philosophy of nature (becoming), or epistemology (knowledge).
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Is the book's main concern being, change, or knowledge?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: then it is a work in epistemology, which is just another name for theory of knowledge.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.title: Ethics versus politics
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.action: Classify a normative work as ethics (the good life, individual conduct) or politics (the good society, individual and community).
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.check: Is the book about the individual's good life or about society?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/the-qu.quote: the sphere of politics or political philosophy.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.title: First- versus second-order questions
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.action: Distinguish first-order questions about the world and conduct from second-order questions about our knowledge, thought and language.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.check: Is this book asking about the world, or about how we think and speak of it?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.quote: there are also “second-order questions” that can be asked

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.title: Modern philosophy is specialist
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.action: Expect modern philosophy confined to second-order questions to be as hard for non-philosophers as science for non-scientists.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.check: Is this a specialist work on second-order questions written for experts?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.quote: This makes modern philosophy very hard to read for nonphilosophers

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.title: Read first-order books
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.action: Choose philosophical books that ask first-order questions and were written for lay readers.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.check: Does the book I chose ask first-order questions for ordinary readers?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.quote: These books ask the kinds of questions that we have called first-order ones.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.title: The classics are accessible
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.action: Read the great philosophical classics from Plato onward; they were written for the general reader.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.check: Have I tried a classic rather than assuming it is only for specialists?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.quote: These books are accessible to the lay reader; you can succeed in reading them if you wish to.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.title: Being critical does no harm
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.action: Value criticism, but do not give up first-order questions entirely.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.check: Am I critical without abandoning the big questions?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/modern.quote: it is never harmful to be critical.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Philosophy's method is thinking
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Recognize that philosophical questions are answered by reflection, not experiment, observation or documents.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Could this question be settled by research, or only by thinking?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: There is, in short, nothing to do but think.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Grounded in experience
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Test philosophical answers against experience; good philosophy is not thinking divorced from experience.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Does the author's reasoning connect with experience, or float free of it?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: Philosophy, when it is good, is not “pure” speculation—thinking divorced from experience.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Test by common experience
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Judge philosophical answers by common human experience, which you share with the philosopher.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Can I check this claim against my own everyday experience?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: such tests are based on common experience alone

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: You can think as well
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Remember you are as well placed as the great philosophers to reflect on change and being from experience.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Am I using my own experience to think about the question?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: you are in as good a position to think about its nature and causes as the greatest philosophers.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Follow their deeper thinking
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Attend to how great philosophers formulated penetrating questions and worked out answers by thinking more profoundly about common experience.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Can I trace how the author's question and answer were worked out?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: by thinking more profoundly about the experience than the rest of us have.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Spot non-philosophical questions
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Distinguish truly philosophical questions from those a philosopher raised that belong to later scientific investigation.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Could this question now be answered by scientific investigation?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: it is necessary to be able to distinguish the truly philosophical questions from the other questions
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.mistake: Treating a philosopher's outdated scientific claims as his philosophy.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Set aside outdated science
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Treat classical philosophers' scientific errors as largely irrelevant; judge their philosophical questions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Am I criticizing the philosophy, or merely the dated science?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: the misinformation or lack of information about scientific matters that mars the work of the classical philosophers is irrelevant.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Research cannot settle norms
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Do not accept surveys or experiments as answers to normative questions such as how one ought to live.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Is the author trying to answer an ought-question with data?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: He may decide to ask 1,000 persons what kind of life they would like to lead
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.mistake: A scientist answering a normative question by polling.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Identify the expository style
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Identify which of the five styles a philosopher uses and know its advantages and disadvantages.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Which style is this: dialogue, treatise, objections, geometrical system, or aphorism?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: The student or reader of philosophy should be able to distinguish between them and know the advantages and disadvantages of each.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Discover through the dialogue
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Read a Platonic dialogue heuristically, letting the questioning lead you to discover things for yourself.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: What did I discover for myself by following the conversation?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: this style is heuristic, that is, it allows the reader, indeed leads him, to discover things for himself.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Follow the treatise's order
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: In a treatise, follow its order: main problem first, thorough treatment of the subject, special problems along the way or at the end.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Can I identify the treatise's beginning, middle and end?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: They state the main problem first, go through the subject matter in a thorough and business-like way

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Philosophy versus science works
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Classify each work: purely philosophical, a mixture of philosophy and early science, or mainly scientific.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Is this particular work philosophy, early science, or a mixture?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: are mixtures of philosophical theory and early scientific investigation

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Follow the article structure
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: In Aquinas's style, follow the pattern: question, wrong answer with arguments, authoritative counter-text, "I answer that", replies to each argument.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Can I locate each part of the article and the author's own answer?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: A question is posed; the opposite (wrong) answer to it is given

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Weigh met objections
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Value a work that reports conflicting views and tries to meet all possible objections to its solutions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Has the author faced the strongest objections to his view?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: his attempt to meet all possible objections to his own solutions.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Geometrical style of philosophy
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Recognize the geometrical style, with propositions, proofs, corollaries and scholiums, modelled on mathematics.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Is this philosophy written in mathematical form?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: they attempted to organize philosophy itself in a way akin to the organization of mathematics.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Skip only in geometrical works
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Skip freely in geometrically arranged works like Spinoza, but not in Kant, Aristotle or Plato, where reasoning is continuous.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Is this work's line of reasoning continuous, so that skipping loses the thread?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: You cannot skip anything in Kant or Aristotle, because the line of reasoning is continuous
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.mistake: Skipping in a continuous treatise or a dialogue.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Form can defeat communication
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: Be alert that philosophy in mathematical form, or science in dialogue form, may fail to communicate its meaning.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Is the chosen form hiding what the author means?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: it seems likely that the form they chose was a major reason for the failure.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.title: Aphorisms leave arguments undone
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.action: In aphoristic works, notice where you are building connections and arguments the author never defended.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.check: Has the author defended this insight, or have I supplied the argument?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-phi.quote: The author is like a hit-and-run driver

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Find the questions
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Discover the question or questions the philosophical work tries to answer, whether stated or implicit.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Can I state the questions this book tries to answer?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: the most important thing to discover in reading any philosophical work is the question or questions it tries to answer.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Find controlling principles
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Look for the author's controlling principles, stated or unstated, that shape how he answers his questions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: What underlying principle governs the author's answers?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: How the author answers these questions will be deeply affected by his controlling principles.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Look in other works
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Look for controlling principles in the author's other works, since they may be treated elsewhere or assumed throughout.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Have I checked whether the author's other books state principles this one assumes?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: it is always important to recognize, in reading any Aristotelean work, that things said in other works are relevant to the discussion.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Expect many rereadings
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Treat finding controlling principles as the ideal goal of thorough reading, which may take years of rereading.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Have I reread enough to see what pervades the whole work?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: Sometimes it takes years to do this, and many readings and rereadings.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Avoid books about philosophers
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Do not take the shortcut of reading books about philosophers' lives and opinions; make the discovery yourself.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Did I find the principles myself, or borrow someone else's account?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: we do not recommend that you take the shortcut of reading books about the philosophers, their lives and opinions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.mistake: Relying on secondary accounts instead of the text.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Check consistency with principles
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Decide whether the author adheres to his controlling principles throughout his work.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Do the author's conclusions actually follow from his stated principles?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: you will want to decide whether he adheres to them throughout his work.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Resolve inconsistency
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: If the author is inconsistent, decide whether he means his principles or his conclusions, or whether neither is valid.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Which does the author really mean: the stated principles or the conclusions?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: you have to decide which of two sets of propositions he really means

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Explain versus describe
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Expect theoretical philosophy to explain the ultimate causes and conditions of things, not describe phenomena as science does.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Is the author explaining ultimate causes, or describing connections of phenomena?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: The philosophical problem is to explain, not to describe, as science does, the nature of things.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Focus on terms, initial propositions
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Put your major effort into the philosopher's terms and initial propositions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Have I pinned down the key terms and starting propositions?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: The major effort of the reader, therefore, must be with respect to the terms and the initial propositions.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Familiar words, special senses
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Watch for terms expressed in common words used in special senses, and resist reading them in their familiar meaning.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Am I reading this ordinary word in the author's special sense?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: If he does not overcome the tendency to use familiar words in a familiar way, he will probably make gibberish and nonsense of the book.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.mistake: Reading familiar words in their everyday sense.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Understand, don't imagine, ideas
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Grasp abstract terms by having the idea they express; do not try to imagine what ideas refer to.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Am I understanding the general idea, or trying to picture it?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: People who try to imagine what ideas refer to befuddle themselves

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Attend closely to principles
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Pay closest attention to the philosopher's principles, whether assumptions or claims of self-evidence.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Can I list the author's assumptions and his self-evident claims?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: you must pay closest attention to the philosopher’s principles.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Assume to see what follows
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Grant the author's assumptions to see what follows, even if you hold contrary presuppositions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Did I provisionally accept the assumptions to follow the argument?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: Make them to see what follows, even if you yourself have contrary presuppositions.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Know your own prejudgments
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Get clear about your own prejudgments so you do not misjudge the author's.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: What do I presuppose that might color my judgment of the author?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: the clearer you are about your own prejudgments, the more likely you will be not to misjudge those made by others.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Test self-evident claims yourself
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Test the author's self-evident principles against your own common sense and daily observation, not special research.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Does my own experience of the world bear out this supposedly self-evident claim?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: He refers you to your own common sense and daily observation of the world in which you live.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Read by thinking
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Read a philosophical book as it was written, by thinking, with no aid but your own mind.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Was I thinking with the author, rather than seeking outside aids?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: the method according to which you should read a philosophical book is very similar to the method according to which it is written.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.title: Rules fit philosophy best
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.action: Apply the rules of analytical reading most fully to philosophical books, where they fit most directly.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.check: Have I applied every analytical rule to this philosophical book?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/hints-.quote: apply more directly to the reading of philosophical books than to the reading of any other kind.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.title: Ignore the author's background
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.action: In good theoretical philosophy, do not concern yourself with the author's personality or social and economic background.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.check: Am I judging the argument, not the author's background?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.quote: You do not have to be concerned about the “personality” of the author

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.title: Read others on the problem
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.action: Read other great philosophers on the same problem before making up your mind about any of them.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.check: Have I read other philosophers who dealt with this problem?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.quote: You had better listen in on it before you make up your mind about what any of them says.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.title: Disagreement marks mysteries
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.action: Do not be troubled by persistent disagreement among philosophers; take it as a sign of a great unsolved problem.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.check: Does lasting disagreement here point to a deep unsolved problem?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.quote: It is good to know where the true mysteries are.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.title: Make up your own mind
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.action: Judge for yourself what is true and false; others' disagreements matter less than your own judgment.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.check: Have I reached my own judgment on the question?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.quote: Your responsibility is only to make up your own mind.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.title: Don't borrow answers
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.action: Answer philosophical questions for yourself; adopting others' opinions evades the questions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.check: Is my answer my own, or someone else's opinion?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.quote: Taking the opinions of others is not solving them, but evading them.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.mistake: Taking others' opinions in place of an answer.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.title: Ground answers in argument
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.action: Back your answers with solid arguments rather than expert testimony.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.check: What arguments, not authorities, support my answer?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/on-mak.quote: you cannot depend on the testimony of experts, as you may have to do in the case of science.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Natural versus dogmatic theology
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: Classify a theological book as natural theology, reached by unaided reason, or dogmatic theology, founded on articles of faith.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Are the first principles reached by reason, or held by faith?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: There are two kinds of theology, natural theology and dogmatic theology.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Natural theology is philosophy
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: Read natural theology as a branch of philosophy, the last chapter of metaphysics.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Is this argument reached by the natural working of the mind?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: Natural theology is a branch of philosophy

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Dogmatic theology rests on dogma
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: Recognize that a work of dogmatic theology depends on dogmas and the authority of a church that proclaims them.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Which dogmas and which church authority does this book depend on?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: A work of dogmatic theology always depends upon dogmas and the authority of a church that proclaims them.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Treat dogmas like axioms
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: If you are not of the faith, treat the book's dogmas with the respect you give a mathematician's assumptions.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Did I accept the dogmas as starting points while reading?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: by treating its dogmas with the same respect you treat the assumptions of a mathematician.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Faith is not assumption
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: Remember that for believers an article of faith is the most certain knowledge, not a tentative assumption.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Am I mistaking the believer's certainty for mere assumption?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: an article of faith is not something that the faithful assume.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Don't fight first principles
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: Accept, at least temporarily, the articles of faith that are the author's first principles, so you can attend to the book.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Am I still arguing with the premises instead of reading the book?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: The first mistake is to refuse to accept, even temporarily, the articles of faith that are the first principles of the author.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.mistake: Struggling with the first principles and never reading the book.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Reasoning is not dogma
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: Do not assume that arguments and conclusions built on dogmatic principles are themselves dogmatic; judge the reasoning.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Have I evaluated the reasoning separately from the principles?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: The second mistake is to assume that, because the first principles are dogmatic
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.mistake: Treating the arguments as dogmatic because the principles are.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Check the reasoning
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: Examine whether the reasoning from accepted principles is cogent; defective reasoning yields invalid conclusions even from acceptable principles.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Do the conclusions really follow from the accepted principles?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: if the reasoning is defective, the most acceptable first principles will lead to invalid conclusions.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.title: Accept, then read carefully
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.action: As a non-believing reader, accept the first principles as true while reading, then read with the care any expository work deserves.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.check: Did I grant the principles and then apply all the analytical rules?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/a-note.quote: His task is to accept the first principles as true while he is reading the book

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.title: Recognize a canonical book
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.action: Recognize a canonical book: one read as sacred or authoritative, such as scripture read as revelation, or Marx for orthodox Marxists.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.check: Am I or others reading this book as having authority beyond question?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.quote: We use the term “canonical” to refer to such books

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.title: Three marks of the institution
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.action: Identify the institution behind a canonical reading: it teaches, has a body of doctrine, and has a faithful, obedient membership.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.check: Is there a teaching institution with doctrine and obedient members behind this book?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.quote: (1) is a teaching institution, (2) has a body of doctrine to teach, and (3) has a faithful and obedient membership.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.title: Reverential reading forbids error
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.action: Notice that reading reverentially means not questioning the authorized reading or finding error in the text.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.check: Am I barred from finding error here, and do I know it?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.quote: The members of any such organization read reverentially.

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.title: One right reading
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.action: Recognize that canonical books have one and only one right, orthodox reading.
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.check: Is there an authorized interpretation I am expected to reach?
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.quote: These are books for which there is one and only one right reading

analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.title: Make sense and find true
analytical/how-to-read-philosophy/how-to.action: As a faithful reader, make sense of the canonical book and find it true in some sense of "true".
